| getNodeData(id?) / getEdgeData(id?) | Separate single/list calls: getNodeData / getNodes, getEdgeData / getEdges                                                                                      |
| addNodeData / removeNodeData        | addNode(s) / removeNode(s)                                                                                                                                      |
| setElementState / getElementState   | setElementStates / getItemStates                                                                                                                                |
| hideElement / showElement           | hideItem / showItem                                                                                                                                             |
| focusElement / resize               | focusItem / setSize                                                                                                                                             |
| draw / render                       | [render for initial rendering](/en/docs/api/graph#graph-lifecycle-render), [updateOptions for visual changes](/en/docs/api/graph#graph-lifecycle-updateoptions) |

Use the [method index](/en/docs/api/graph) for full arguments, returns, and missing-ID behavior. New code should avoid toData, isDestroyed, and internal getCanvas/updateData.

<span id="extension-transform-and-plugin-migration" style="{ display: 'block', scrollMarginTop: '8rem' }" />

## Extension, Transform and Plugin [#extension-transform-and-plugin]

G6 base classes do not migrate unchanged. Select the category and follow [tutorials](/en/docs/guides/extensions) and [contracts](/en/docs/api/graph#graph-extensions). The controlled context is not a full Graph. Hosts can explicitly inject plugin subscriptions, with cleanup in destroy.

## Unsupported capabilities and alternatives [#unsupported-capabilities-and-alternatives]

Run algorithms in a separate analysis pipeline and write results into data. Implement peripheral controls in application UI or Plugins. Keep G6 pages that cannot fit supported primitives, runtimes, or lifecycles; partial migration is not full compatibility.

## Migration acceptance checklist [#migration-acceptance-checklist]

1. Pin both versions and retain the original fallback.
2. Verify data, styles, labels, states, groups, and key gestures.
3. Cover updates, unsubscription, asynchronous unmounting, and repeated mounting.
4. Measure layout, rendering, interactions, and resources under equivalent visual/runtime conditions before switching.


# Troubleshooting (/en/docs/compatibility/troubleshooting)



Keep a minimal reproduction and console errors, then change one condition at a time. Verify the environment with the [quick start](/en/docs/getting-started/quick-start) instead of changing data, layout, and styling together.

[Blank canvas](#blank-canvas) · [Graph is very small](#tiny-graph-or-unexpected-position) · [Missing labels](#missing-or-overlapping-labels) · [Installation and runtime](#installation-and-runtime)

## Blank canvas [#blank-canvas]

Check mounted/non-zero container dimensions, initialization errors, unique node IDs, and endpoints. Start with two nodes and an edge, without optional styling or extensions.

```ts
const container = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('#container');
console.table({
  exists: Boolean(container),
  width: container?.clientWidth ?? 0,
  height: container?.clientHeight ?? 0,
  visibility: document.visibilityState,
});
```

If dimensions are valid but WebGL fails, check GPU/host/CSP instead of repeatedly constructing Graph.
[Runtime requirements](/en/docs/compatibility/browser) · [Data identity rules](/en/docs/api/options#options-data)

## Tiny graph or unexpected position [#tiny-graph-or-unexpected-position]

Check coordinates, outliers, and dimensions before changing fitView padding/maxZoom. First render, resize, setData, and layout fit differently. Do not force fitting after every user zoom.
[Why the graph is still small](/en/docs/guides/viewport#why-is-the-graph-still-small-after-fitting)

## Missing or overlapping labels [#missing-or-overlapping-labels]

Confirm node/edge.style.label produces text; then check zoom thresholds, collisions, colors, and clipping. Disable policies for a comparison, then restore them individually.
[Label guide](/en/docs/guides/label) · [Policy fields](/en/docs/api/options#options-label)

## Clicking, dragging, or edge events do not respond [#clicking-dragging-or-edge-events-do-not-respond]

Check behaviors, required Behavior types, and modifiers; \[] disables defaults. Inspect DOM overlays, edge hit areas, and event types. Subscribing to a derived event does not enable its Behavior.
[Interaction composition](/en/docs/guides/behaviors) · [Event reference](/en/docs/api/graph/events)

## Worker does not run or falls back [#worker-does-not-run-or-falls-back]

Inspect Worker requests, execution threads, clone errors, and server responses. Function/cyclic configuration may not clone; worker: true is not evidence of success.
[Worker deployment and cancellation](/en/docs/guides/layout-worker)

## Leftovers or duplicate responses after unmount [#leftovers-or-duplicate-responses-after-unmount]

Pair creation/destroy, on/off, and requests/cancellation. Handle StrictMode’s extra mounting with cleanup instead of skipping setup.
[React](/en/docs/getting-started/react) · [Vue](/en/docs/getting-started/vue) · [Extension cleanup](/en/docs/api/graph#extension-registration)

## Performance issues [#performance-issues]

### What if force layout makes startup slow? [#what-if-force-layout-makes-startup-slow]

Measure layout separately from render. Omit layout for supplied positions and assess Worker/iteration options where supported. See [performance tuning](/en/docs/metrics/performance#performance-tuning).

### What if highlighting or selection stutters? [#what-if-highlighting-or-selection-stutters]

Reuse Graph and update states instead of rebuilding or replacing the graph for a highlight. See the [state guide](/en/docs/guides/states).

## Installation and runtime [#installation-and-runtime]

### What browsers and WebGL capabilities are required? [#what-browsers-and-webgl-capabilities-are-required]

Real DOM, Canvas 2D, and a usable WebGL1 or WebGL2 context are required. See [runtime requirements](/en/docs/compatibility/browser) for modules, Worker, and CSP.

### Can Graph run directly in Node.js or during SSR? [#can-graph-run-directly-in-nodejs-or-during-ssr]

Graph does not render in ordinary Node.js/SSR. Create it after client mounting and destroy on unmount; see [framework integration](/en/docs/getting-started/react).

### Where should TypeScript types be imported from? [#where-should-typescript-types-be-imported-from]

Import values and types from the `@antv/g6-lite` package root and use the declarations shipped with your installed version. See [Configuration options](/en/docs/api/options) for constructor options and data types.

### What if an installed package does not contain a field? [#what-if-an-installed-package-does-not-contain-a-field]

Identify the actual version and root types rather than copying development-only fields. See [installation](/en/docs/getting-started/quick-start) for known archive and UMD differences.

## Choosing features and finding examples [#choosing-features-and-finding-examples]

### How should I choose between G6Lite and G6 v5? [#how-should-i-choose-between-g6lite-and-g6-v5]

Compare required graphics, runtime, and interactions, then validate with your own data. See [What is G6Lite?](/en/docs) for G6Lite's intended use cases.

### Can I use Combo? [#can-i-use-combo]

Grouping, nesting, and collapsing can be evaluated but remain experimental. Check [Combo boundaries](/en/docs/api/options#options-combo).

### Can examples run online? [#can-examples-run-online]

Run the [example gallery](/en/docs/examples); each case includes code, data descriptions, and interaction expectations.

## Provide reproducible information [#provide-reproducible-information]

```text
Package version / source commit:
Framework / bundler / deployment base path:
Browser / OS / GPU / DPR / container CSS size:
Minimal GraphData and options:
Steps:
Expected / actual:
First console error and failed network request:
Does the minimal quick-start graph work?
```


# Technical architecture (/en/docs/concepts/architecture)





This page explains module responsibilities and collaboration for readers exploring rendering, performance paths, or extension boundaries. See [Graph lifecycle methods](/en/docs/api/graph#graph-lifecycle) for the application calling sequence.

## Architecture layers [#architecture-layers]

<ArchitectureDiagram locale="en" />

Applications use `Graph` and extension contracts from the package root. Graph orchestrates transforms, layouts, and the runtime; DataModel owns graph data and states; RenderScheduler coordinates drawing based on the scope of each change. Renderer, Picking, and GPU buffers are internal implementation details.

These layers share one graph runtime. Layouts provide positions, interactions produce data or state changes, and the scheduler sends changes to the appropriate drawing layers. This division lets layouts, information layers, and interactions be extended independently.

## Drawing layers [#drawing-layers]

G6Lite batches nodes and edges through WebGL and uses Canvas 2D for text measurement, label collision, and grouping bounds:

| Layer, bottom to top | Content                        | Reason                                                    |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Canvas 2D underlay   | Combo boundaries               | Fits group bounds and background information              |
| Main WebGL canvas    | Nodes, edges, and arrows       | Supports batched geometry and buffer updates              |
| Canvas 2D overlay    | Labels, icons, and decorations | Supports text measurement, layout, and collision handling |

The layers share the camera, dimensions, DPR, and scheduling signals within one Graph. WebGL prefers WebGL2 and falls back to WebGL1. See [Browsers and runtime](/en/docs/compatibility/browser) for environment requirements.

## Rendering and update paths [#rendering-and-update-paths]

### First-render data flow [#first-render-data-flow]

Calling `render()` prepares input, builds the runtime, and draws the first frame:

<FirstRenderFlow locale="en" />

After asynchronous layout, Graph checks generation and destruction before committing stale results. The render Promise describes initialization/submission, not GPU completion; consult the [lifecycle contract](/en/docs/api/graph#graph-lifecycle) for plugin mounting and other boundaries. Generations are an internal cancellation and result-commit mechanism; applications manage instances through public lifecycle methods.

### Frequent-update paths [#frequent-update-paths]

RenderScheduler selects processing based on the change level:

| Change                                | Main path                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Node selected / highlight / inactive  | Resolve state and patch GPU styles, reprocessing when required               |
| Edge business fields or states        | Fully process data to keep edge types, visibility, and arrow batches aligned |
| Batched node positions                | Update adjacency data, upload affected buffer ranges, redraw Canvas layers   |
| Label or Combo information            | Redraw the corresponding Canvas 2D information layer                         |
| Camera pan and zoom                   | Update uniforms and draw without rebuilding graph-data buffers               |
| Full replacement or structural change | Update DataModel and fully or partially process render data and buffers      |

Selection, highlighting, and dragging should update the existing instance through state, position, and batch APIs. See [Data](/en/docs/guides/data) for choosing update methods and [Performance tuning](/en/docs/metrics/performance#performance-tuning) for practical guidance.

## Layout and interaction collaboration [#layout-and-interaction-collaboration]

### Layout and Worker [#layout-and-worker]

The layout layer computes positions from graph data and configuration. Graph commits the result to DataModel and passes it to Renderer. Official algorithms are lazy-loaded by `layout.type`; supported expensive layouts can run in a Worker to reduce main-thread blocking.

Cancelled layout results are not committed to the active render generation. A Worker does not remove algorithm cost, and data with existing coordinates can omit layout. See [Layout configuration](/en/docs/guides/layout) for algorithms, options, and Worker limits.

### Interaction and picking [#interaction-and-picking]

InteractionDispatcher centralizes pointer events and hit detection, then delivers normalized events to Behaviors:

```text
Native event → Hit detection → Graph event → Behavior → Public data or state API
```

Nodes and edges prefer GPU Picking and fall back to CPU detection when the picking buffer is unavailable. Combo uses its own geometric hit path. Picking buffers are maintained on demand; drawing does not always require a picking pass.

Interaction changes return through the update scheduler, so Behaviors do not need to manipulate framebuffers. See [Interactions](/en/docs/guides/behaviors) and [Events](/en/docs/guides/events) for application usage.

## Extension boundary [#extension-boundary]

G6Lite supports node, edge, label, decoration, layout, behavior, transform, and plugin extensions. These contribute shape descriptions, information layers, positions, event responses, or runtime orchestration.

Stateful extensions collaborate through the data, state, viewport, and `requestRender()` capabilities of `ExtensionContext`. They should not hold internal DataModel, Renderer, WebGL contexts, or GPU buffers.

See [Extensions](/en/docs/guides/extensions) for registration, instance scope, and cleanup. See the [Extension API](/en/docs/api/graph#graph-extensions) for signatures and types.

## Resource ownership and cleanup [#resource-ownership-and-cleanup]

| Resource                                                    | Owner              | Release boundary                           |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------ |
| Container, application fetch, external subscriptions        | Application        | Unmount or obsolete request                |
| Graph canvases, scheduling, resize observation, interaction | Graph              | destroy                                    |
| Worker / layout request                                     | Layout runtime     | Completion, cancellation, destruction      |
| Plugin DOM and subscriptions                                | Extension instance | Extension destroy                          |
| WebGL buffers / framebuffers                                | Internal renderer  | Runtime destruction / resource restoration |

These are implementation responsibilities, not additional application APIs. See [React](/en/docs/getting-started/react), [Vue](/en/docs/getting-started/vue), and the [public extension context](/en/docs/api/graph#extension-registration). Context restoration depends on the browser/device and does not guarantee automatic restoration of application state or page conditions.


# Combo overview (/en/docs/elements/combo)





## What is a combo [#what-is-a-combo]

A combo groups related nodes, such as Web and Mobile in a Client group. A combo can also contain other combos. Its expanded outline follows the positions and sizes of its members. When collapsed, it hides member nodes and can appear as a circle or rectangle.

## Data structure [#data-structure]

Define combos in `data.combos`. A node’s `comboId` identifies its combo, and a child combo’s `parentId` identifies its parent combo. Edge endpoints still use node IDs.

| Field       | Type                        | Required | Description                            |
| ----------- | --------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `id`        | `string`                    | Yes      | Unique combo ID                        |
| `parentId`  | `string`                    | No       | Parent combo ID                        |
| `collapsed` | `boolean`                   | No       | Whether the combo starts collapsed     |
| `states`    | `ElementState[]`            | No       | Initial states, such as `['selected']` |
| `style`     | `Partial<ComboStyleConfig>` | No       | Style for this combo                   |
| `data`      | `Record<string, unknown>`   | No       | Application data, such as a group name |

## Configuration [#configuration]

Set the default style in `combo.style`. To override a field for one combo, set it in that combo’s `style`. Supply node coordinates or let a layout calculate them.

Below, Web and Mobile belong to Client, which is nested in Platform. Archive starts collapsed.



```ts
data: {
  nodes: [
    { id: 'web', x: 100, y: 120, comboId: 'client' },
    { id: 'mobile', x: 220, y: 120, comboId: 'client' },
    { id: 'old-a', x: 420, y: 100, comboId: 'archive' },
    { id: 'old-b', x: 500, y: 140, comboId: 'archive' },
    { id: 'outside', x: 300, y: 260 },
  ],
  edges: [
    { id: 'live', source: 'mobile', target: 'outside' },
    { id: 'archived', source: 'old-a', target: 'outside' },
  ],
  combos: [
    { id: 'platform', data: { name: 'Platform' }, style: { padding: 24 } },
    { id: 'client', parentId: 'platform', data: { name: 'Client (selected)' }, states: ['selected'] },
    { id: 'archive', collapsed: true, data: { name: 'Archive (collapsed)' } },
  ],
},
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    // #region graph-data
    data: {
      nodes: [
        { id: 'web', x: 100, y: 120, comboId: 'client' },
        { id: 'mobile', x: 220, y: 120, comboId: 'client' },
        { id: 'old-a', x: 420, y: 100, comboId: 'archive' },
        { id: 'old-b', x: 500, y: 140, comboId: 'archive' },
        { id: 'outside', x: 300, y: 260 },
      ],
      edges: [
        { id: 'live', source: 'mobile', target: 'outside' },
        { id: 'archived', source: 'old-a', target: 'outside' },
      ],
      combos: [
        { id: 'platform', data: { name: 'Platform' }, style: { padding: 24 } },
        { id: 'client', parentId: 'platform', data: { name: 'Client (selected)' }, states: ['selected'] },
        { id: 'archive', collapsed: true, data: { name: 'Archive (collapsed)' } },
      ],
    },
    // #endregion graph-data
    node: { style: { size: 22, label: (node) => node.id } },
    edge: { style: { lineWidth: 2, endArrow: true } },
    combo: {
      style: {
        padding: 30,
        label: (combo) => String(combo.data?.name ?? combo.id),
        labelPlacement: 'top',
        collapsedType: 'rect',
        collapsedSize: [150, 44],
        stateStyles: { selected: { stroke: '#873bf4', strokeWidth: 2 } },
      },
    },
    behaviors: [],
    autoFit: { padding: 56, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}
```



See [Common combo options](/en/docs/guides/combo) for styling, collapsing, and dragging.


# Edge overview (/en/docs/elements/edge)





## What is an edge? [#what-is-an-edge]

An edge connects two nodes and represents a relationship such as a service call or process dependency. `source` identifies the starting node, and `target` identifies the destination. Use `endArrow` for an arrow at the target or `startArrow` for an arrow at the source.

Two nodes can share several edges, such as separate read and write connections. When `source` and `target` are the same node, the edge draws as a self-loop.

## Edge types [#edge-types]

| Built-in type | Use                                                               | Main options             |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `line`        | Default type for a direct connection                              | Width, color, and arrows |
| `arc`         | Curves for separating relationships or controlling the bend       | `curvature`              |
| `cubic`       | Smooth cubic Bézier connections between horizontal levels         | `curveOffset`            |
| `polyline`    | Routed connections in flowcharts, org charts, and directory trees | `router`, `radius`       |

See [Common edge options](/en/docs/guides/edge) for path parameters and parallel-edge settings.

## Data structure [#data-structure]

List edges in `data.edges`. Each item is a [`GraphEdge`](/en/docs/guides/data#graphedge).

| Field    | Type          | Required | Meaning                                                                                                             |
| -------- | ------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `source` | `string`      | Yes      | Starting node ID from `data.nodes`                                                                                  |
| `target` | `string`      | Yes      | Destination node ID from `data.nodes`                                                                               |
| `id`     | `string`      | No       | Unique edge ID, generated if omitted. Supply one to update, select, or distinguish edges between the same endpoints |
| `data`   | `EdgeData`    | No       | Application data such as protocol, latency, or weight                                                               |
| `states` | `EdgeState[]` | No       | Initial states such as `['selected']`                                                                               |

## Configuration methods [#configuration-methods]

Set `edge` in `new Graph()` to configure the graph-wide edge type and appearance. Store each edge’s properties in `data.edges` and read them with style functions in `edge.style`. This example labels the edge by protocol and sets its width by latency.

```ts
import { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';

const graph = new Graph({
  container: '#container',
  data: {
    nodes: [{ id: 'api', x: 80, y: 100 }, { id: 'db', x: 260, y: 100 }],
    edges: [{ id: 'api-db', source: 'api', target: 'db', data: { protocol: 'SQL', latency: 120 } }],
  },
  edge: {
    type: 'line',
    style: {
      endArrow: true,
      label: (_source, _target, edge) => String(edge.data?.protocol ?? ''),
      lineWidth: (_source, _target, edge) => Number(edge.data?.latency ?? 0) >= 100 ? 4 : 2,
    },
  },
});

await graph.render();
```

After rendering, call `graph.updateEdgeData('api-db', { latency: 60 })` to update that edge, or `graph.updateOptions({ edge: { style: { stroke: '#1783FF' } } })` to change all edge colors. See [Update edges dynamically](/en/docs/guides/edge#update-edges-dynamically).

## Custom edges [#custom-edges]

Use an `EdgeExtension` to package a built-in path with reusable styles, such as an arc whose color and width depend on its weight. See [Custom edges](/en/docs/guides/custom-edge).


# Node overview (/en/docs/elements/node)





## What is a node? [#what-is-a-node]

A node represents an object or concept in a graph, such as a user, device, or service. Each node has a unique `id`. Edges refer to node IDs through `source` and `target` to represent relationships.

## Node types [#node-types]

### Built-in nodes [#built-in-nodes]

Set `node.type` to use a built-in G6Lite node. The previews show filled and outlined circles, along with square and rounded rectangle corners.

| Node type | Type name | Use and dimensions                                                                           |
| --------- | --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Circle    | `circle`  | Default type for markers such as users or devices. Set the diameter with `size`.             |
| Rectangle | `rect`    | Useful for service names or cards. Set the shape with `width`, `height`, and `borderRadius`. |

See [Node body styles](/en/docs/guides/node#nodestyleconfig) for size and corner radius defaults.

### Custom nodes [#custom-nodes]

Use a `NodeExtension` with a `circle` or `rect` base to package a reusable node. For example, fill a service node according to its health and use `drawOverlay()` to add an alert marker. Call `register('node', name, extension)`, then assign the registered name to `node.type`. See [Custom nodes](/en/docs/guides/custom-node).

## Data structure [#data-structure]

List nodes in `data.nodes`. Each entry is a [`GraphNode`](/en/docs/guides/data#graphnode).

| Field      | Type          | Required | Meaning                                                    |
| ---------- | ------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`       | `string`      | Yes      | Unique ID for connecting, querying, and updating the node  |
| `name`     | `string`      | No       | Name available to label callbacks                          |
| `data`     | `NodeData`    | No       | Application data available to style functions              |
| `x`, `y`   | `number`      | No       | Position in graph coordinates when no layout is configured |
| `fx`, `fy` | `number`      | No       | Coordinates fixed after layout                             |
| `comboId`  | `string`      | No       | ID of a group declared in `data.combos`                    |
| `states`   | `NodeState[]` | No       | Initial states, such as `['selected']`                     |

```ts
const data = {
  nodes: [
    { id: 'api', name: 'API', x: 80, y: 100, data: { health: 'ok' } },
    { id: 'db', name: 'Database', x: 220, y: 100, data: { health: 'warning' } },
  ],
  edges: [{ source: 'api', target: 'db' }],
};
```

## Configuration methods [#configuration-methods]

### Configure all nodes at creation [#configure-all-nodes-at-creation]

Pass `node` to `new Graph()`. A constant style value applies to every node, such as the diameter of `32` below.

### Map styles from node data [#map-styles-from-node-data]

Assign a function to a field in `node.style`. This example uses each node's `data.health` for its fill and `name` for its label. The `#container` element needs to exist and have a width and height.

```ts
import { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';

const graph = new Graph({
  container: '#container',
  data,
  node: {
    type: 'circle',
    style: {
      size: 32,
      fill: (node) => node.data?.health === 'warning' ? '#F59E0B' : '#1783FF',
      label: (node) => node.name ?? node.id,
    },
  },
});

await graph.render();
```

Style fields resolve in this order: `node.style`, the extension's `getStyle()`, the extension's default styles, then the theme or built-in fallbacks. See [Common node options](/en/docs/guides/node#nodeconfig) for the full list of fields and how to configure them.

### Update nodes after rendering [#update-nodes-after-rendering]

Use `graph.updateNodeData()` to change one node's application data. Use `graph.updateOptions()` to change the graph's node configuration. Style objects merge by field. The example below gives the database node its healthy color and changes both circles to a diameter of `40`.

```ts
graph.updateNodeData('db', { health: 'ok' });
graph.updateOptions({ node: { style: { size: 40 } } });
```

## Node states [#node-states]

Set initial states in the node's `states` array. After rendering, call `graph.setItemState('db', 'selected', true)` to select the node. Pass `false` as the last argument to clear the selection. Set `node.stateStyles.selected` to customize the selection stroke, fill, or halo. See [Element states](/en/docs/guides/states) and [node state styles](/en/docs/guides/node#options-node-state-styles).


# Element overview (/en/docs/elements/overview)





The three kinds of elements in a G6Lite graph are **nodes**, **edges**, and **Combos**. Labels add names, describe relationships, or identify groups.

## Nodes [#node]

Nodes represent objects such as users, devices, or services. Choose `circle` or `rect` with `node.type`, then set size, fill, and stroke in `node.style`. The examples compare solid and outlined circles, and square and rounded rectangle corners.

[Node overview](/en/docs/elements/node)

## Edges [#edge]

Edges represent relationships such as friendships or service calls. Choose a straight line (`line`), arc (`arc`), cubic curve (`cubic`), or polyline (`polyline`) with `edge.type`. The arc below uses `lineDash`, and the cubic curve and polyline use `endArrow` to show direction.

Use `parallelEdges` to separate multiple relationships between a pair of nodes. Set `source` and `target` to the same node to draw a self-loop.

The polyline above uses the `orth` router. See the [org chart for tree](/en/docs/examples/org-chart), [indented tree for indented](/en/docs/examples/indented-tree), and [fishbone diagram for fishbone](/en/docs/examples/fishbone). See [Edge overview](/en/docs/elements/edge) for types and data structure.

## Combos [#combo]

Combos organize related nodes into groups. Use `comboId` to add a node to a group and `parentId` to nest a group. An expanded Combo draws a boundary around its members. Set `collapsedType` to show a circle or rectangle when collapsed, with a member count or custom text.

[Combo overview](/en/docs/elements/combo)

## Labels [#label]

Set a node name with `node.style.label`, describe a relationship with `edge.style.label`, or add a group title with `combo.style.label`. Use `labelPlacement` to position the text, `labelBackground` to add a background to a node or edge label, and `labelAutoRotate` to rotate a label along its edge.

[Label styling and visibility](/en/docs/guides/label)

## Parts of an element [#element-parts]

A node can combine a circle or rectangle with an `icon`, a `label`, and `node.decorations` such as a badge. An edge combines a path with optional arrows and a label. An expanded Combo can show a title on its boundary.

## Element states [#element-states]

`default` uses the base appearance. The other built-in states are `active`, `selected`, `highlight`, `inactive`, `disabled`, and `hidden`. The hidden preview is blank. The disabled preview shows a muted gray node.

The custom `review` state adds an orange fill. Combined with `selected`, it keeps the selection outline. Set initial states through `states` in the data or call `graph.setItemState()` after rendering. See [element states](/en/docs/guides/states) for how each element combines styles.

## Configure elements [#configure]

Set `node`, `edge`, and `combo` at the same level in `new Graph()`. This example uses `node.style` for the service nodes, `edge.style` for protocol labels and arrows, and `combo.style` for the storage group boundary and title. Click a node to see the outline set in `node.stateStyles.selected`.



```ts
node: {
  type: 'rect',
  style: {
    width: 96,
    height: 38,
    borderRadius: 8,
    fill: '#eef2ff',
    stroke: '#6366f1',
    strokeWidth: 1,
    label: (node) => node.name ?? node.id,
    labelPlacement: 'center',
    labelColor: '#1e293b',
  },
  stateStyles: { selected: { stroke: '#4338ca', strokeWidth: 3 } },
},
edge: {
  style: {
    stroke: '#64748b',
    endArrow: true,
    label: (_source, _target, edge) => String(edge.data?.protocol ?? ''),
    labelColor: '#334155',
    labelBackground: '#fff',
    labelBackgroundPadding: 4,
  },
},
combo: {
  style: {
    label: 'Storage',
    labelPlacement: 'top',
    labelColor: '#065f46',
    padding: 20,
    borderRadius: 12,
    fill: 'rgba(16,185,129,0.08)',
    stroke: '#6ee7b7',
  },
},
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: [
        { id: 'web', name: 'Browser' },
        { id: 'api', name: 'API' },
        { id: 'cache', name: 'Cache', comboId: 'storage' },
        { id: 'db', name: 'Database', comboId: 'storage' },
      ],
      edges: [
        { source: 'web', target: 'api', data: { protocol: 'HTTPS' } },
        { source: 'api', target: 'cache', data: { protocol: 'GET' } },
        { source: 'api', target: 'db', data: { protocol: 'SQL' } },
      ],
      combos: [{ id: 'storage' }],
    },
    // #region element-options
    node: {
      type: 'rect',
      style: {
        width: 96,
        height: 38,
        borderRadius: 8,
        fill: '#eef2ff',
        stroke: '#6366f1',
        strokeWidth: 1,
        label: (node) => node.name ?? node.id,
        labelPlacement: 'center',
        labelColor: '#1e293b',
      },
      stateStyles: { selected: { stroke: '#4338ca', strokeWidth: 3 } },
    },
    edge: {
      style: {
        stroke: '#64748b',
        endArrow: true,
        label: (_source, _target, edge) => String(edge.data?.protocol ?? ''),
        labelColor: '#334155',
        labelBackground: '#fff',
        labelBackgroundPadding: 4,
      },
    },
    combo: {
      style: {
        label: 'Storage',
        labelPlacement: 'top',
        labelColor: '#065f46',
        padding: 20,
        borderRadius: 12,
        fill: 'rgba(16,185,129,0.08)',
        stroke: '#6ee7b7',
      },
    },
    // #endregion element-options
    layout: { type: 'dagre', rankdir: 'LR', ranksep: 84, nodesep: 16, nodeSize: 96 },
    label: { hideOnLowZoom: false, scaleWithZoom: false },
    behaviors: ['click-select', 'drag-canvas', 'zoom-canvas'],
    autoFit: { padding: 36, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}
```



## Shape rendering and extensions [#drawing]

Switch examples to see how extensions use `register()` in G6Lite. Each guide includes the runnable source.

* [Custom nodes](/en/docs/guides/custom-node) change the node style by service status and draw an overlay.
* [Custom edges](/en/docs/guides/custom-edge) set arc color and width by edge weight.
* [Custom node decorations](/en/docs/guides/custom-decoration) draw and stack badges next to a node.
* [Custom label renderers](/en/docs/guides/custom-label-renderer) draw multiline text for nodes and edges.


# Quick start (/en/docs/getting-started/quick-start)





Choose an integration method. Both create the same team collaboration graph with 6 nodes and 7 edges.

* [Package manager](#package-manager) works with projects that use a bundler such as Vite or Webpack. Install the package and import `Graph` from `@antv/g6-lite`.
* [CDN](#cdn) works directly in HTML. Import `Graph` with a `<script type="module">` tag.

## Package manager [#package-manager]

### Install [#install]

For projects using a bundler such as Vite or Webpack, install G6Lite with one of the following package managers:

<div className="quick-start-install">
  ```bash
  # npm
  npm install @antv/g6-lite@0.1.0
  ```

  ```bash
  # pnpm
  pnpm add @antv/g6-lite@0.1.0
  ```

  ```bash
  # Yarn
  yarn add @antv/g6-lite@0.1.0
  ```
</div>

### Create the graph [#create-the-graph]

After installation, add a container with an explicit size:

```html
<div id="container" style="width: 100%; height: 360px"></div>
```

Then create a graph in your JavaScript or TypeScript entry after the container has mounted. Use `await` in an ES module or an `async` function.

```ts
import { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';

const data = {
  nodes: [
    { id: 'Alice', data: { color: '#5B8FF9', size: 40 } },
    { id: 'Bob', data: { color: '#5B8FF9', size: 28 } },
    { id: 'Carol', data: { color: '#5B8FF9', size: 28 } },
    { id: 'David', data: { color: '#61DDAA', size: 40 } },
    { id: 'Eva', data: { color: '#61DDAA', size: 28 } },
    { id: 'Frank', data: { color: '#61DDAA', size: 28 } },
  ],
  edges: [
    { source: 'Alice', target: 'Bob' },
    { source: 'Alice', target: 'Carol' },
    { source: 'David', target: 'Eva' },
    { source: 'David', target: 'Frank' },
    { source: 'Alice', target: 'David' },
    { source: 'Bob', target: 'Eva' },
    { source: 'Carol', target: 'Frank' },
  ],
};

const graph = new Graph({
  container: '#container',
  data,
  node: {
    style: {
      size: (node) => Number(node.data?.size ?? 26),
      fill: (node) => String(node.data?.color ?? '#5B8FF9'),
      stroke: '#fff',
      strokeWidth: 2,
      label: (node) => node.id,
      labelPlacement: 'bottom',
      labelColor: '#334155',
    },
  },
  edge: { style: { stroke: '#CBD5E1', lineWidth: 1.5 } },
  layout: {
    type: 'd3-force',
    linkDistance: 100,
    nodeStrength: -400,
    collideRadius: 32,
  },
  behaviors: ['zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas', 'drag-node', 'hover-highlight'],
});

try {
  await graph.render();
  graph.fitView({ padding: 48, maxZoom: 1.2 });
} catch (error) {
  graph.destroy();
  throw error;
}
```

TypeScript declarations are included in the package.

Call `graph.destroy()` before removing the container or unmounting the component.

## CDN [#cdn]

```js
import { Graph } from 'https://esm.sh/@antv/g6-lite@0.1.0?bundle';
```

### Create the graph [#create-the-graph-1]

Save the HTML below as `index.html` and open it in your browser.

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
    <title>G6Lite team collaboration network</title>
  </head>
  <body>
    <div id="container" style="height: 360px"></div>
    <script type="module">
      import { Graph } from 'https://esm.sh/@antv/g6-lite@0.1.0?bundle';

      const data = {
        nodes: [
          { id: 'Alice', data: { color: '#5B8FF9', size: 40 } },
          { id: 'Bob', data: { color: '#5B8FF9', size: 28 } },
          { id: 'Carol', data: { color: '#5B8FF9', size: 28 } },
          { id: 'David', data: { color: '#61DDAA', size: 40 } },
          { id: 'Eva', data: { color: '#61DDAA', size: 28 } },
          { id: 'Frank', data: { color: '#61DDAA', size: 28 } },
        ],
        edges: [
          { source: 'Alice', target: 'Bob' },
          { source: 'Alice', target: 'Carol' },
          { source: 'David', target: 'Eva' },
          { source: 'David', target: 'Frank' },
          { source: 'Alice', target: 'David' },
          { source: 'Bob', target: 'Eva' },
          { source: 'Carol', target: 'Frank' },
        ],
      };

      const graph = new Graph({
        container: '#container',
        data,
        node: {
          style: {
            size: (node) => Number(node.data?.size ?? 26),
            fill: (node) => String(node.data?.color ?? '#5B8FF9'),
            stroke: '#fff',
            strokeWidth: 2,
            label: (node) => node.id,
            labelPlacement: 'bottom',
            labelColor: '#334155',
          },
        },
        edge: { style: { stroke: '#CBD5E1', lineWidth: 1.5 } },
        layout: {
          type: 'd3-force',
          linkDistance: 100,
          nodeStrength: -400,
          collideRadius: 32,
        },
        behaviors: ['zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas', 'drag-node', 'hover-highlight'],
      });

      graph.render().then(() => {
        graph.fitView({ padding: 48, maxZoom: 1.2 });
      }).catch((error) => {
        graph.destroy();
        console.error(error);
      });
      window.addEventListener('pagehide', () => graph.destroy(), { once: true });
    </script>
  </body>
</html>
```

The single-page example destroys the instance on `pagehide`. Recreate it if the browser restores the page from its back/forward cache.

# React integration (/en/docs/getting-started/react)





## Use with React [#use-with-react]

Import `GraphView` into your page.

```tsx
import GraphView from './GraphView';

export default function App() {
  return <GraphView />;
}
```

<span id="prepare-two-datasets" style="{ display: 'block', scrollMarginTop: '8rem' }" />

<span id="react-respond-to-data-dependency-changes" style="{ display: 'block', scrollMarginTop: '8rem' }" />

### Define GraphView [#define-graphview]

Save the following as `GraphView.tsx`. The component creates a graph on mount, calls `setData()` when you switch datasets, and destroys the instance on unmount.

```tsx
'use client';

import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react';
import { Graph, type GraphData } from '@antv/g6-lite';

const basicData: GraphData = {
  nodes: [{ id: 'Alice' }, { id: 'Bob' }, { id: 'Carol' }],
  edges: [
    { source: 'Alice', target: 'Bob' },
    { source: 'Alice', target: 'Carol' },
  ],
};

const expandedData: GraphData = {
  nodes: [...basicData.nodes, { id: 'David' }],
  edges: [...basicData.edges, { source: 'Bob', target: 'David' }],
};

const fitView = { padding: 32, maxZoom: 1 };

export default function GraphView() {
  const containerRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const graphRef = useRef<Graph | null>(null);
  const [ready, setReady] = useState(false);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!containerRef.current) return;

    const graph = new Graph({
      container: containerRef.current,
      data: basicData,
      layout: { type: 'circular', radius: 120 },
      node: { style: { size: 24, label: (node) => node.id, labelPlacement: 'bottom' } },
      edge: { style: { endArrow: true } },
      autoFit: fitView,
      behaviors: ['zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas', 'drag-node', 'hover-highlight'],
    });

    graph.render().then(() => {
      if (graph.destroyed) return;
      graphRef.current = graph;
      setReady(true);
    }).catch((error) => {
      if (!graph.destroyed) {
        graph.destroy();
        console.error(error);
      }
    });

    return () => {
      graphRef.current = null;
      graph.destroy();
    };
  }, []);

  async function changeData(data: GraphData) {
    const graph = graphRef.current;
    if (!graph) return;
    try {
      await graph.setData(data, { fitView });
    } catch (error) {
      if (!graph.destroyed) console.error(error);
    }
  }

  return (
    <div>
      <select
        aria-label="Graph data"
        defaultValue="basic"
        disabled={!ready}
        onChange={(event) => void changeData(event.target.value === 'expanded' ? expandedData : basicData)}
      >
        <option value="basic">Basic network</option>
        <option value="expanded">Extended network</option>
      </select>
      <div ref={containerRef} style={{ width: '100%', height: 360 }} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Result [#update-the-graph-when-data-changes]

Select “Extended network” to add David and the Bob → David edge. Select “Basic network” to restore the original graph.

<QuickStartExample locale="en" variant="framework-data" />

<span id="vue-synchronize-data-with-watch" style="{ display: 'block', scrollMarginTop: '8rem' }" />


<span id="prepare-two-datasets" style="{ display: 'block', scrollMarginTop: '8rem' }" />

<span id="vue-synchronize-data-with-watch" style="{ display: 'block', scrollMarginTop: '8rem' }" />

### Define GraphView [#define-graphview]

Save the following as `GraphView.vue`. The component creates a graph on mount, calls `setData()` when you switch datasets, and destroys the instance on unmount.

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { onBeforeUnmount, onMounted, ref } from 'vue';
import { Graph, type GraphData } from '@antv/g6-lite';

const basicData: GraphData = {
  nodes: [{ id: 'Alice' }, { id: 'Bob' }, { id: 'Carol' }],
  edges: [
    { source: 'Alice', target: 'Bob' },
    { source: 'Alice', target: 'Carol' },
  ],
};

const expandedData: GraphData = {
  nodes: [...basicData.nodes, { id: 'David' }],
  edges: [...basicData.edges, { source: 'Bob', target: 'David' }],
};

const fitView = { padding: 32, maxZoom: 1 };
const containerRef = ref<HTMLDivElement | null>(null);
const ready = ref(false);
let graph: Graph | undefined;

onMounted(async () => {
  if (!containerRef.value) return;

  const instance = new Graph({
    container: containerRef.value,
    data: basicData,
    layout: { type: 'circular', radius: 120 },
    node: { style: { size: 24, label: (node) => node.id, labelPlacement: 'bottom' } },
    edge: { style: { endArrow: true } },
    autoFit: fitView,
    behaviors: ['zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas', 'drag-node', 'hover-highlight'],
  });
  graph = instance;

  try {
    await instance.render();
    if (!instance.destroyed) ready.value = true;
  } catch (error) {
    if (!instance.destroyed) {
      instance.destroy();
      console.error(error);
    }
  }
});

onBeforeUnmount(() => graph?.destroy());

async function changeData(event: Event) {
  const instance = graph;
  if (!ready.value || !instance || instance.destroyed) return;

  const { value } = event.target as HTMLSelectElement;
  const data = value === 'expanded' ? expandedData : basicData;
  try {
    await instance.setData(data, { fitView });
  } catch (error) {
    if (!instance.destroyed) console.error(error);
  }
}
</script>

<template>
  <div>
    <select aria-label="Graph data" :disabled="!ready" @change="changeData">
      <option value="basic">Basic network</option>
      <option value="expanded">Extended network</option>
    </select>
    <div ref="containerRef" style="width: 100%; height: 360px" />
  </div>
</template>
```

## Result [#update-the-graph-when-data-changes]

Select “Extended network” to add David and the Bob → David edge. Select “Basic network” to restore the original graph.

<QuickStartExample locale="en" variant="framework-data" />


# Graph overview (/en/docs/graph/overview)





## What is a Graph? [#what-is-a-graph]

A graph describes objects as nodes and relationships as edges. A G6Lite `Graph` instance draws that data in a container and provides methods to query elements, adjust the viewport, and listen for interactions.

A graph instance typically goes through four steps.

1. **Create.** Call `new Graph(options)` to bind the container and initialize rendering resources.
2. **Render.** Await `graph.render()` to complete the initial layout and draw the graph.
3. **Update.** Reuse the instance. Call `setData()` to replace graph data and `updateOptions()` to change supported options.
4. **Destroy.** Call `graph.destroy()` when leaving the page or unmounting the component to release the canvas and listeners.

<span id="working-with-a-graph" />

## Use G6Lite Graph [#use-g6lite-graph]

Follow the [quick start](/en/docs/getting-started/quick-start) to install `@antv/g6-lite`. Mount a container with nonzero width and height, then create and render the graph.

```html
<div id="container" style="width: 100%; height: 320px"></div>
```

```ts
import { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';

const graph = new Graph({
  container: '#container',
  data: {
    nodes: [
      { id: 'browser', x: 0, y: 0 },
      { id: 'api', x: 120, y: 0 },
    ],
    edges: [{ source: 'browser', target: 'api' }],
  },
});

await graph.render();
```

After the first render, you can focus a node or update the data. For method timing and cleanup, see the [Graph lifecycle API](/en/docs/api/graph#graph-lifecycle).

<span id="container-and-options" />

## Graph options [#graph-options]

`GraphOptions` is the configuration object passed to the constructor. See the [GraphOptions API](/en/docs/api/options#graphoptions) for the full type definitions and details.

| Option       | Type                                  | Default              | Purpose                                                                                |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------- | -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `container`  | `string \| HTMLElement`               | Required             | Mounts the graph. String values are CSS selectors.                                     |
| `data`       | `GraphData`                           | Required             | Supplies nodes, edges, and optional Combo groups.                                      |
| `autoFit`    | `boolean \| number \| FitViewOptions` | `false`              | Controls refitting on container resize. The first render fits the graph automatically. |
| `node`       | `NodeConfig`                          | Circle nodes         | Sets node shapes, styles, and states.                                                  |
| `edge`       | `EdgeConfig`                          | Straight edges       | Sets edge shapes, arrowheads, and states.                                              |
| `combo`      | `ComboConfig`                         | Built-in styles      | Sets group appearance, labels, and collapsed shapes.                                   |
| `label`      | `LabelOptions`                        | Built-in policy      | Controls label scaling and visibility.                                                 |
| `layout`     | `LayoutConfig`                        | Input coordinates    | Chooses the algorithm and options for positioning nodes.                               |
| `behaviors`  | `BehaviorOption[]`                    | Canvas zoom and drag | Configures interactions such as zooming, dragging, and selection.                      |
| `theme`      | `ThemeOption`                         | `'light'`            | Sets default styles for the canvas and elements.                                       |
| `transforms` | `TransformOption[]`                   | None                 | Processes input data in order before layout.                                           |
| `plugins`    | `PluginOption[]`                      | None                 | Mounts registered plugins.                                                             |

The container sets the initial canvas dimensions. See [Viewport and coordinates](/en/docs/guides/viewport) for fitting and resizing.

## Graph properties [#graph-properties]

| Property                                                          | Type      | Description                                                                                                       |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`graph.destroyed`](/en/docs/api/graph#graph-lifecycle-destroyed) | `boolean` | Read-only. Becomes `true` when destruction begins. Check it before using the graph after an asynchronous request. |

Use `await graph.render()` to wait for the initial render.

## Example [#example]

### Complete creation and configuration example [#complete-creation-and-configuration-example]

The example uses Dagre to lay out the dependencies from left to right and groups Cache and Database in a Combo. Click a node to see its selected style, or drag and zoom the canvas.



```ts
import { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: [
        { id: 'web', name: 'Browser' },
        { id: 'api', name: 'API' },
        { id: 'cache', name: 'Cache', comboId: 'storage' },
        { id: 'db', name: 'Database', comboId: 'storage' },
      ],
      edges: [
        { source: 'web', target: 'api', data: { protocol: 'HTTPS' } },
        { source: 'api', target: 'cache', data: { protocol: 'GET' } },
        { source: 'api', target: 'db', data: { protocol: 'SQL' } },
      ],
      combos: [{ id: 'storage' }],
    },
    // #region element-options
    node: {
      type: 'rect',
      style: {
        width: 96,
        height: 38,
        borderRadius: 8,
        fill: '#eef2ff',
        stroke: '#6366f1',
        strokeWidth: 1,
        label: (node) => node.name ?? node.id,
        labelPlacement: 'center',
        labelColor: '#1e293b',
      },
      stateStyles: { selected: { stroke: '#4338ca', strokeWidth: 3 } },
    },
    edge: {
      style: {
        stroke: '#64748b',
        endArrow: true,
        label: (_source, _target, edge) => String(edge.data?.protocol ?? ''),
        labelColor: '#334155',
        labelBackground: '#fff',
        labelBackgroundPadding: 4,
      },
    },
    combo: {
      style: {
        label: 'Storage',
        labelPlacement: 'top',
        labelColor: '#065f46',
        padding: 20,
        borderRadius: 12,
        fill: 'rgba(16,185,129,0.08)',
        stroke: '#6ee7b7',
      },
    },
    // #endregion element-options
    layout: { type: 'dagre', rankdir: 'LR', ranksep: 84, nodesep: 16, nodeSize: 96 },
    label: { hideOnLowZoom: false, scaleWithZoom: false },
    behaviors: ['click-select', 'drag-canvas', 'zoom-canvas'],
    autoFit: { padding: 36, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}
```

# Breathing node (/en/docs/examples/breathing-node)





Compare selected, highlight and normal states with the built-in breathing-node effect.

## Try it

Toggle selected and highlight to see the node animation.

## Data

3 built-in breathing-node nodes and 2 edges compare initial selected, highlight and normal states.

## Complete runnable code

```ts
// Local presentation helpers in this repository are used only for the example controls.
/**
 * Breathing node demo.
 * Demonstrates the built-in breathing-node extension on selected/highlight states.
 */

import { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import { createDemoPanel } from './demo-panel.ts';

export async function run(container: string | HTMLElement) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    autoFit: true,
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: [
        { id: 'selected', x: 180, y: 180, data: { label: 'Selected' }, states: ['selected'] },
        { id: 'highlight', x: 360, y: 180, data: { label: 'Highlight' }, states: ['highlight'] },
        { id: 'normal', x: 540, y: 180, data: { label: 'Normal' } },
      ],
      edges: [
        { id: 'edge-selected-highlight', source: 'selected', target: 'highlight' },
        { id: 'edge-highlight-normal', source: 'highlight', target: 'normal' },
      ],
    },
    // #region breathing-options
    node: {
      type: 'breathing-node',
      style: {
        size: 36,
        fill: '#1677ff',
        stroke: '#fff',
        strokeWidth: 2,
        label: (node) => String(node.data?.label ?? node.id),
        labelPlacement: 'bottom',
        labelFontSize: 12,
      },
      stateStyles: {
        selected: { fill: '#1677ff', stroke: '#003eb3', strokeWidth: 3, haloWidth: 16 },
        highlight: { fill: '#2E8B57', stroke: '#1F6B43', strokeWidth: 3, haloWidth: 12 },
      },
    },
    // #endregion breathing-options
    edge: {
      style: {
        stroke: '#d1d5db',
        lineWidth: 2,
        endArrow: true,
      },
    },
    behaviors: ['zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas', 'drag-node', 'click-select'],
  });

  const ui = createDemoPanel(container, '切换选中和高亮，观察节点呼吸动画。');
  const destroy = graph.destroy.bind(graph);
  graph.destroy = () => {
    ui.destroy();
    destroy();
  };

  const toggleState = (state: 'selected' | 'highlight') => {
    const active = graph.getItemStates(state).includes(state);
    graph.setItemState(state, state, !active);
  };
  try {
    await graph.render();
    ui.addAction('切换选中', () => toggleState('selected'));
    ui.addAction('切换高亮', () => toggleState('highlight'));
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}
```


## Related documentation

- [Custom nodes](/en/docs/guides/custom-node)
- [Drawing contracts](/en/docs/api/extensions#extension-drawing)

# Combo containers (/en/docs/examples/combo)





Explore nested groups, collapse and expand, runtime regrouping, and data export.

## Try it

Click a group background to collapse or expand it. Use the canvas buttons for bulk actions and the menu to move nodes, create a combo, or export data.

## Data

Ten business nodes, nine edges, and four nested groups.

## Complete runnable code

```ts
// Local presentation helpers in this repository are used only for the example controls.
/**
 * Combo (Group Container) Demo
 * Demonstrates: nested application groups, fixed positioning, collapse/expand,
 * membership changes, runtime combo creation, and data export.
 */

import { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import { createDemoPanel } from './demo-panel.ts';

const NODE_COLORS: Record<string, string> = {
  client: '#7D9FD3',
  service: '#70A991',
  data: '#C89C5D',
  observability: '#9299A8',
};

export async function run(container: string | HTMLElement) {
  const containerEl =
    typeof container === 'string'
      ? (document.querySelector(container) as HTMLElement)
      : container;
  containerEl.style.position = 'relative';

  const graph = new Graph({
    autoFit: true,
    container: containerEl,
    data: {
      nodes: [
        {
          id: 'web',
          name: 'Web 端',
          x: 100,
          y: 150,
          comboId: 'client-apps',
          data: { layer: 'client' },
        },
        {
          id: 'mobile',
          name: '移动端',
          x: 100,
          y: 255,
          comboId: 'client-apps',
          data: { layer: 'client' },
        },
        {
          id: 'console',
          name: '运营控制台',
          x: 100,
          y: 360,
          comboId: 'client-apps',
          data: { layer: 'client' },
        },
        {
          id: 'gateway',
          name: 'API 网关',
          x: 335,
          y: 255,
          comboId: 'service-layer',
          data: { layer: 'service' },
        },
        {
          id: 'auth',
          name: '认证服务',
          x: 500,
          y: 150,
          comboId: 'service-layer',
          data: { layer: 'service' },
        },
        {
          id: 'order',
          name: '订单服务',
          x: 500,
          y: 255,
          comboId: 'service-layer',
          data: { layer: 'service' },
        },
        {
          id: 'worker',
          name: '异步任务',
          x: 500,
          y: 360,
          comboId: 'service-layer',
          data: { layer: 'service' },
        },
        {
          id: 'cache',
          name: 'Redis 缓存',
          x: 720,
          y: 150,
          comboId: 'data-layer',
          data: { layer: 'data' },
        },
        {
          id: 'mysql',
          name: 'MySQL',
          x: 720,
          y: 255,
          comboId: 'data-layer',
          data: { layer: 'data' },
        },
        {
          id: 'mq',
          name: '消息队列',
          x: 720,
          y: 360,
          comboId: 'data-layer',
          data: { layer: 'data' },
        },
      ],
      edges: [
        { source: 'web', target: 'gateway' },
        { source: 'mobile', target: 'gateway' },
        { source: 'console', target: 'gateway' },
        { source: 'gateway', target: 'auth' },
        { source: 'gateway', target: 'order' },
        { source: 'gateway', target: 'worker' },
        { source: 'auth', target: 'cache' },
        { source: 'order', target: 'mysql' },
        { source: 'worker', target: 'mq' },
      ],
      combos: [
        {
          id: 'client-apps',
          data: { name: '客户端' },
          style: {
            fill: 'rgba(104, 145, 205, 0.08)',
            stroke: 'rgba(104, 145, 205, 0.42)',
            padding: 38,
          },
        },
        {
          id: 'business-platform',
          data: { name: '业务平台' },
          style: {
            fill: 'rgba(112, 132, 160, 0.045)',
            stroke: 'rgba(112, 132, 160, 0.28)',
            padding: 24,
            labelFontSize: 13,
          },
        },
        {
          id: 'service-layer',
          parentId: 'business-platform',
          data: { name: '服务层' },
          style: {
            fill: 'rgba(91, 158, 130, 0.08)',
            stroke: 'rgba(91, 158, 130, 0.4)',
            padding: 38,
          },
        },
        {
          id: 'data-layer',
          parentId: 'business-platform',
          data: { name: '数据层' },
          style: {
            fill: 'rgba(205, 155, 82, 0.09)',
            stroke: 'rgba(205, 155, 82, 0.42)',
            padding: 38,
          },
        },
      ],
    },
    node: {
      type: 'circle',
      style: {
        size: 18,
        fill: (node) => NODE_COLORS[String(node.data?.layer)] ?? '#9CA3AF',
        stroke: '#FFFFFF',
        strokeWidth: 2,
        label: (node) =>
          node.name ?? (node.data?.label as string | undefined) ?? node.id,
        labelPlacement: 'bottom',
        labelOffsetY: 4,
        labelFontSize: 11,
        labelColor: '#475569',
      },
      stateStyles: {
        selected: { stroke: '#3B82F6', strokeWidth: 3 },
      },
    },
    edge: {
      type: 'cubic',
      style: {
        stroke: 'rgba(115, 137, 166, 0.58)',
        lineWidth: 1.2,
        endArrow: false,
      },
    },
    combo: {
      style: {
        borderRadius: 12,
        label: (combo) =>
          (combo.data as Record<string, string> | undefined)?.name ?? combo.id,
        labelPlacement: 'inside',
        labelFontSize: 12,
        labelColor: '#526071',
        collapsedType: 'rect',
        collapsedSize: [72, 38],
        count: false,
        stateStyles: {
          selected: { stroke: '#3B82F6', strokeWidth: 2 },
          active: { stroke: '#60A5FA', strokeWidth: 2 },
        },
      },
    },
    behaviors: ['zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas', 'drag-node', 'click-select'],
  });

  await graph.render();
  graph.fitView(0.82);

  const ui = createDemoPanel(containerEl, '点击分组背景可折叠或展开');
  let consoleInService = false;
  let runtimeCreated = false;

  ui.addAction('全部折叠', () => {
    graph.collapseCombo('client-apps');
    graph.collapseCombo('business-platform');
    if (runtimeCreated) graph.collapseCombo('observability');
    ui.setStatus('已折叠顶层分组');
  });

  ui.addAction('全部展开', () => {
    graph.expandCombo('business-platform');
    graph.expandCombo('client-apps');
    graph.expandCombo('service-layer');
    graph.expandCombo('data-layer');
    if (runtimeCreated) graph.expandCombo('observability');
    ui.setStatus('已展开全部分组');
  });

  const toggleGroup = (comboId: string) => {
    graph.toggleCombo(comboId);
    const group = graph.getComboData(comboId);
    ui.setStatus(`${group?.data?.name ?? comboId}${group?.collapsed ? '已折叠' : '已展开'}`);
  };

  graph.on('combo:click', ({ comboId }) => toggleGroup(comboId));
  const more = ui.gui.addFolder('更多').close();
  ui.addAction('切换数据层', () => {
    graph.expandCombo('business-platform');
    toggleGroup('data-layer');
  }, more);

  const consoleButton = ui.addAction('控制台加入服务层', () => {
    graph.expandCombo('business-platform');
    graph.expandCombo('service-layer');
    if (consoleInService) {
      graph.addToCombo('console', 'client-apps');
      consoleButton.name('控制台加入服务层');
      ui.setStatus('运营控制台已回到客户端');
    } else {
      graph.addToCombo('console', 'service-layer');
      consoleButton.name('控制台回到客户端');
      ui.setStatus('运营控制台已加入服务层');
    }
    consoleInService = !consoleInService;
  }, more);

  const runtimeButton = ui.addAction('创建可观测分组', () => {
    if (runtimeCreated) return;
    graph.addNodes([
      {
        id: 'logs',
        x: 570,
        y: 455,
        data: { layer: 'observability', label: '日志采集' },
      },
      {
        id: 'metrics',
        x: 720,
        y: 455,
        data: { layer: 'observability', label: '指标监控' },
      },
    ]);
    graph.createCombo(
      {
        id: 'observability',
        data: { name: '可观测性', source: 'createCombo' },
        style: {
          fill: 'rgba(134, 126, 176, 0.08)',
          stroke: 'rgba(134, 126, 176, 0.42)',
          padding: 32,
          label: '可观测性',
          labelPlacement: 'inside',
          labelColor: '#645F83',
          collapsedType: 'rect',
          collapsedSize: [84, 38],
          count: false,
        },
      },
      ['logs', 'metrics'],
    );
    runtimeCreated = true;
    runtimeButton.name('已创建可观测分组').disable();
    graph.fitView(0.78);
    ui.setStatus('createCombo() 已执行');
  }, more);

  ui.addAction('导出数据', () => {
    const data = graph.getData();
    const blob = new Blob([JSON.stringify(data, null, 2)], { type: 'application/json' });
    const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
    const link = document.createElement('a');
    link.href = url;
    link.download = 'g6lite-combo-data.json';
    link.click();
    URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
    ui.setStatus(`${data.nodes.length} 节点 · ${data.combos?.length ?? 0} 分组`);
  }, more);

  return {
    getData: () => graph.getData(),
    fitView: () => graph.fitView({ padding: 64 }),
    destroy() {
      graph.destroy();
      ui.destroy();
    },
  };
}
```

# Context menu (/en/docs/examples/context-menu)





Open a node context menu to focus or highlight it.

## Try it

Right-click a node, then focus or highlight it.

## Data

Three flow nodes listen for node:contextmenu.

## Complete runnable code

```ts
/**
 * Demo: open a node context menu from node:contextmenu.
 */
import { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import GUI from 'lil-gui';

export async function run(container: string | HTMLElement) {
  const host = typeof container === 'string' ? document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(container)! : container;
  host.style.position = 'relative';

  const graph = new Graph({
    autoFit: true,
    container: host,
    data: {
      nodes: [
        { id: 'design', data: { label: '设计' }, x: 180, y: 160 },
        { id: 'review', data: { label: '评审' }, x: 380, y: 160 },
        { id: 'build', data: { label: '实现' }, x: 560, y: 160 },
      ],
      edges: [
        { source: 'design', target: 'review' },
        { source: 'review', target: 'build' },
      ],
    },
    node: {
      type: 'rect',
      style: {
        fill: '#5B8FF9',
        width: 88,
        height: 36,
        borderRadius: 8,
        label: (node) => String(node.data?.label ?? node.id),
        labelPlacement: 'center',
        labelColor: '#fff',
      },
    },
    edge: { style: { endArrow: true, lineWidth: 1.5 } },
    behaviors: ['zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas'],
  });
  await graph.render();
  graph.fitView({ padding: 80 });

  const menu = new GUI({ container: host, title: '节点操作', width: 128 }).hide();
  const element = menu.domElement;
  element.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
  Object.assign(element.style, {
    position: 'absolute',
    zIndex: '30',
    maxWidth: '100%',
    maxHeight: '100%',
  });

  let activeId = '';
  const close = () => {
    menu.hide();
  };
  const addAction = (label: string, action: () => void) => {
    menu.add({
      [label]() {
        action();
        close();
      },
    }, label);
  };
  addAction('聚焦', () => graph.focusItem(activeId, 80));
  addAction('高亮', () => {
    for (const node of graph.getNodes()) graph.clearItemStates(node.id);
    graph.setItemState(activeId, 'selected', true);
  });

  graph.on('node:contextmenu', ({ nodeId, nativeEvent }) => {
    nativeEvent.preventDefault();
    activeId = nodeId;
    const bounds = host.getBoundingClientRect();
    menu.open().show();
    const x = Math.max(0, Math.min(nativeEvent.clientX - bounds.left, bounds.width - element.offsetWidth));
    const y = Math.max(0, Math.min(nativeEvent.clientY - bounds.top, bounds.height - element.offsetHeight));
    element.style.left = `${x}px`;
    element.style.top = `${y}px`;
  });
  graph.on('canvas:click', close);

  return {
    getData: () => graph.getData(),
    fitView: () => graph.fitView({ padding: 80 }),
    destroy() {
      graph.destroy();
      menu.destroy();
    },
  };
}
```


## Related documentation

- [Event guide](/en/docs/guides/events)
- [Event reference](/en/docs/api/graph/events)

# Register a custom interaction (/en/docs/examples/custom-behavior)





Register a behavior that selects a clicked node and clears selection on the canvas.

## Try it

Click a node to select it, or click empty canvas to clear the selection.

## Data

Four flow nodes are selected by the custom pin-node behavior.

## Complete runnable code

```ts
/**
 * Demo: register a behavior that selects the clicked node.
 */
import {
  Graph,
  register,
  type BehaviorExtension,
  type BehaviorOptions,
  type ExtensionContext,
} from '@antv/g6-lite';

const PIN_BEHAVIOR = 'pin-node' as const;

type PinBehaviorOptions = BehaviorOptions<typeof PIN_BEHAVIOR>;

function createPinBehavior(): BehaviorExtension<PinBehaviorOptions> {
  let context: ExtensionContext | undefined;
  return {
    init(nextContext) {
      context = nextContext;
    },
    getEvents() {
      return {
        'node:click': ({ nodeId }) => {
          if (!context) return;
          const stateMap = Object.fromEntries(
            context.data.getNodeIds().map((id) => [id, id === nodeId ? ['selected'] : []]),
          );
          context.state.setAll(stateMap);
        },
        'canvas:click': () => {
          if (!context) return;
          const stateMap = Object.fromEntries(context.data.getNodeIds().map((id) => [id, []]));
          context.state.setAll(stateMap);
        },
      };
    },
    destroy() {
      context = undefined;
    },
  };
}

register('behavior', PIN_BEHAVIOR, () => createPinBehavior());

export async function run(container: string | HTMLElement) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    autoFit: true,
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: [
        { id: 'inbox', data: { label: '收件箱' } },
        { id: 'draft', data: { label: '草稿' } },
        { id: 'sent', data: { label: '已发送' } },
        { id: 'archive', data: { label: '归档' } },
      ],
      edges: [
        { source: 'inbox', target: 'draft' },
        { source: 'draft', target: 'sent' },
        { source: 'sent', target: 'archive' },
      ],
    },
    node: {
      type: 'rect',
      style: {
        fill: '#5B8FF9',
        width: 88,
        height: 36,
        borderRadius: 8,
        label: (node) => String(node.data?.label ?? node.id),
        labelPlacement: 'center',
        labelColor: '#fff',
      },
    },
    edge: { style: { endArrow: true } },
    layout: { type: 'dagre', rankdir: 'LR', nodesep: 24, ranksep: 70, nodeSize: [88, 36] },
    behaviors: ['zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas', { type: PIN_BEHAVIOR } satisfies PinBehaviorOptions],
  });
  await graph.render();
  return graph;
}
```


## Related documentation

- [Custom interactions](/en/docs/guides/custom-behavior)
- [Behavior reference](/en/docs/api/options#options-behaviors)

# Custom label renderer (/en/docs/examples/custom-label-renderer)





Share one custom label renderer between nodes and edges.

## Try it

Inspect the custom multiline labels on nodes and edges.

## Data

Nodes and edges share one multiline label renderer.

## Complete runnable code

```ts
/**
 * Demo: unified custom node/edge LabelRenderer lifecycle.
 * The multiline behavior lives entirely in this demo, not in G6Lite core.
 */
import { Graph, register, type LabelRenderer } from '@antv/g6-lite';

interface MultilineLayoutData {
  lines: string[];
  lineHeight: number;
  contentWidth: number;
}

// #region renderer
const multilineRenderer: LabelRenderer<MultilineLayoutData> = {
  measure({ ctx, text, style }) {
    ctx.font = `${style.labelFontWeight} ${style.labelFontSize}px ${style.labelFontFamily}`;
    const lines = text.split('\n');
    const lineHeight = style.labelFontSize * 1.2;
    const contentWidth = Math.max(...lines.map((line) => ctx.measureText(line).width));
    const padding = style.labelBackgroundPadding;
    return {
      width: contentWidth + padding * 2,
      height: lines.length * lineHeight + padding * 2,
      data: { lines, lineHeight, contentWidth },
    };
  },
  draw({ ctx, style, layout }) {
    const data = layout.data;
    if (!data) return;
    if (style.labelBackground) {
      ctx.fillStyle = style.labelBackground;
      ctx.fillRect(-layout.width / 2, -layout.height / 2, layout.width, layout.height);
    }
    ctx.font = `${style.labelFontWeight} ${style.labelFontSize}px ${style.labelFontFamily}`;
    ctx.fillStyle = style.labelColor;
    ctx.textAlign = 'center';
    ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';
    data.lines.forEach((line, index) => {
      const y = (index - (data.lines.length - 1) / 2) * data.lineHeight;
      ctx.fillText(line, 0, y);
    });
  },
};

register('label', 'demo-multiline', multilineRenderer);
// #endregion renderer

export async function run(container: string | HTMLElement) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    // Labels are two lines and hang below nodes (labelPlacement: 'bottom');
    // the bottom padding reserves their height so they stay inside the view.
    autoFit: { padding: [24, 48, 64, 48] },
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: [
        { id: 'source', data: { label: 'Source Service\nShanghai' } },
        { id: 'gateway', data: { label: 'API Gateway\nPrimary' } },
        { id: 'target', data: { label: 'Target Store\nHangzhou' } },
      ],
      edges: [
        { source: 'source', target: 'gateway', data: { label: 'HTTPS\nrequest' } },
        { source: 'gateway', target: 'target', data: { label: 'RPC\nresponse' } },
      ],
    },
    layout: { type: 'dagre', rankdir: 'LR', nodeSize: 32, ranksep: 180 },
    behaviors: ['zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas', 'drag-node'],
    // #region node-label
    node: {
      labelRenderer: 'demo-multiline',
      style: {
        size: 32,
        label: (node) => String(node.data?.label ?? node.id),
        labelPlacement: 'bottom',
        labelFontSize: 12,
        labelBackground: 'rgba(255,255,255,0.92)',
        labelBackgroundPadding: 4,
      },
    },
    // #endregion node-label
    // #region edge-label
    edge: {
      type: 'arc',
      labelRenderer: 'demo-multiline',
      style: {
        label: (_source, _target, edge) => String(edge.data?.label ?? ''),
        labelFontSize: 10,
        labelBackground: 'rgba(255,255,255,0.9)',
        labelBackgroundPadding: 3,
        labelAutoRotate: true,
      },
    },
    // #endregion edge-label
  });
  await graph.render();
  return graph;
}
```


## Related documentation

- [Custom labels](/en/docs/guides/custom-label-renderer)
- [Drawing contracts](/en/docs/api/extensions#extension-drawing)

# Custom layout (/en/docs/examples/custom-layout)





Register a layout extension that places nodes in two rows.

## Try it

Inspect the two-row positions produced by the custom layout.

## Data

Six flow nodes are placed in two rows by the two-row layout.

## Complete runnable code

```ts
/**
 * Demo: register a layout extension that places nodes in two rows.
 */
import { Graph, register, type LayoutExtension } from '@antv/g6-lite';

const TWO_ROW_LAYOUT = 'two-row';

const twoRowLayout: LayoutExtension = {
  execute(data) {
    const columns = Math.ceil(data.nodes.length / 2);
    return {
      nodes: data.nodes.map((node, index) => ({
        ...node,
        x: 120 + (index % columns) * 150,
        y: 140 + Math.floor(index / columns) * 150,
      })),
    };
  },
};

register('layout', TWO_ROW_LAYOUT, () => ({ ...twoRowLayout }));

export async function run(container: string | HTMLElement) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    autoFit: true,
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: ['采集', '清洗', '特征', '训练', '评估', '发布'].map((label) => ({
        id: label,
        data: { label },
      })),
      edges: [
        { source: '采集', target: '清洗' },
        { source: '清洗', target: '特征' },
        { source: '特征', target: '训练' },
        { source: '训练', target: '评估' },
        { source: '评估', target: '发布' },
      ],
    },
    node: {
      type: 'rect',
      style: {
        fill: '#5AD8A6',
        width: 72,
        height: 36,
        borderRadius: 18,
        label: (node) => String(node.data?.label ?? node.id),
        labelPlacement: 'center',
      },
    },
    edge: { style: { endArrow: true, stroke: '#8C8C8C' } },
    layout: { type: TWO_ROW_LAYOUT },
    behaviors: ['zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas'],
  });
  await graph.render();
  return graph;
}
```
