# Common combo options (/en/docs/guides/combo)





Set combo appearance through `combo.style`. See the [Combo overview](/en/docs/elements/combo) for membership data and a complete example.

<span id="declare-combos" style="{ display: 'block', scrollMarginTop: '8rem' }" />

<span id="combodata" style="{ display: 'block', scrollMarginTop: '8rem' }" />

## ComboConfig [#comboconfig]

`ComboConfig` is the `combo` option in `new Graph()`. Set defaults in `style` and override fields for an individual combo in `data.combos[].style`.

<span id="basic-appearance-and-local-overrides" style="{ display: 'block', scrollMarginTop: '8rem' }" />

<span id="combo-style" style="{ display: 'block', scrollMarginTop: '8rem' }" />

<span id="style" style="{ display: 'block', scrollMarginTop: '8rem' }" />

## Combo styles [#combo-styles]

### Outline and padding [#basic-style-fields]

Set outline color and width with `stroke` and `strokeWidth`, and background color with `fill`. Use `padding` to adjust the space between the outline and its members. An array applies its largest value to all four sides.

### Label style [#padding-bounds-and-labels]

Set label text with `label` and its position with `labelPlacement`. Use `top` or `bottom` outside the outline, `inside` at the top-left inside it, or `center` in the middle. Set font size and color with `labelFontSize` and `labelColor`.

### Style by data [#callbacks-and-precedence]

Style functions receive the current combo. Read application data from `combo.data` or count direct members with `combo.childNodeIds.size`. Per-combo styles override global defaults, and state styles can override both.

<span id="options-combo-code-and-matching-result" style="{ display: 'block', scrollMarginTop: '8rem' }" />

The left combo uses the defaults. The middle combo overrides its outline with orange. The right combo uses a style function to display its member count. Open **Complete code** for the individual styles.



```ts
combo: { style: {
  fill: 'rgba(23,131,255,0.08)', stroke: '#1783FF', strokeWidth: 2,
  opacity: 1, borderRadius: 12, padding: 40,
  label: (combo) => String(combo.data?.name ?? combo.id),
  labelFontSize: 12, labelColor: '#1e3a8a', labelPlacement: 'top',
} },
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const groups = [{ id: 'global', x: 100 }, { id: 'local', x: 320 }, { id: 'callback', x: 540 }];
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: groups.flatMap(({ id, x }) => [
        { id: id + '-a', x, y: 100, comboId: id },
        { id: id + '-b', x, y: 160, comboId: id },
      ]),
      edges: [],
      combos: [
        { id: 'global', data: { name: 'Global' } },
        { id: 'local', data: { name: 'Local' }, style: {
          fill: 'rgba(246,144,61,0.15)', stroke: '#f6903d', strokeWidth: 3,
          opacity: 0.75, borderRadius: 0, padding: 32,
          labelFontSize: 14, labelColor: '#7c2d12', labelPlacement: 'inside',
        } },
        { id: 'callback', style: {
          fill: (combo) => combo.childNodeIds.size >= 2 ? 'rgba(135,59,244,0.12)' : 'transparent',
          stroke: '#873bf4', borderRadius: 20, padding: [8, 40, 12, 24],
          label: (combo) => 'Members: ' + combo.childNodeIds.size, labelPlacement: 'bottom',
        } },
      ],
    },
    node: { style: { size: 22 } },
    // #region combo-options
    combo: { style: {
      fill: 'rgba(23,131,255,0.08)', stroke: '#1783FF', strokeWidth: 2,
      opacity: 1, borderRadius: 12, padding: 40,
      label: (combo) => String(combo.data?.name ?? combo.id),
      labelFontSize: 12, labelColor: '#1e3a8a', labelPlacement: 'top',
    } },
    // #endregion combo-options
    behaviors: [],
    autoFit: { padding: 56, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}
```



See the [combo style reference](/en/docs/api/options#config-combo-style) for all fields, units, and defaults.

### State styles [#options-combo-state-styles]

Set the selected outline, fill, and other styles in `combo.style.stateStyles.selected`. An individual combo can set its own `style.stateStyles`. Click a combo in the example to toggle selection.



```ts
combo: { style: {
  padding: 28, label: (combo) => combo.id,
  stateStyles: {
    selected: { fill: 'rgba(135,59,244,0.12)', stroke: '#873bf4', strokeWidth: 3 },
    inactive: { opacity: 0.3 },
  },
} },
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const groups = [
    { id: 'Base', x: 100 }, { id: 'Selected', x: 270 },
    { id: 'Local', x: 440 }, { id: 'Inactive', x: 610 },
  ];
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: groups.flatMap(({ id, x }) => [
        { id: id + '-a', x, y: 100, comboId: id },
        { id: id + '-b', x, y: 160, comboId: id },
      ]),
      edges: [],
      combos: [
        { id: 'Base' },
        { id: 'Selected', states: ['selected'] },
        { id: 'Local', states: ['selected'], style: {
          stateStyles: { selected: { stroke: '#f6903d', labelColor: '#9a3412' } },
        } },
        { id: 'Inactive', states: ['selected', 'inactive'] },
      ],
    },
    node: { style: { size: 22 } },
    // #region state-styles
    combo: { style: {
      padding: 28, label: (combo) => combo.id,
      stateStyles: {
        selected: { fill: 'rgba(135,59,244,0.12)', stroke: '#873bf4', strokeWidth: 3 },
        inactive: { opacity: 0.3 },
      },
    } },
    // #endregion state-styles
    behaviors: [],
    autoFit: { padding: 56, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  graph.on('combo:click', ({ comboId }) => {
    const selected = graph.getComboData(comboId)?.states.has('selected') ?? false;
    graph.setItemState(comboId, 'selected', !selected);
  });
  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}
```



States apply in the order `active → highlight → selected → disabled → inactive`. The last state to set a field wins. See the [state style reference](/en/docs/api/options#config-combo-state-style) for supported overrides.

## Collapse and expand [#collapse-and-expand]

Set `collapsed: true` in the combo data to start collapsed. After rendering, use `collapseCombo()`, `expandCombo()`, or `toggleCombo()`. The example toggles when you click a combo.

```ts
graph.on('combo:click', ({ comboId }) => graph.toggleCombo(comboId));
```

### Collapsed shape and text [#collapsed-appearance]

Set the collapsed shape with `collapsedType` and its size with `collapsedSize`. The text comes from `label` first. When `label` is omitted, the text defaults to the number of descendant nodes. Use `count` to supply your own text.

| Shape                                                | Configuration                                                                   |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| <span id="combo-collapsed-circle" />Circle (default) | `collapsedType: 'circle'` and `collapsedSize: 64` draw a circle 64 units across |
| <span id="combo-collapsed-rect" />Rectangle          | `collapsedType: 'rect'` and `collapsedSize: [120, 48]` set the width and height |

From left to right, the combos show the node count, custom count text, and the combo name. Click a combo to see its expanded outline.



```ts
combos: [
  { id: 'circle', collapsed: true },
  { id: 'rect', collapsed: true, style: {
    collapsedType: 'rect', collapsedSize: [120, 48],
    count: (combo) => 'Items: ' + combo.childNodeIds.size,
  } },
  { id: 'label', collapsed: true, style: {
    collapsedType: 'rect', collapsedSize: [120, 48], label: 'Archive',
  } },
],
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const groups = [{ id: 'circle', x: 100 }, { id: 'rect', x: 300 }, { id: 'label', x: 500 }];
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: groups.flatMap(({ id, x }) => [
        { id: id + '-a', x: x - 24, y: 100, comboId: id },
        { id: id + '-b', x: x + 24, y: 160, comboId: id },
      ]),
      edges: [],
      // #region collapsed-shapes
      combos: [
        { id: 'circle', collapsed: true },
        { id: 'rect', collapsed: true, style: {
          collapsedType: 'rect', collapsedSize: [120, 48],
          count: (combo) => 'Items: ' + combo.childNodeIds.size,
        } },
        { id: 'label', collapsed: true, style: {
          collapsedType: 'rect', collapsedSize: [120, 48], label: 'Archive',
        } },
      ],
      // #endregion collapsed-shapes
    },
    node: { style: { size: 22 } },
    combo: { style: {
      stroke: '#1783ff', strokeWidth: 2, padding: 24,
      collapsedType: 'circle', collapsedSize: 64, count: true,
    } },
    behaviors: [],
    autoFit: { padding: 56, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  graph.on('combo:click', ({ comboId }) => graph.toggleCombo(comboId));
  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}
```



### Visibility in nested groups [#visibility-in-nested-groups]

Collapsing a parent hides its descendant nodes and their edges. Child combo outlines remain visible. Expanding keeps any existing hidden states on nodes and edges.

## Change membership [#change-membership]

Call `addToCombo(nodeId, comboId)` to move a node into a different combo. The combo outline recalculates. When you click Mobile in the example, `updateNodePosition()` also moves it next to its new group.



```ts
graph.on('node:click', ({ nodeId }) => {
  if (nodeId !== 'mobile') return;
  const target = graph.getNodeCombo(nodeId) === 'client' ? 'service' : 'client';
  graph.addToCombo(nodeId, target);
  // Membership changes do not move nodes; position this example explicitly.
  graph.updateNodePosition(nodeId, target === 'client' ? 200 : 380, 180);
});
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: [
        { id: 'web', x: 120, y: 100, comboId: 'client' },
        { id: 'mobile', x: 200, y: 180, comboId: 'client' },
        { id: 'api', x: 460, y: 100, comboId: 'service' },
      ],
      edges: [{ id: 'request', source: 'mobile', target: 'api' }],
      combos: [
        { id: 'client', style: { label: 'Client' } },
        { id: 'service', style: { label: 'Service', stroke: '#f6903d' } },
      ],
    },
    node: { style: {
      size: 24, label: (node) => node.id,
      fill: (node) => node.id === 'mobile' ? '#f6903d' : '#1783ff',
    } },
    combo: { style: { padding: 40, strokeWidth: 2 } },
    behaviors: ['drag-node', 'drag-canvas', 'zoom-canvas'],
    autoFit: { padding: 56, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  // #region change-membership
  graph.on('node:click', ({ nodeId }) => {
    if (nodeId !== 'mobile') return;
    const target = graph.getNodeCombo(nodeId) === 'client' ? 'service' : 'client';
    graph.addToCombo(nodeId, target);
    // Membership changes do not move nodes; position this example explicitly.
    graph.updateNodePosition(nodeId, target === 'client' ? 200 : 380, 180);
  });
  // #endregion change-membership
  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}
```



Use `removeFromCombo()` to ungroup a node. Use `createCombo()` to group existing nodes and `removeCombo()` to remove a combo while retaining its nodes. See the [combo methods](/en/docs/api/graph#graph-combo) for signatures.

## Drag groups [#drag-groups]

Enable `drag-node` to drag an entire combo. Drag the empty space inside a combo above to move its members together. To change membership, call `addToCombo()` or `removeFromCombo()`.

```ts
behaviors: ['drag-node', 'drag-canvas'],
```

## Update combo styles [#options-combo-runtime-updates]

To change one combo’s style, edit the data snapshot and apply it with `setData()`. This reruns the configured layout. Set `fitView: false` to retain the current view. Set global combo styles when you create the graph.

```ts
const data = graph.getData();
const combo = data.combos?.find(({ id }) => id === 'local');
if (combo) {
  combo.style = { ...combo.style, stroke: '#16a085' };
  await graph.setData(data, { fitView: false });
}
```

## Queries [#queries]

`getNodeCombo()` returns a node’s combo. `getComboChildren()` returns the direct members. `getComboData()` returns the read-only combo model.

```ts
const groupId = graph.getNodeCombo('mobile');
const members = graph.getComboChildren('client');
const collapsed = graph.getComboData('client')?.collapsed;
```

### ComboModel fields [#read-only-query-model]

| Field                           | Meaning                                       |
| ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `id`, `parentId`                | Combo ID and parent combo ID                  |
| `childNodeIds`, `childComboIds` | IDs of direct member nodes and child combos   |
| `collapsed`, `states`           | Collapsed flag and current element states     |
| `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`     | Center and dimensions of the expanded outline |
| `style`, `data`                 | Per-combo style and application data          |

### Bounds updates and data export [#bounds-updates-and-data-export]

Bounds are recalculated during rendering. `getData()` exports the current membership and collapsed state. For JSON export, save or recreate style functions separately.

## Common questions [#common-questions]

### Why is there no group outline or title? [#why-is-there-no-group-outline-or-title]

Members need a valid `comboId` and positions. Empty combos have no outline. Set a title with `label`.

### Why does content remain after hiding or collapsing a parent? [#why-does-content-remain-after-hiding-or-collapsing-a-parent]

`hidden` hides the combo itself. For collapse behavior, see [Visibility in nested groups](#visibility-in-nested-groups).

### Why do some nodes stay hidden after expanding? [#why-do-some-nodes-stay-hidden-after-expanding]

Check node and edge `hidden` states and whether an ancestor remains collapsed.

### Why does dragging not change membership or selection? [#why-does-dragging-not-change-membership-or-selection]

Dragging changes positions. Set membership through the [combo methods](/en/docs/api/graph#graph-combo) and selection through the [state methods](/en/docs/api/graph#graph-states).

### Why can updateOptions not change Combo appearance? [#why-can-updateoptions-not-change-combo-appearance]

Update the data to change a per-combo style. See [Update combo styles](#options-combo-runtime-updates).

<span id="options-combo-related-entries" style="{ display: 'block', scrollMarginTop: '8rem' }" />

## Related [#related]

* [Combo configuration reference](/en/docs/api/options#options-combo)
* [Complete combo example](/en/docs/examples/combo)


# Custom interactions (/en/docs/guides/custom-behavior)





When built-ins cannot express a business rule, consume public Graph events through a Behavior and update data or state through ExtensionContext. Here, clicking a node makes it uniquely active. Canvas clicks clear only active, preserving A's initial selected state.

## Public type pattern [#public-type-pattern]

Give the name a literal type and business options their own type, then use satisfies at activation. Full generics, event mappings, and lifecycle signatures are in the [Behavior contract](/en/docs/api/options#custom-interaction-contract).

## Recommended exports [#recommended-exports]

Export a stable name, options type, and explicit registration function. Register before creating Graph, and use a business or package prefix to avoid global registry collisions. Do not rely on import side effects for registration order.

## Complete implementation [#complete-implementation]

The code below drives the canvas. Every factory call creates a fresh closure. State updates remove only the state owned by this Behavior and append it to the target. click-select is omitted, so clicks do not alter selected.



```ts
import {
  Graph, register,
  type BehaviorExtension, type BehaviorOptions, type ElementState, type ExtensionContext,
} from '@antv/g6-lite';

export const BUSINESS_SELECT = 'docs-business-select' as const;
export interface BusinessSelectOptions extends BehaviorOptions<typeof BUSINESS_SELECT> {
  state?: ElementState;
}

export function createBusinessSelect(): BehaviorExtension<BusinessSelectOptions> {
  let context: ExtensionContext | undefined;
  let state: ElementState = 'active';
  const select = (nodeId?: string) => {
    if (!context || context.isDestroyed()) return;
    const next: Record<string, ElementState[]> = {};
    for (const id of context.data.getNodeIds()) {
      const retained = context.state.get(id).filter((value) => value !== state);
      next[id] = id === nodeId ? [...retained, state] : retained;
    }
    context.state.setAll(next);
  };
  return {
    init(nextContext, options) { context = nextContext; state = options.state ?? 'active'; },
    getEvents() {
      return {
        'node:click': ({ nodeId, nativeEvent }) => {
          if (nativeEvent.button === 0) select(nodeId);
        },
        'canvas:click': () => select(),
      };
    },
    destroy() { context = undefined; },
  };
}

// #region registration
export function registerBusinessSelect() {
  register('behavior', BUSINESS_SELECT, () => createBusinessSelect());
}
// #endregion registration

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  registerBusinessSelect();
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: [
        { id: 'A', x: 0, y: 0, states: ['selected'] },
        { id: 'B', x: 160, y: 0 }, { id: 'C', x: 320, y: 0 },
      ],
      edges: [{ source: 'A', target: 'B' }, { source: 'B', target: 'C' }],
    },
    node: {
      style: { size: 32, label: (node) => node.id, labelOffsetY: 8 },
      stateStyles: { active: { fill: '#F08F56', stroke: '#914C1D', strokeWidth: 2 } },
    },
    behaviors: [{ type: BUSINESS_SELECT, state: 'active' } satisfies BusinessSelectOptions],
    autoFit: { padding: 56, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  const status = document.createElement('div');
  status.style.cssText = 'position:absolute;left:12px;bottom:12px;z-index:20;background:white;color:#334155;padding:6px 10px;border-radius:6px;font:12px system-ui;';
  status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
  const updateStatus = () => {
    status.textContent = `active: ${graph.findNodesByState('active').join(', ') || 'none'} | selected: ${graph.findNodesByState('selected').join(', ') || 'none'}`;
  };
  const destroy = graph.destroy.bind(graph);
  graph.destroy = () => { status.remove(); destroy(); };
  try {
    await graph.render();
    graph.on('node:click', updateStatus);
    graph.on('canvas:click', updateStatus);
    updateStatus();
    container.append(status);
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}
```



## Register and activate [#register-and-activate]

The example calls registerBusinessSelect before constructing Graph and checks the configuration with satisfies BusinessSelectOptions. String names also activate the Behavior; normalized init options include type, and missing state defaults to active.

Multiple Graphs can reuse the registered factory; each mounted Behavior owns its context and state. Re-registering a name does not replace mounted instances. See [mounting and updates](/en/docs/api/options#mounting-and-updates).

## Event typing [#event-typing]

getEvents infers argument tuples from GraphEventMap. node:click has typed nodeId and nativeEvent; destroy has no arguments. Extend consumer event types by intersection:

```ts
import type { BehaviorExtension, BehaviorOptions, GraphEventMap } from '@antv/g6-lite';

interface BusinessEventMap {
  'business:reset': [payload: { source: 'toolbar' | 'shortcut' }];
}
type BusinessBehavior = BehaviorExtension<
  BehaviorOptions<'business-select'>,
  GraphEventMap & BusinessEventMap
>;
```

The application can call `graph.emit('business:reset', { source: 'toolbar' })` to invoke this handler. Augment `GraphEventMap` to check the payload at the call site. See the [custom event example](/en/docs/guides/events/custom).

## Lifecycle and cleanup [#lifecycle-and-cleanup]

The engine runs create → init → getEvents, then unbinds handlers and calls destroy on teardown. [`setBehaviors()`](/en/docs/api/graph#setbehaviors) and `updateOptions({ behaviors })` destroy the old behaviors and create those in the new list. A behavior with the same name still receives new options in the new instance’s init. Readonly options are a type constraint, with no guarantee of runtime freezing.

The engine cleans up getEvents bindings. Clean up your own window listeners, timers, observers, and DOM in destroy. Graph stays alive when behaviors switch, so use a behavior-local AbortController or teardown flag for asynchronous work and handle Promise rejections.

## Use a custom behavior in your project [#boundaries-and-replacement]

Use `context.state` to change element states and `context.data.updateNode()` or `updateEdge()` to change business data. Register the behavior under a distinct name, such as `docs-business-select`, to avoid overriding a built-in behavior. [Extension context API](/en/docs/api/extensions#extensioncontext) · [Registration rules](/en/docs/api/extensions#registration-rules)

In the example above, click B, then click empty canvas. B gains and then loses its `active` state. A stays `selected` throughout. The `select()` function in the full code shows how to change only the state owned by this behavior. [Try the example](#complete-implementation)

Continue with the [Behavior reference](/en/docs/api/options#options-behaviors), [interaction guide](/en/docs/guides/behaviors), or [Extension system](/en/docs/guides/extensions).

**Related runnable examples**

* [Register a custom interaction](/en/docs/examples/custom-behavior)


# Custom node decorations (/en/docs/guides/custom-decoration)





Use builtin-badge for existing counts, icons, and text badges. Register DecorationRenderer for custom content; the engine owns positioning, stacking, and overflow.

## Measure, draw, and register [#measure-draw-and-register]

measure returns full finite positive bounds. This example converts a fixed CSS font using DPR and caches calculations in layout.data. draw is centered on the decoration and explicitly sets fonts, colors, and alignment.



```ts
const pill: DecorationRenderer = {
  measure({ ctx, data, dpr, labelScale = dpr }) {
    const text = String(data ?? '');
    ctx.font = 12 * labelScale + 'px sans-serif';
    return { width: ctx.measureText(text).width + 12 * labelScale, height: 22 * labelScale, data: { text, unit: labelScale } };
  },
  draw({ ctx, layout }) {
    const value = layout.data as { text: string; unit: number } | undefined;
    if (!value) return;
    ctx.fillStyle = '#e6f4ff';
    ctx.fillRect(-layout.width / 2, -layout.height / 2, layout.width, layout.height);
    ctx.font = 12 * value.unit + 'px sans-serif';
    ctx.fillStyle = '#0958d9';
    ctx.textAlign = 'center'; ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';
    ctx.fillText(value.text, 0, 0);
  },
};
register('decoration', 'docs-pill', pill);
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph, register, type DecorationRenderer } from '@antv/g6-lite';

// #region renderer
const pill: DecorationRenderer = {
  measure({ ctx, data, dpr, labelScale = dpr }) {
    const text = String(data ?? '');
    ctx.font = 12 * labelScale + 'px sans-serif';
    return { width: ctx.measureText(text).width + 12 * labelScale, height: 22 * labelScale, data: { text, unit: labelScale } };
  },
  draw({ ctx, layout }) {
    const value = layout.data as { text: string; unit: number } | undefined;
    if (!value) return;
    ctx.fillStyle = '#e6f4ff';
    ctx.fillRect(-layout.width / 2, -layout.height / 2, layout.width, layout.height);
    ctx.font = 12 * value.unit + 'px sans-serif';
    ctx.fillStyle = '#0958d9';
    ctx.textAlign = 'center'; ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';
    ctx.fillText(value.text, 0, 0);
  },
};
register('decoration', 'docs-pill', pill);
// #endregion renderer

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: [{ id: 'A', x: 0, y: 0 }, { id: 'B', x: 260, y: 0 }],
      edges: [{ source: 'A', target: 'B' }],
    },
    node: {
      style: { size: 40, label: (node) => node.id, labelPlacement: 'center', labelColor: '#fff' },
      // #region placement
      decorations: [{
        renderer: 'docs-pill', placement: 'right', attachment: 'outside',
        layout: 'stack', sort: 'width-desc', itemGap: 4, maxVisible: 3,
        overflow: 'hover-expand', overflowData: (count: number) => '+' + count,
        items: (node) => node.id === 'A' ? ['CPU 42%', 'API', 'DB', 'Cache', 'Queue'] : ['Ready'],
        hideOnCollision: false,
      }],
      // #endregion placement
    },
    behaviors: ['zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas'],
    autoFit: { padding: 96, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  try { await graph.render(); return graph; }
  catch (error) { graph.destroy(); throw error; }
}
```



A has five items, B only Ready. A initially shows two items and +3. Hover its decoration region to expand all; leave to collapse. Expand full code for items and placement.

## Position and stack [#position-and-stack]

1. Match renderer to its registration. Use data for one item and items for a stack.
2. placement chooses the side; attachment chooses boundary or outside positioning.
3. layout: 'stack' enables vertical items; sort, maxVisible, and overflow control visibility. maxVisible includes the overflow item: 3 shows two items plus +3 here.
4. overflowData goes to the same renderer, which must also support that input.

Do not reimplement node positioning, sorting, or overflow inside the renderer. See [decoration configuration](/en/docs/api/options#config-node-decoration) for offsets, anchors, ratios, and defaults.

## Collisions and updates [#collisions-and-updates]

The example disables decoration collision hiding for comparison. In real data, choose by density; hideOnCollision: false can overlap and does not reserve decoration collision-grid space. minZoom is independent of label policy.

Update callback-driven items through public data methods, not shared renderer state. Input node dimensions are already in screen units. This example deliberately uses fixed CSS text and converts by dpr only. See [DecorationRenderer](/en/docs/api/extensions#decorationrenderer) for units.

## Common questions [#common-questions]

### Why is there no fallback text? [#why-is-there-no-fallback-text]

Unknown renderers, invalid measurements, and exceptions skip decoration content rather than using Label fallback. Check diagnostics, minZoom, hidden states, and collisions.

### Why did measurement not lead to drawing? [#why-did-measurement-not-lead-to-drawing]

Culling, collision, or overflow selection can skip draw. Keep measurement pure rather than treating invocation counts as business state.

### Can I use the built-in badge instead? [#can-i-use-the-built-in-badge-instead]

Yes; see [node badges](/en/docs/examples/decoration-badges). Reuse existing visuals before implementing a renderer.

**Related runnable examples**

* [Node badges](/en/docs/examples/decoration-badges)


# Custom edges (/en/docs/guides/custom-edge)





Use an `EdgeExtension` to reuse an edge type for a class of relationships. The `base` selects the path, arrows show direction, and `edge.style.label` supplies text. To vary width or color by data in one graph, use [style functions](/en/docs/guides/edge#options-edge-style-callbacks).

## Register and activate [#register-and-activate]

Choose `arc` as the base path, use `getStyle()` to set color and width by weight, and register the type with `register('edge', ...)`.



```ts
const weightedEdge: EdgeExtension = {
  base: 'arc',
  style: { curvature: 0.2, endArrow: true, hitAreaWidth: 14 },
  getStyle(_source, _target, edge) {
    const weight = Number(edge.data?.weight ?? 1);
    return { stroke: weight > 2 ? '#cf1322' : '#5366ad', lineWidth: weight + 1 };
  },
  stateStyles: { selected: { stroke: '#873bf4', lineWidth: 4 } },
};
register('edge', 'docs-weighted-edge', weightedEdge);
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph, register, type EdgeExtension } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import GUI from 'lil-gui';

// #region descriptor
const weightedEdge: EdgeExtension = {
  base: 'arc',
  style: { curvature: 0.2, endArrow: true, hitAreaWidth: 14 },
  getStyle(_source, _target, edge) {
    const weight = Number(edge.data?.weight ?? 1);
    return { stroke: weight > 2 ? '#cf1322' : '#5366ad', lineWidth: weight + 1 };
  },
  stateStyles: { selected: { stroke: '#873bf4', lineWidth: 4 } },
};
register('edge', 'docs-weighted-edge', weightedEdge);
// #endregion descriptor

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: [{ id: 'A', x: 0, y: 0 }, { id: 'B', x: 190, y: 80 }, { id: 'C', x: 380, y: 0 }],
      edges: [
        { id: 'light', source: 'A', target: 'B', data: { weight: 1 } },
        { id: 'heavy', source: 'B', target: 'C', data: { weight: 4 } },
      ],
    },
    node: { style: { size: 28, label: (node) => node.id } },
    // #region edge-activation
    edge: { type: 'docs-weighted-edge', style: { label: (_s, _t, edge) => edge.id ?? '' } },
    // #endregion edge-activation
    behaviors: ['click-select', 'zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas'],
    autoFit: { padding: 64, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  const ui = createDemoPanel(container);
  const destroy = graph.destroy.bind(graph);
  graph.destroy = () => { ui.destroy(); destroy(); };
  try {
    await graph.render();
    // #region edge-weight-update
    ui.addAction('Toggle heavy weight', () => {
      const weight = graph.getEdgeData('heavy')?.data?.weight === 4 ? 1 : 4;
      graph.updateEdgeData('heavy', { weight });
    });
    // #endregion edge-weight-update
    return graph;
  }
  catch (error) { graph.destroy(); throw error; }
}


export function createDemoPanel(container: string | HTMLElement, description = '') {
  const host = typeof container === 'string' ? document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(container)! : container;
  if (getComputedStyle(host).position === 'static') host.style.position = 'relative';

  let gui: GUI | undefined;
  const getGui = () => {
    if (!gui) {
      gui = new GUI({ container: host, width: 160 });
      gui.domElement.classList.add('g6lite-demo-controls');
      gui.domElement.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      Object.assign(gui.domElement.style, {
        position: 'absolute',
        top: '10px',
        right: '10px',
        zIndex: '30',
        maxWidth: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
        maxHeight: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
      });
    }
    return gui;
  };

  let status: HTMLDivElement | undefined;
  const setStatus = (message: string) => {
    if (!status) {
      status = document.createElement('div');
      status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
      status.dataset.role = 'status';
      status.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      status.style.cssText =
        'position:absolute;left:12px;bottom:10px;z-index:20;max-width:min(28rem,calc(100% - 24px));color:#64748b;font:12px/1.45 system-ui,sans-serif;pointer-events:none;white-space:pre-wrap;';
      host.append(status);
    }
    status.textContent = message;
  };
  if (description) setStatus(description);

  return {
    get gui() {
      return getGui();
    },
    addAction(label: string, action: () => void, folder = getGui()) {
      return folder.add({ [label]: action }, label);
    },
    addChoice<T extends string>(
      label: string,
      choices: readonly T[] | Record<string, T>,
      value: T,
      onChange: (value: T) => void,
    ) {
      const options = Array.isArray(choices) ? [...choices] : choices;
      return getGui().add({ value }, 'value', options).name(label).onChange(onChange);
    },
    setStatus,
    destroy() {
      gui?.destroy();
      status?.remove();
    },
  };
}
```



Set `edge.type` to the registered name in `new Graph()`. In this example, `light` starts with weight `1` and `heavy` with weight `4`.

## Common questions [#common-questions]

### Can I implement arbitrary drawing or shaders? [#can-i-implement-arbitrary-drawing-or-shaders]

EdgeExtension provides base, style, getStyle, and stateStyles, without arbitrary draw / shader hooks. See [EdgeExtension](/en/docs/api/extensions#edgeextension).

### Why is a label missing? [#why-is-a-label-missing]

Descriptor defaults do not replace label activation. This example explicitly provides edge.style.label; data or descriptor text alone does not guarantee label traversal.

### Why is an edge difficult to select? [#why-is-an-edge-difficult-to-select]

Set hitAreaWidth and enable interaction. The example uses 14 without increasing visual width; see [picking width](/en/docs/guides/edge#picking-width).

See [registration](/en/docs/api/graph#extension-registration) for caching and errors.


# Custom Label Renderer (/en/docs/guides/custom-label-renderer)





Use LabelRenderer for multiline, rich, or custom-truncated content; prefer [label configuration](/en/docs/guides/label) for ordinary text. One renderer below draws node names/cities and edge protocols/types.

## Register and activate [#register-and-activate]

1. measure sets its font and calculates full bounds including background padding; cache lines in layout.data.
2. draw explicitly sets fonts and colors and paints near the origin, without relying on Canvas state left by measure.
3. Register a label name, set node.labelRenderer / edge.labelRenderer, and provide nonempty label text.



```ts
const multilineRenderer: LabelRenderer<MultilineLayoutData> = {
  measure({ ctx, text, style }) {
    ctx.font = `${style.labelFontWeight} ${style.labelFontSize}px ${style.labelFontFamily}`;
    const lines = text.split('\n');
    const lineHeight = style.labelFontSize * 1.2;
    const contentWidth = Math.max(...lines.map((line) => ctx.measureText(line).width));
    const padding = style.labelBackgroundPadding;
    return {
      width: contentWidth + padding * 2,
      height: lines.length * lineHeight + padding * 2,
      data: { lines, lineHeight, contentWidth },
    };
  },
  draw({ ctx, style, layout }) {
    const data = layout.data;
    if (!data) return;
    if (style.labelBackground) {
      ctx.fillStyle = style.labelBackground;
      ctx.fillRect(-layout.width / 2, -layout.height / 2, layout.width, layout.height);
    }
    ctx.font = `${style.labelFontWeight} ${style.labelFontSize}px ${style.labelFontFamily}`;
    ctx.fillStyle = style.labelColor;
    ctx.textAlign = 'center';
    ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';
    data.lines.forEach((line, index) => {
      const y = (index - (data.lines.length - 1) / 2) * data.lineHeight;
      ctx.fillText(line, 0, y);
    });
  },
};

register('label', 'demo-multiline', multilineRenderer);
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
/**
 * Demo: unified custom node/edge LabelRenderer lifecycle.
 * The multiline behavior lives entirely in this demo, not in G6Lite core.
 */
import { Graph, register, type LabelRenderer } from '@antv/g6-lite';

interface MultilineLayoutData {
  lines: string[];
  lineHeight: number;
  contentWidth: number;
}

// #region renderer
const multilineRenderer: LabelRenderer<MultilineLayoutData> = {
  measure({ ctx, text, style }) {
    ctx.font = `${style.labelFontWeight} ${style.labelFontSize}px ${style.labelFontFamily}`;
    const lines = text.split('\n');
    const lineHeight = style.labelFontSize * 1.2;
    const contentWidth = Math.max(...lines.map((line) => ctx.measureText(line).width));
    const padding = style.labelBackgroundPadding;
    return {
      width: contentWidth + padding * 2,
      height: lines.length * lineHeight + padding * 2,
      data: { lines, lineHeight, contentWidth },
    };
  },
  draw({ ctx, style, layout }) {
    const data = layout.data;
    if (!data) return;
    if (style.labelBackground) {
      ctx.fillStyle = style.labelBackground;
      ctx.fillRect(-layout.width / 2, -layout.height / 2, layout.width, layout.height);
    }
    ctx.font = `${style.labelFontWeight} ${style.labelFontSize}px ${style.labelFontFamily}`;
    ctx.fillStyle = style.labelColor;
    ctx.textAlign = 'center';
    ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';
    data.lines.forEach((line, index) => {
      const y = (index - (data.lines.length - 1) / 2) * data.lineHeight;
      ctx.fillText(line, 0, y);
    });
  },
};

register('label', 'demo-multiline', multilineRenderer);
// #endregion renderer

export async function run(container: string | HTMLElement) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    // Labels are two lines and hang below nodes (labelPlacement: 'bottom');
    // the bottom padding reserves their height so they stay inside the view.
    autoFit: { padding: [24, 48, 64, 48] },
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: [
        { id: 'source', data: { label: 'Source Service\nShanghai' } },
        { id: 'gateway', data: { label: 'API Gateway\nPrimary' } },
        { id: 'target', data: { label: 'Target Store\nHangzhou' } },
      ],
      edges: [
        { source: 'source', target: 'gateway', data: { label: 'HTTPS\nrequest' } },
        { source: 'gateway', target: 'target', data: { label: 'RPC\nresponse' } },
      ],
    },
    layout: { type: 'dagre', rankdir: 'LR', nodeSize: 32, ranksep: 180 },
    behaviors: ['zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas', 'drag-node'],
    // #region node-label
    node: {
      labelRenderer: 'demo-multiline',
      style: {
        size: 32,
        label: (node) => String(node.data?.label ?? node.id),
        labelPlacement: 'bottom',
        labelFontSize: 12,
        labelBackground: 'rgba(255,255,255,0.92)',
        labelBackgroundPadding: 4,
      },
    },
    // #endregion node-label
    // #region edge-label
    edge: {
      type: 'arc',
      labelRenderer: 'demo-multiline',
      style: {
        label: (_source, _target, edge) => String(edge.data?.label ?? ''),
        labelFontSize: 10,
        labelBackground: 'rgba(255,255,255,0.9)',
        labelBackgroundPadding: 3,
        labelAutoRotate: true,
      },
    },
    // #endregion edge-label
  });
  await graph.render();
  return graph;
}
```



Drag nodes or zoom to inspect both lines and backgrounds. Expand the complete source for both activation configurations. The engine handles position, rotation, scale policy, and collisions.

## Protocol [#protocol]

Inputs include text, resolved style, ctx, dpr, and zoom. type='node' provides node; type='edge' provides edge / source / target. Narrow type before using category-specific fields. See [LabelRenderer](/en/docs/api/extensions#labelrenderer).

Font sizes, offsets, and padding in style already use backing-store pixels; do not multiply by DPR or zoom. The draw origin is the label center and edge rotation is already applied.

Return finite positive dimensions covering all content. layout.data caches only this measurement. Culling or collisions may skip drawing; measure should not change business state. Implement backgrounds and truncation yourself; labelMaxWidth does not automatically clip custom text.

## Common questions [#common-questions]

### Why was text skipped? [#why-was-text-skipped]

Check nonempty label, hidden states, low-zoom thresholds, and collisions before assuming failure. Temporarily disable policies for diagnosis, then restore useful density limits.

### What happens for invalid dimensions or drawing errors? [#what-happens-for-invalid-dimensions-or-drawing-errors]

The current label falls back to default single-line rendering with diagnostics. Do not return 0, NaN, or infinite dimensions. Decoration failures behave differently; see [drawing contracts](/en/docs/api/extensions#extension-drawing).

### Do edge labels always follow the rendered path? [#do-edge-labels-always-follow-the-rendered-path]

Current polyline / cubic positions and rotations use the endpoint chord and may not follow routed paths. See [edge labels](/en/docs/guides/edge#edge-labels).

See the complete [custom label example](/en/docs/examples/custom-label-renderer) and [registration](/en/docs/api/graph#extension-registration) for shared caching.

**Related runnable examples**

* [Custom label renderer](/en/docs/examples/custom-label-renderer)


# Custom layouts (/en/docs/guides/custom-layout)





Use a `LayoutExtension` to calculate node positions from graph data. This example arranges nodes in a row with equal spacing. See the [Layout overview](/en/docs/guides/layout-overview) for built-in layouts.

## Implement and execute [#implement-and-execute]

Read current data and runtime.options, retain node IDs/business fields, and return finite x/y. Reading options from runtime also supports standalone execution without init.



```ts
export function createColumnLayout(): LayoutExtension<ColumnOptions> {
  let context: ExtensionContext | undefined;
  return {
    init(next) { context = next; },
    async execute(data, { width, height, signal, options }) {
      const gap = Number(options.gap ?? 100);
      const nodes = [];
      for (const [index, node] of data.nodes.entries()) {
        await pause(signal, Number(options.delay ?? 0));
        if (signal?.aborted || context?.isDestroyed()) throw new DOMException('Canceled', 'AbortError');
        nodes.push({ ...node, x: width / 2 + (index - (data.nodes.length - 1) / 2) * gap, y: height / 2 });
      }
      return { nodes };
    },
    destroy() { context = undefined; },
  };
}
register('layout', 'docs-column', () => createColumnLayout());
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph, register, type ExtensionContext, type LayoutExtension } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import GUI from 'lil-gui';

interface ColumnOptions extends Record<string, unknown> { gap?: number; delay?: number }
function pause(signal: AbortSignal | undefined, delay: number) {
  return new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
    if (signal?.aborted) { reject(new DOMException('Canceled', 'AbortError')); return; }
    const abort = () => { clearTimeout(timer); reject(new DOMException('Canceled', 'AbortError')); };
    const timer = setTimeout(() => { signal?.removeEventListener('abort', abort); resolve(); }, delay);
    signal?.addEventListener('abort', abort, { once: true });
  });
}
// #region layout
export function createColumnLayout(): LayoutExtension<ColumnOptions> {
  let context: ExtensionContext | undefined;
  return {
    init(next) { context = next; },
    async execute(data, { width, height, signal, options }) {
      const gap = Number(options.gap ?? 100);
      const nodes = [];
      for (const [index, node] of data.nodes.entries()) {
        await pause(signal, Number(options.delay ?? 0));
        if (signal?.aborted || context?.isDestroyed()) throw new DOMException('Canceled', 'AbortError');
        nodes.push({ ...node, x: width / 2 + (index - (data.nodes.length - 1) / 2) * gap, y: height / 2 });
      }
      return { nodes };
    },
    destroy() { context = undefined; },
  };
}
register('layout', 'docs-column', () => createColumnLayout());
// #endregion layout

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: { nodes: ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E', 'F'].map((id) => ({ id })), edges: [] },
    layout: { type: 'docs-column', gap: 100 },
    node: { style: { size: 30, label: (node) => node.id } },
    behaviors: ['zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas'],
    autoFit: { padding: 56, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  let revision = 0;
  const ui = createDemoPanel(container);
  const status = document.createElement('div');
  status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
  status.style.cssText = 'position:absolute;bottom:12px;left:12px;font:12px system-ui;color:#334155;background:white;padding:4px;';
  const apply = async (mode: string) => {
    const request = ++revision;
    status.textContent = mode === 'slow' ? 'Running slow layout…' : 'Running…';
    if (mode === 'grid') graph.cancelLayout();
    graph.setLayout(mode === 'grid' ? { type: 'grid' } : { type: 'docs-column', gap: 100, delay: mode === 'slow' ? 180 : 0 });
    await graph.layout();
    if (graph.destroyed || request !== revision) return;
    graph.fitView({ padding: 56, maxZoom: 1 });
    status.textContent = mode === 'grid' ? 'Canceled old run; grid' : 'Column layout complete';
  };
  const destroy = graph.destroy.bind(graph);
  graph.destroy = () => { revision++; ui.destroy(); status.remove(); destroy(); };
  try {
    await graph.render();
    status.textContent = 'Column layout complete';
    for (const [mode, label] of [['column', 'Layout again'], ['slow', 'Slow layout'], ['grid', 'Cancel + grid']]) {
      ui.addAction(label, () => {
        void apply(mode).catch((error) => { if (!graph.destroyed) status.textContent = String(error); });
      });
    }
    container.append(status);
    return graph;
  }
  catch (error) { graph.destroy(); throw error; }
}


export function createDemoPanel(container: string | HTMLElement, description = '') {
  const host = typeof container === 'string' ? document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(container)! : container;
  if (getComputedStyle(host).position === 'static') host.style.position = 'relative';

  let gui: GUI | undefined;
  const getGui = () => {
    if (!gui) {
      gui = new GUI({ container: host, width: 160 });
      gui.domElement.classList.add('g6lite-demo-controls');
      gui.domElement.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      Object.assign(gui.domElement.style, {
        position: 'absolute',
        top: '10px',
        right: '10px',
        zIndex: '30',
        maxWidth: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
        maxHeight: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
      });
    }
    return gui;
  };

  let status: HTMLDivElement | undefined;
  const setStatus = (message: string) => {
    if (!status) {
      status = document.createElement('div');
      status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
      status.dataset.role = 'status';
      status.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      status.style.cssText =
        'position:absolute;left:12px;bottom:10px;z-index:20;max-width:min(28rem,calc(100% - 24px));color:#64748b;font:12px/1.45 system-ui,sans-serif;pointer-events:none;white-space:pre-wrap;';
      host.append(status);
    }
    status.textContent = message;
  };
  if (description) setStatus(description);

  return {
    get gui() {
      return getGui();
    },
    addAction(label: string, action: () => void, folder = getGui()) {
      return folder.add({ [label]: action }, label);
    },
    addChoice<T extends string>(
      label: string,
      choices: readonly T[] | Record<string, T>,
      value: T,
      onChange: (value: T) => void,
    ) {
      const options = Array.isArray(choices) ? [...choices] : choices;
      return getGui().add({ value }, 'value', options).name(label).onChange(onChange);
    },
    setStatus,
    destroy() {
      gui?.destroy();
      status?.remove();
    },
  };
}
```



Six nodes start in a row. Layout again recalculates. Start Slow layout and immediately choose Cancel + grid to invalidate the old run and restore a grid. Run the column layout again to verify recovery.

## Cancellation and resources [#cancellation-and-resources]

The wait helper clears its timer on abort and removes its listener on completion. Each step checks signal / isDestroyed. Chunk expensive work and yield so cancellation can run.

Graph calls destroy after success, failure, or cancellation. Cleanup must tolerate partial initialization. Layout fallback may absorb failures; fulfilled await alone does not prove application. The buttons use their own generation check before status updates and fitting.

## Graph versus standalone execution [#graph-versus-standalone-execution]

Graph.render / layout / setData use init → execute → destroy. Standalone runLayout skips init but still calls execute / destroy. This example reads options from runtime so both paths work.

```ts
import { runLayout, type GraphData } from '@antv/g6-lite';
export async function calculate(data: GraphData) {
  // Register docs-column above first. This calculates positions, without updating Graph.
  return runLayout(data, { type: 'docs-column', gap: 100 }, { width: 640, height: 320 });
}
```

See the [runLayout example](/en/docs/api/graph#graph-layout-runlayout) for displaying calculated results. Do not request rendering from execute; Graph applies results. context.data can be the old graph, not this execution's input.

## Common questions [#common-questions]

### Does worker: true move a custom layout to a Worker? [#does-worker-true-move-a-custom-layout-to-a-worker]

No. Registered extensions currently take the main-thread path. Own messages, cancellation, and cleanup if implementing your own Worker; see [Worker guidance](/en/docs/guides/layout-worker).

### Why can cancellation still fulfill the Promise? [#why-can-cancellation-still-fulfill-the-promise]

Cancellation invalidates old results rather than promising rejection. Keep an application generation check to prevent stale UI updates.

See [LayoutExtension](/en/docs/api/extensions#layoutextension) for runtime fields and fallback, and the [two-row example](/en/docs/examples/custom-layout).

**Related runnable examples**

* [Custom layout](/en/docs/examples/custom-layout)


# Custom nodes (/en/docs/guides/custom-node)





Use `NodeExtension` to package a reusable node appearance. You can also set colors and sizes directly in [node configuration](/en/docs/guides/node#options-node).

## Use cases [#use-cases]

1. Choose circle / rect to retain built-in rendering and picking.
2. Define default style and pure getStyle; register before first render.
3. Activate node.type and use public data methods for business updates.

## Overlays and boundary anchors [#overlays-and-boundary-anchors]

`drawOverlay()` draws the stripe on the left. `getBoundaryAnchor()` places the right badge a quarter of the node’s height above its center. Click **Toggle B status** to see the stripe and badge stay in place as B changes appearance.



```ts
drawOverlay(ctx, { x, y, zoom }) {
  ctx.save();
  ctx.fillStyle = '#5366ad';
  ctx.fillRect(x - 44 * zoom, y - 12 * zoom, 4 * zoom, 24 * zoom);
  ctx.restore();
},
getBoundaryAnchor({ placement, width, height, crossOffsetRatio }) {
  if (placement === 'right') return { x: width / 2, y: -height / 4 };
  if (placement === 'left') return { x: -width / 2, y: height * crossOffsetRatio };
  return { x: width * crossOffsetRatio, y: placement === 'top' ? -height / 2 : height / 2 };
},
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph, register, type NodeExtension } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import GUI from 'lil-gui';

// #region descriptor
const statusNode: NodeExtension = {
  base: 'rect',
  style: { size: 40, width: 100, height: 40, borderRadius: 6, strokeWidth: 2 },
  getStyle(node) {
    return node.data?.status === 'error'
      ? { fill: '#fff1f0', stroke: '#cf1322' }
      : { fill: '#e6f4ff', stroke: '#1677ff' };
  },
  // #region overlay-and-anchor
  drawOverlay(ctx, { x, y, zoom }) {
    ctx.save();
    ctx.fillStyle = '#5366ad';
    ctx.fillRect(x - 44 * zoom, y - 12 * zoom, 4 * zoom, 24 * zoom);
    ctx.restore();
  },
  getBoundaryAnchor({ placement, width, height, crossOffsetRatio }) {
    if (placement === 'right') return { x: width / 2, y: -height / 4 };
    if (placement === 'left') return { x: -width / 2, y: height * crossOffsetRatio };
    return { x: width * crossOffsetRatio, y: placement === 'top' ? -height / 2 : height / 2 };
  },
  // #endregion overlay-and-anchor
};
register('node', 'docs-status-node', statusNode);
// #endregion descriptor

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: [
        { id: 'A', x: 0, y: 0, data: { status: 'ok' } },
        { id: 'B', x: 240, y: 0, data: { status: 'error' } },
      ],
      edges: [{ id: 'A-B', source: 'A', target: 'B' }],
    },
    node: {
      type: 'docs-status-node',
      style: { label: (node) => node.id, labelPlacement: 'center', labelColor: '#1f2937' },
      stateStyles: { selected: { stroke: '#873bf4', strokeWidth: 4 } },
      decorations: [{ renderer: 'builtin-badge', placement: 'right', attachment: 'boundary', data: { kind: 'count', value: 3 } }],
    },
    edge: { style: { endArrow: true } },
    behaviors: ['click-select', 'zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas'],
    autoFit: { padding: 64, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  const ui = createDemoPanel(container);
  const destroy = graph.destroy.bind(graph);
  graph.destroy = () => { ui.destroy(); destroy(); };
  try {
    await graph.render();
    ui.addAction('Toggle B status', () => {
      const status = graph.getNodeData('B')?.data?.status === 'error' ? 'ok' : 'error';
      graph.updateNodeData('B', { status });
    });
    return graph;
  }
  catch (error) { graph.destroy(); throw error; }
}


export function createDemoPanel(container: string | HTMLElement, description = '') {
  const host = typeof container === 'string' ? document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(container)! : container;
  if (getComputedStyle(host).position === 'static') host.style.position = 'relative';

    if (!gui) {
      gui = new GUI({ container: host, width: 160 });
      gui.domElement.classList.add('g6lite-demo-controls');
      gui.domElement.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      Object.assign(gui.domElement.style, {
        position: 'absolute',
        top: '10px',
        right: '10px',
        zIndex: '30',
        maxWidth: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
        maxHeight: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
      });
    }
    return gui;
  };

  let status: HTMLDivElement | undefined;
  const setStatus = (message: string) => {
    if (!status) {
      status = document.createElement('div');
      status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
      status.dataset.role = 'status';
      status.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      status.style.cssText =
        'position:absolute;left:12px;bottom:10px;z-index:20;max-width:min(28rem,calc(100% - 24px));color:#64748b;font:12px/1.45 system-ui,sans-serif;pointer-events:none;white-space:pre-wrap;';
      host.append(status);
    }
    status.textContent = message;
  };
  if (description) setStatus(description);

  return {
    get gui() {
      return getGui();
    },
    addAction(label: string, action: () => void, folder = getGui()) {
      return folder.add({ [label]: action }, label);
    },
    addChoice<T extends string>(
      label: string,
      choices: readonly T[] | Record<string, T>,
      value: T,
      onChange: (value: T) => void,
    ) {
      const options = Array.isArray(choices) ? [...choices] : choices;
      return getGui().add({ value }, 'value', options).name(label).onChange(onChange);
    },
    setStatus,
    destroy() {
      gui?.destroy();
      status?.remove();
    },
  };
}
```



## Built-in extension [#built-in-extension]

Set `node.type` to `breathing-node` to add a pulse to active, selected, or highlighted nodes. Toggle selection or highlighting in the example and compare with the normal node on the right.



```ts
node: {
  type: 'breathing-node',
  style: {
    size: 36,
    fill: '#1677ff',
    stroke: '#fff',
    strokeWidth: 2,
    label: (node) => String(node.data?.label ?? node.id),
    labelPlacement: 'bottom',
    labelFontSize: 12,
  },
  stateStyles: {
    selected: { fill: '#1677ff', stroke: '#003eb3', strokeWidth: 3, haloWidth: 16 },
    highlight: { fill: '#2E8B57', stroke: '#1F6B43', strokeWidth: 3, haloWidth: 12 },
  },
},
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
/**
 * Breathing node demo.
 * Demonstrates the built-in breathing-node extension on selected/highlight states.
 */

import { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import GUI from 'lil-gui';

export async function run(container: string | HTMLElement) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    autoFit: true,
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: [
        { id: 'selected', x: 180, y: 180, data: { label: 'Selected' }, states: ['selected'] },
        { id: 'highlight', x: 360, y: 180, data: { label: 'Highlight' }, states: ['highlight'] },
        { id: 'normal', x: 540, y: 180, data: { label: 'Normal' } },
      ],
      edges: [
        { id: 'edge-selected-highlight', source: 'selected', target: 'highlight' },
        { id: 'edge-highlight-normal', source: 'highlight', target: 'normal' },
      ],
    },
    // #region breathing-options
    node: {
      type: 'breathing-node',
      style: {
        size: 36,
        fill: '#1677ff',
        stroke: '#fff',
        strokeWidth: 2,
        label: (node) => String(node.data?.label ?? node.id),
        labelPlacement: 'bottom',
        labelFontSize: 12,
      },
      stateStyles: {
        selected: { fill: '#1677ff', stroke: '#003eb3', strokeWidth: 3, haloWidth: 16 },
        highlight: { fill: '#2E8B57', stroke: '#1F6B43', strokeWidth: 3, haloWidth: 12 },
      },
    },
    // #endregion breathing-options
    edge: {
      style: {
        stroke: '#d1d5db',
        lineWidth: 2,
        endArrow: true,
      },
    },
    behaviors: ['zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas', 'drag-node', 'click-select'],
  });

  const ui = createDemoPanel(container, '切换选中和高亮，观察节点呼吸动画。');
  const destroy = graph.destroy.bind(graph);
  graph.destroy = () => {
    ui.destroy();
    destroy();
  };

  const toggleState = (state: 'selected' | 'highlight') => {
    const active = graph.getItemStates(state).includes(state);
    graph.setItemState(state, state, !active);
  };
  try {
    await graph.render();
    ui.addAction('切换选中', () => toggleState('selected'));
    ui.addAction('切换高亮', () => toggleState('highlight'));
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}
```
