## Common questions [#common-questions]

### Why did registration have no effect? [#why-did-registration-have-no-effect]

Check the name, node.type, registration order, and configured overrides. Descriptors are cached by name, not owned mutable state for each Graph.

### Why did the badge move without changing edge endpoints? [#why-did-the-badge-move-without-changing-edge-endpoints]

The anchor hook positions decorations. Arbitrary shapes and picking outlines are outside the current contract.

### Why does the animation redraw continuously? [#why-does-the-animation-redraw-continuously]

Check whether drawOverlay always returns true. Static content returns void / false; avoid continuous per-node drawing on large graphs.

See [custom nodes and explicit edge IDs](/en/docs/examples/custom-node-extension) and [registration](/en/docs/api/graph#extension-registration).

**Related runnable examples**

* [Breathing node](/en/docs/examples/breathing-node)
* [Custom nodes and explicit edge IDs](/en/docs/examples/custom-node-extension)


# Custom Plugins (/en/docs/guides/custom-plugin)





This example adds a click counter to the graph container. The count increases when you click a node or the button on the panel.

## Implement the plugin [#implement-register-and-mount]

Use a factory to create the plugin. Keep the count, panel, and unsubscribe callback inside the factory so each plugin instance has its own state.

| Method                   | What it does in the example                                                                                         |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `init(context, options)` | Reads options such as the caption.                                                                                  |
| `mount(container)`       | Adds the panel to the graph container and subscribes to node clicks.                                                |
| `destroy()`              | Unsubscribes from clicks and removes the panel. Also release any timers or other resources the plugin creates here. |

## Register and use the plugin [#register-and-use-the-plugin]

Register the factory with `register('plugin', 'docs-counter', createCounter)`, then add `{ type: 'docs-counter', caption: 'Clicks' }` to `plugins`. See the [plugin overview](/en/docs/guides/plugins#configure-a-plugin) for the graph configuration.

## Code example [#code-example]

Click a node or **Plugin +1** to increment the count. Click **Render again** to reset the count to zero. The next node click still increments it by one.



```ts
export function createCounter(): PluginExtension<CounterOptions> {
  let ui: ReturnType<typeof createDemoPanel> | undefined;
  let unsubscribe: (() => void) | undefined;
  let settings: CounterOptions | undefined;
  let count = 0;
  const report = () => ui?.setStatus(`${settings?.caption ?? 'Clicks'}: ${count}`);
  const increment = () => { count++; report(); };
  return {
    init(_context, options) { settings = options; },
    mount(container) {
      ui = createDemoPanel(container);
      ui.addAction('Plugin +1', increment);
      if (settings?.onRenderAgain) ui.addAction('Render again', settings.onRenderAgain);
      report();
      unsubscribe = settings?.subscribe?.(increment);
    },
    destroy() {
      unsubscribe?.(); unsubscribe = undefined;
      ui?.destroy();
      ui = undefined;
      settings = undefined;
    },
  };
}
register('plugin', NAME, () => createCounter());
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph, register, type PluginExtension, type PluginOptions } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import GUI from 'lil-gui';

const NAME = 'docs-counter' as const;
interface CounterOptions extends PluginOptions<typeof NAME> {
  caption?: string;
  subscribe?: (listener: () => void) => () => void;
  onRenderAgain?: () => void;
}
// #region plugin
export function createCounter(): PluginExtension<CounterOptions> {
  let ui: ReturnType<typeof createDemoPanel> | undefined;
  let unsubscribe: (() => void) | undefined;
  let settings: CounterOptions | undefined;
  let count = 0;
  const report = () => ui?.setStatus(`${settings?.caption ?? 'Clicks'}: ${count}`);
  const increment = () => { count++; report(); };
  return {
    init(_context, options) { settings = options; },
    mount(container) {
      ui = createDemoPanel(container);
      ui.addAction('Plugin +1', increment);
      if (settings?.onRenderAgain) ui.addAction('Render again', settings.onRenderAgain);
      report();
      unsubscribe = settings?.subscribe?.(increment);
    },
    destroy() {
      unsubscribe?.(); unsubscribe = undefined;
      ui?.destroy();
      ui = undefined;
      settings = undefined;
    },
  };
}
register('plugin', NAME, () => createCounter());
// #endregion plugin

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: { nodes: [{ id: 'A', x: 0, y: 0 }, { id: 'B', x: 200, y: 0 }], edges: [] },
    node: { style: { size: 32, label: (node) => node.id } },
    // #region activate
    plugins: [{
      type: NAME, caption: 'Clicks',
      subscribe(listener: () => void) {
        graph.on('node:click', listener);
        return () => graph.off('node:click', listener);
      },
      onRenderAgain() { void graph.render().catch(console.error); },
    } satisfies CounterOptions],
    // #endregion activate
    behaviors: ['zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas'],
    autoFit: { padding: 64, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  try { await graph.render(); return graph; }
  catch (error) { graph.destroy(); throw error; }
}


export function createDemoPanel(container: string | HTMLElement, description = '') {
  const host = typeof container === 'string' ? document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(container)! : container;
  if (getComputedStyle(host).position === 'static') host.style.position = 'relative';

  let gui: GUI | undefined;
  const getGui = () => {
    if (!gui) {
      gui = new GUI({ container: host, width: 160 });
      gui.domElement.classList.add('g6lite-demo-controls');
      gui.domElement.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      Object.assign(gui.domElement.style, {
        position: 'absolute',
        top: '10px',
        right: '10px',
        zIndex: '30',
        maxWidth: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
        maxHeight: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
      });
    }
    return gui;
  };

  let status: HTMLDivElement | undefined;
  const setStatus = (message: string) => {
    if (!status) {
      status = document.createElement('div');
      status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
      status.dataset.role = 'status';
      status.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      status.style.cssText =
        'position:absolute;left:12px;bottom:10px;z-index:20;max-width:min(28rem,calc(100% - 24px));color:#64748b;font:12px/1.45 system-ui,sans-serif;pointer-events:none;white-space:pre-wrap;';
      host.append(status);
    }
    status.textContent = message;
  };
  if (description) setStatus(description);

  return {
    get gui() {
      return getGui();
    },
    addAction(label: string, action: () => void, folder = getGui()) {
      return folder.add({ [label]: action }, label);
    },
    addChoice<T extends string>(
      label: string,
      choices: readonly T[] | Record<string, T>,
      value: T,
      onChange: (value: T) => void,
    ) {
      const options = Array.isArray(choices) ? [...choices] : choices;
      return getGui().add({ value }, 'value', options).name(label).onChange(onChange);
    },
    setStatus,
    destroy() {
      gui?.destroy();
      status?.remove();
    },
  };
}
```



Open the full code to see how the application provides a `subscribe` option. It calls `graph.on()` and returns a function that calls `graph.off()`. If a click counts more than once after remounting, check that `destroy()` calls the unsubscribe function.

See [PluginExtension](/en/docs/api/extensions#pluginextension) for the full contract.


# Data (/en/docs/guides/data)





## Overview [#overview]

A graph contains nodes, edges, and optional Combo groups. Map application objects to nodes and relationships to edges, then pass the data to `Graph`. Once the graph is rendered, replace the whole dataset or update the elements that changed.

## Data structure [#data-structure]

### Graph data (GraphData) [#nodes-edges-and-groups]

A, B, and C belong to the same Combo in this diagram. Each edge connects two nodes by ID.

<GraphDataModelDiagram locale="en" />

| Field    | Type                        | Required | Default   | Description                                                 |
| -------- | --------------------------- | -------- | --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `nodes`  | [`GraphNode[]`](#graphnode) | Yes      | —         | Node list. Pass `[]` to create an empty graph.              |
| `edges`  | [`GraphEdge[]`](#graphedge) | Yes      | —         | Edge list. Pass `[]` if the graph has no edges.             |
| `combos` | [`ComboData[]`](#combodata) | No       | No groups | Group list. Nodes reference these groups through `comboId`. |

<span id="positions-and-states" />

### Node data (GraphNode) [#graphnode]

| Field     | Type                                                       | Required | Default                          | Description                                                                                                                         |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`      | `string`                                                   | Yes      | —                                | Unique node ID. Edges use it to specify endpoints, and you can use it to query or update the node.                                  |
| `name`    | `string`                                                   | No       | —                                | Node name. Read and display it in a `node.style.label` callback.                                                                    |
| `data`    | [`NodeData`](/en/docs/api/options#config-node-data-fields) | No       | —                                | Application data such as `{ score: 80 }`. If supplied, `cluster` must be a string.                                                  |
| `x`       | `number`                                                   | No       | `0` without layout               | Horizontal graph coordinate. With a layout, the algorithm determines the final position. Use `fx` to fix the horizontal coordinate. |
| `y`       | `number`                                                   | No       | `0` without layout               | Vertical graph coordinate. With a layout, the algorithm determines the final position. Use `fy` to fix the vertical coordinate.     |
| `fx`      | `number`                                                   | No       | Horizontal coordinate is unfixed | Sets the node's horizontal coordinate after layout.                                                                                 |
| `fy`      | `number`                                                   | No       | Vertical coordinate is unfixed   | Sets the node's vertical coordinate after layout.                                                                                   |
| `comboId` | `string`                                                   | No       | No group membership              | ID of the containing Combo. It must reference a group declared in `combos`.                                                         |
| `states`  | `NodeState[]`                                              | No       | `[]`                             | Initial node states such as `['selected']`. Use `node.stateStyles` to configure their appearance.                                   |

### Edge data (GraphEdge) [#graphedge]

| Field    | Type          | Required | Default                 | Description                                                                                          |
| -------- | ------------- | -------- | ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`     | `string`      | No       | Generated automatically | Unique edge ID. Supply a stable ID to identify the same edge after replacing the dataset.            |
| `source` | `string`      | Yes      | —                       | Start node ID. It must reference a node in `nodes`.                                                  |
| `target` | `string`      | Yes      | —                       | End node ID. It must reference a node in `nodes`. Using the same ID as `source` creates a self-loop. |
| `data`   | `EdgeData`    | No       | —                       | Application data of type `Record<string, unknown>`, such as `{ weight: 2 }`.                         |
| `states` | `EdgeState[]` | No       | `[]`                    | Initial edge states such as `['selected']`. Use `edge.stateStyles` to configure their appearance.    |

### Group data (ComboData) [#combodata]

| Field       | Type                        | Required | Default                 | Description                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------- | --------------------------- | -------- | ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`        | `string`                    | Yes      | —                       | Unique group ID. Nodes reference it through `comboId` and child groups through `parentId`.                                                   |
| `parentId`  | `string`                    | No       | No parent group         | Parent group ID. It must reference a group in the same `combos` list. Parent links must be acyclic.                                          |
| `collapsed` | `boolean`                   | No       | `false`                 | Set to `true` to start collapsed and hide descendant nodes and their incident edges.                                                         |
| `style`     | `Partial<ComboStyleConfig>` | No       | Graph-level group style | Overrides specific style fields for this group, for example `{ fill: '#e6f4ff' }`. [Group style options](/en/docs/api/options#options-combo) |
| `data`      | `Record<string, unknown>`   | No       | —                       | Application data such as `{ department: 'engineering' }`.                                                                                    |
| `states`    | `ElementState[]`            | No       | `[]`                    | Initial group states such as `['selected']`. Use `combo.stateStyles` to configure their appearance.                                          |

## Data operations [#data-operations]

### Initialize data [#initialize-data]

Pass `data` to `new Graph()` and await the initial `render()` before calling data mutation methods. The `#container` element must be mounted and have a nonzero width and height.

```ts
import { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';

const graph = new Graph({
  container: '#container',
  data: {
    nodes: [{ id: 'A', x: 0, y: 0 }, { id: 'B', x: 120, y: 0 }],
    edges: [{ id: 'A-B', source: 'A', target: 'B' }],
  },
});

await graph.render();
```

### Choose an update path [#choose-an-update-path]

| Change                            | Method                            | What changes                                              |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Dataset switch / full response    | setData                           | Replaces data, runs configured layout, fits by default    |
| Small business-field changes      | updateNodeData / updateEdgeData   | Shallow-merges data without layout                        |
| Add/remove elements               | addNode(s) / addEdge(s) / remove… | Supply new positions; node removal removes adjacent edges |
| Position changes                  | updateNodePosition(s)             | Graph position changes; identity remains                  |
| Selection, visibility, membership | State / Combo methods             | Use the relevant APIs without full replacement            |

### Replace all data [#replace-all-data]

Pass a complete `GraphData` object to `setData()`. It runs the configured layout and fits the graph by default. Use `fitView: false` to keep the current zoom and pan.

```ts
await graph.setData(nextData, { fitView: false });
```

The incoming data defines the initial selection. To preserve selection, restore it for stable IDs still present in the new dataset. [Preserve selection](/en/docs/guides/states) · [Viewport example](/en/docs/guides/viewport)

### Incremental updates [#incremental-updates]

Continue with the graph from the initialization example. Add node C and edge B-C, then update their application data.

```ts
graph.addNode({ id: 'C', x: 240, y: 0 });
graph.addEdge({ id: 'B-C', source: 'B', target: 'C' });

graph.updateNodeData('C', { score: 80 });
graph.updateEdgeData('B-C', { weight: 2 });
```

Removing an edge keeps its endpoints. Removing a node also removes all its incident edges.

```ts
graph.removeEdge('B-C');
graph.removeNode('C');
```

In the example below, inspect A, change its score, or add and remove node D.



```ts
const update = () => graph.updateNodeData('A', {
  score: Number(graph.getNodeData('A')?.data?.score ?? 0) + 1,
});
const add = () => {
  if (graph.hasNode('D')) return;
  graph.addNode({ id: 'D', x: 360, y: 70 });
  graph.addEdge({ id: 'C-D', source: 'C', target: 'D' });
};
const remove = () => graph.removeNode('D'); // Also removes C-D.
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import GUI from 'lil-gui';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: [
        { id: 'A', x: 0, y: 0, data: { score: 1 } },
        { id: 'B', x: 200, y: -50 }, { id: 'C', x: 200, y: 70 },
      ],
      edges: [{ id: 'A-B', source: 'A', target: 'B' }, { id: 'A-C', source: 'A', target: 'C' }],
    },
    node: { style: {
      size: (node) => node.id === 'A' ? 28 + Number(node.data?.score ?? 1) * 2 : 28,
      label: (node) => node.id === 'A' ? `A: ${node.data?.score}` : node.id, labelOffsetY: 10,
    } },
    behaviors: ['zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas'],
    autoFit: { padding: [76, 48, 120, 48], maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  // #region query
  const inspect = () => ({
    node: graph.getNodeData('A'),
    neighbors: graph.getNeighborNodes('A'),
    edges: graph.getAdjacentEdges('A'),
    snapshot: graph.getData(),
  });
  // #endregion query
  // #region mutation
  const update = () => graph.updateNodeData('A', {
    score: Number(graph.getNodeData('A')?.data?.score ?? 0) + 1,
  });
  const add = () => {
    if (graph.hasNode('D')) return;
    graph.addNode({ id: 'D', x: 360, y: 70 });
    graph.addEdge({ id: 'C-D', source: 'C', target: 'D' });
  };
  const remove = () => graph.removeNode('D'); // Also removes C-D.
  // #endregion mutation
  const ui = createDemoPanel(container);
  const status = document.createElement('div');
  status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
  status.style.cssText = 'position:absolute;left:12px;bottom:12px;right:12px;padding:8px;background:white;color:#334155;font:12px/1.5 system-ui;white-space:pre-line;pointer-events:none;z-index:20;';
  let last = 'Ready';
  const report = () => {
    const result = inspect();
    status.textContent = [
      `${last} | nodes=${graph.getNodeCount()}, edges=${graph.getEdgeCount()}`,
      `A score=${result.node?.data?.score} | neighbors=${result.neighbors.join(', ')}`,
      `adjacent=${result.edges.map((edge) => edge.id).join(', ')}`,
    ].join('\n');
  };
  const copy = () => {
    const snapshot = graph.getData();
    snapshot.nodes[0].data = { ...snapshot.nodes[0].data, score: 999 };
    last = `snapshot score=999; graph score=${graph.getNodeData('A')?.data?.score}`;
  };
  const actions: Array<[string, () => void]> = [
    ['Inspect A', () => { last = 'Inspected'; }], ['Edit snapshot', copy],
    ['Update A', () => { update(); last = 'Updated A'; }],
    ['Add D', () => { add(); last = 'Added D'; }],
    ['Remove D', () => { remove(); last = 'Removed D'; }],
  ];
  const destroy = graph.destroy.bind(graph);
  graph.destroy = () => {
    ui.destroy(); status.remove(); destroy();
  };
  try {
    await graph.render();
    if (graph.destroyed) return graph;
    for (const [label, action] of actions) {
      ui.addAction(label, () => { action(); report(); });
    }
    container.append(status); report(); return graph;
  } catch (error) { graph.destroy(); throw error; }
}


export function createDemoPanel(container: string | HTMLElement, description = '') {
  const host = typeof container === 'string' ? document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(container)! : container;
  if (getComputedStyle(host).position === 'static') host.style.position = 'relative';

  let gui: GUI | undefined;
  const getGui = () => {
    if (!gui) {
      gui = new GUI({ container: host, width: 160 });
      gui.domElement.classList.add('g6lite-demo-controls');
      gui.domElement.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      Object.assign(gui.domElement.style, {
        position: 'absolute',
        top: '10px',
        right: '10px',
        zIndex: '30',
        maxWidth: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
        maxHeight: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
      });
    }
    return gui;
  };

  let status: HTMLDivElement | undefined;
  const setStatus = (message: string) => {
    if (!status) {
      status = document.createElement('div');
      status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
      status.dataset.role = 'status';
      status.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      status.style.cssText =
        'position:absolute;left:12px;bottom:10px;z-index:20;max-width:min(28rem,calc(100% - 24px));color:#64748b;font:12px/1.45 system-ui,sans-serif;pointer-events:none;white-space:pre-wrap;';
      host.append(status);
    }
    status.textContent = message;
  };
  if (description) setStatus(description);

  return {
    get gui() {
      return getGui();
    },
    addAction(label: string, action: () => void, folder = getGui()) {
      return folder.add({ [label]: action }, label);
    },
    addChoice<T extends string>(
      label: string,
      choices: readonly T[] | Record<string, T>,
      value: T,
      onChange: (value: T) => void,
    ) {
      const options = Array.isArray(choices) ? [...choices] : choices;
      return getGui().add({ value }, 'value', options).name(label).onChange(onChange);
    },
    setStatus,
    destroy() {
      gui?.destroy();
      status?.remove();
    },
  };
}
```



Incremental methods schedule a redraw. Use batch methods for multiple elements. Application data is shallow-merged by top-level key, so a nested object is replaced as a whole.

### Query data [#query-data]

Use `getNodes()` and `getEdges()` for lists, or `getNodeData(id)` and `getEdgeData(id)` to look up one element by ID.

```ts
const nodes = graph.getNodes();
const edges = graph.getEdges();
const node = graph.getNodeData('B');
const edge = graph.getEdgeData('A-B');
```

#### Input, models, and snapshots [#input-models-and-snapshots]

| Form             | Purpose                                   | Updating it                                          |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| GraphData input  | Declare nodes, edges, and Combos          | Pass to new Graph / setData                          |
| Query models     | Read the working graph; states is a set   | Use Graph mutation APIs                              |
| getData snapshot | Export positions, memberships, and states | Explicitly setData; nested objects can remain shared |

Stable IDs represent business identity; array order and coordinates do not. Equal endpoints can have distinct edge IDs. Supply stable edge IDs to preserve selection across refreshes.

Models are Graph-owned live views. Query again after replacing or removing data. Before the first render, queries return their respective empty values, while `getData()` returns a snapshot of the constructor data. Queries may still return values after destruction. Check [destroyed](/en/docs/api/graph#graph-lifecycle-destroyed) for the instance state.

After rendering, `getData()` exports the current positions, actual edge IDs, memberships, and states. The snapshot omits collapse-derived `hidden`. Save fixed axes `fx` and `fy` and layout options separately.

##### Query return types [#model-fields]

| Return type                                               | Fields                                                  |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `NodeModel`                                               | `id`, `name?`, `x`, `y`, `data?`, `states`              |
| `EdgeModel`                                               | `id`, `source`, `target`, `data?`, `states`             |
| [ComboModel](/en/docs/guides/combo#read-only-query-model) | Group position, size, members, collapse state, and more |
| `ElementModel`                                            | `NodeModel \| EdgeModel \| ComboModel`                  |

Fields are read-only. A `?` marks an optional field. Node `x` and `y` use graph coordinates, `data` is a `Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>`, and `states` is a `ReadonlySet<ElementState>`.

```ts
const element = graph.getElementData('A-B');
if (element && 'source' in element) {
  console.log(element.source, element.target);
}
const selected = graph.getNodeData('A')?.states.has('selected');
```

### Complex data structures [#complex-data-structures]

**Nested groups.** In initial data, use `parentId` for the parent group and `comboId` for each node's membership. At runtime, you can create groups, move existing nodes, and change the collapsed state. The example adds the existing B node to Storage and then collapses Storage.

```ts
graph.createCombo({ id: 'platform' });
graph.createCombo({ id: 'storage', parentId: 'platform' }, ['B']);
graph.collapseCombo('storage');
```

**Trees.** Flatten the tree into `nodes` and `edges`. Each edge points from parent to child, for example `{ source: 'root', target: 'child' }`. Pass the result to a tree layout such as `mindmap` or `indented`. [Combo guide](/en/docs/guides/combo) · [Tree layout examples](/en/docs/api/options#config-tree-layout-fields)

<span id="map-application-data" />

<span id="validate-data" />

## Load remote data [#load-remote-data]

If the endpoint returns a complete dataset, render an empty graph first, then load the JSON. The example assumes the endpoint returns valid `GraphData`. If it returns application records, map them to graph data and validate IDs, edge endpoints, and group membership before applying them.

```ts
import { Graph, type GraphData } from '@antv/g6-lite';

const graph = new Graph({
  container: '#container',
  data: { nodes: [], edges: [] },
  layout: { type: 'grid' },
});
await graph.render();

const response = await fetch('/data/graph.json');
if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${response.status}`);

const data: GraphData = await response.json();
if (!graph.destroyed) await graph.setData(data);
```

### Cancel stale requests and clean up [#cancel-stale-requests-and-clean-up]

The helper below owns cleanup of this page’s Graph. load accepts an AbortSignal. Handle refresh failures in the caller, and call dispose on exit.

```ts
import type { Graph, GraphData } from '@antv/g6-lite';
export function createLoader(graph: Graph, load: (signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<GraphData>) {
  let version = 0;
  let disposed = false;
  let controller: AbortController | undefined;
  return {
    async refresh() {
      const request = ++version;
      controller?.abort();
      const current = new AbortController();
      controller = current;
      try {
        const next = await load(current.signal);
        if (disposed || graph.destroyed || request !== version) return;
        await graph.setData(next, { fitView: false });
      } catch (error) {
        if (!current.signal.aborted && !disposed) throw error;
      }
    },
    dispose() {
      disposed = true;
      version++;
      controller?.abort();
      graph.destroy();
    },
  };
}
```

## Common questions [#common-questions]

### Why did editing exported data not update the graph? [#why-did-editing-exported-data-not-update-the-graph]

getData does not write back automatically. Use incremental methods for small changes, or explicitly setData for replacement and choose the view policy.

### Why does an old index identify another element after removal? [#why-does-an-old-index-identify-another-element-after-removal]

Array order can change. Query by ID and match nodes and edges separately; do not use saved indices as identity.

<span id="data-and-appearance" />

### Why did labels or colors not change? [#why-did-labels-or-colors-not-change]

Check that fields are inside data and read by the style function. Editing exports or directly mutating models does not follow the public update flow.

### Why did refreshing lose the view or selection? [#why-did-refreshing-lose-the-view-or-selection]

setData fits by default and builds states from new input. fitView: false keeps the camera; preserve selection explicitly by stable IDs.


# Common edge options (/en/docs/guides/edge)





Use `GraphOptions.edge` to choose a path and configure the line, arrows, and labels. See [Edge overview](/en/docs/elements/edge) for endpoints, direction, and edge data.

<span id="basic-configuration" style="{ display: 'block', scrollMarginTop: '8rem' }" />

## EdgeConfig [#edgeconfig]

`EdgeConfig` is the `edge` option passed to `new Graph()`. This example draws a blue line with a target arrow and uses purple when the edge is selected.

```ts
import { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';

const graph = new Graph({
  container: '#container',
  data: {
    nodes: [{ id: 'a', x: 80, y: 100 }, { id: 'b', x: 260, y: 100 }],
    edges: [{ id: 'a-b', source: 'a', target: 'b' }],
  },
  edge: {
    type: 'line',
    style: { stroke: '#1783FF', lineWidth: 2, endArrow: true },
    stateStyles: { selected: { stroke: '#7C3AED', lineWidth: 4 } },
  },
  behaviors: ['click-select'],
});

await graph.render();
```

| Property                                  | Description                                       | Type                                                 | Default                         | Required |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | -------- |
| [`type`](#types)                          | Built-in edge type or registered custom edge name | `string`                                             | `'line'`                        | No       |
| [`style`](#style-fields)                  | Line, path parameters, arrows, and labels         | `EdgeConfig['style']`                                | Theme and built-in styles       | No       |
| [`stateStyles`](#state-styles)            | Appearance overrides by state                     | `Partial<Record<EdgeState, EdgeStateStyleOverride>>` | Extension or theme state styles | No       |
| [`parallelEdges`](#parallel-edge-spacing) | Separate edges with the same endpoints            | `boolean \| ParallelEdgesConfig`                     | Disabled                        | No       |
| [`labelRenderer`](#edge-label-renderer)   | Registered label renderer                         | `string`                                             | Built-in label renderer         | No       |

## Specify the edge type [#types]

Set `edge.type` to specify the edge type. The default is `line`. This example uses `polyline` for all edges in the graph.

```ts
const graph = new Graph({
  container,
  data,
  edge: { type: 'polyline' },
});
```

| Type value | Name                        | Use                                                                    |
| ---------- | --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `line`     | [Straight line](#edge-line) | Connect endpoints directly                                             |
| `arc`      | [Arc](#edge-arc)            | Control the bend or separate edges with the same endpoints             |
| `cubic`    | [Cubic Bézier](#edge-cubic) | Connect horizontal levels with a smooth curve                          |
| `polyline` | [Polyline](#edge-polyline)  | Route connections in flowcharts, directory trees, or fishbone diagrams |

[Register a custom edge](/en/docs/guides/custom-edge) before using its name as `edge.type`.

### Line edges [#edge-line]

`line` connects the endpoints directly. Set `endArrow: true` to draw an arrow at the target.

```ts
const edge = { type: 'line', style: { lineWidth: 2, endArrow: true } };
```

### Arcs and cubic curves [#arcs-and-cubic-curves]

#### Arc edges [#edge-arc]

Use `curvature` to control which way and how far the arc bends. Compare `-0.35`, `0`, and `0.35` below.



```ts
import { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const rows = [
    { id: 'curvature -0.35', y: 60, curvature: -0.35 },
    { id: 'curvature 0', y: 150, curvature: 0 },
    { id: 'curvature 0.35', y: 240, curvature: 0.35 },
  ];
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: rows.flatMap((row) => [
        { id: row.id + '-s', x: 100, y: row.y, data: { label: row.id } },
        { id: row.id + '-t', x: 440, y: row.y },
      ]),
      edges: rows.map((row) => ({ id: row.id, source: row.id + '-s', target: row.id + '-t', data: row })),
    },
    node: { style: { size: 20, label: (node) => String(node.data?.label ?? '') } },
    edge: {
      type: 'arc',
      style: { curvature: (_s, _t, edge) => Number(edge.data?.curvature ?? 0), lineWidth: 2, hitAreaWidth: 12 },
      stateStyles: { selected: { stroke: '#873bf4' } },
    },
    behaviors: ['click-select'],
    autoFit: { padding: 48, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}
```



#### Cubic edges [#edge-cubic]

`curveOffset` sets the horizontal handles of a cubic edge. Compare `30` and `120` below. The path may remain straight when the endpoints share a height.



```ts
import { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const rows = [{ id: 'offset 30', y: 40, offset: 30 }, { id: 'offset 120', y: 180, offset: 120 }];
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: rows.flatMap((row) => [
        { id: row.id + '-s', x: 100, y: row.y, data: { label: row.id } },
        { id: row.id + '-t', x: 440, y: row.y + 80 },
      ]),
      edges: rows.map((row) => ({ id: row.id, source: row.id + '-s', target: row.id + '-t', data: row })),
    },
    node: { type: 'rect', style: { width: 70, height: 28, label: (node) => String(node.data?.label ?? '') } },
    edge: {
      type: 'cubic',
      style: { curveOffset: (_s, _t, edge) => Number(edge.data?.offset ?? 60), lineWidth: 2, hitAreaWidth: 12 },
      stateStyles: { selected: { stroke: '#873bf4' } },
    },
    behaviors: ['click-select'],
    autoFit: { padding: 48, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}
```



<span id="basic-styles" style="{ display: 'block', scrollMarginTop: '8rem' }" />

<span id="edge-style-fields" style="{ display: 'block', scrollMarginTop: '8rem' }" />

## Style [#style-fields]

### Edge path styles [#edge-path-styles]

Line styles control an edge’s color, width, opacity, and direction.

| Field          | Type                       | Default or fallback                                     | Meaning                                                                                                               |
| -------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `stroke`       | `EdgeStyleValue<string>`   | `theme.edgeStroke`; light `'#99ADD1'`, dark `'#637088'` | Edge and arrow color                                                                                                  |
| `lineWidth`    | `EdgeStyleValue<number>`   | `theme.edgeLineWidth`, preset `1`                       | Visual width; use a finite positive value                                                                             |
| `opacity`      | `EdgeStyleValue<number>`   | `1`                                                     | Opacity from `0` to `1`                                                                                               |
| `lineDash`     | `EdgeStyleValue<number[]>` | `[]`                                                    | Empty means solid; the current period uses the sum of the first two values, as described in [Dash rules](#dash-rules) |
| `startArrow`   | `EdgeStyleValue<boolean>`  | `false`                                                 | Source-end arrow pointing toward `source`                                                                             |
| `endArrow`     | `EdgeStyleValue<boolean>`  | `theme.edgeArrow`, `true` in both light and dark        | Target-end arrow pointing toward `target`                                                                             |
| `arrowSize`    | `EdgeStyleValue<number>`   | Derived from line width                                 | Length along the path; use a finite positive explicit length. Nonpositive values use automatic length                 |
| `hitAreaWidth` | `EdgeStyleValue<number>`   | Final `lineWidth`                                       | Total picking width, independent of visual width; see [Picking width](#picking-width)                                 |

Line width, hit width, arrow length, and dash periods stay fixed in screen-rendering pixels as the graph zooms.

### Style functions [#options-edge-style-callbacks]

Style functions receive `(source, target, edge)` and use each edge’s data to set its appearance. The preview maps `edge.data` to thin solid, dashed, and bidirectional edges.



```ts
edge: {
  type: 'line',
  style: {
    stroke: (_source, _target, edge) => String(edge.data?.color ?? '#99ADD1'),
    lineWidth: (_source, _target, edge) => Number(edge.data?.width ?? 1),
    lineDash: (_source, _target, edge) => (edge.data?.dash as number[]) ?? [],
    opacity: (_source, _target, edge) => Number(edge.data?.opacity ?? 1),
    startArrow: (_source, _target, edge) => edge.data?.start === true,
    endArrow: (_source, _target, edge) => edge.data?.end === true,
    arrowSize: 16,
    hitAreaWidth: 14,
  },
  stateStyles: { selected: { stroke: '#873bf4', lineWidth: 6 } },
},
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const rows = [
    { id: 'Plain', y: 60, width: 1.5, color: '#64748b', dash: [], start: false, end: false, opacity: 1 },
    { id: 'Dash', y: 150, width: 3, color: '#f6903d', dash: [8, 8], start: false, end: true, opacity: 0.7 },
    { id: 'Both', y: 240, width: 5, color: '#1783FF', dash: [], start: true, end: true, opacity: 1 },
  ];
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: rows.flatMap((row) => [
        { id: `${row.id}-source`, x: 100, y: row.y, data: { label: row.id } },
        { id: `${row.id}-target`, x: 440, y: row.y },
      ]),
      edges: rows.map((row) => ({
        id: row.id, source: `${row.id}-source`, target: `${row.id}-target`, data: row,
      })),
    },
    node: { style: { size: 20, label: (node) => String(node.data?.label ?? '') } },
    // #region edge-options
    edge: {
      type: 'line',
      style: {
        stroke: (_source, _target, edge) => String(edge.data?.color ?? '#99ADD1'),
        lineWidth: (_source, _target, edge) => Number(edge.data?.width ?? 1),
        lineDash: (_source, _target, edge) => (edge.data?.dash as number[]) ?? [],
        opacity: (_source, _target, edge) => Number(edge.data?.opacity ?? 1),
        startArrow: (_source, _target, edge) => edge.data?.start === true,
        endArrow: (_source, _target, edge) => edge.data?.end === true,
        arrowSize: 16,
        hitAreaWidth: 14,
      },
      stateStyles: { selected: { stroke: '#873bf4', lineWidth: 6 } },
    },
    // #endregion edge-options
    behaviors: ['click-select'],
    autoFit: { padding: 48, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}
```



### Dash rules [#dash-rules]

Use `lineDash` to draw a dashed edge. Its first two values add up to the dash period. This example uses a `lineWidth` of `3` to compare a solid line and two dash spacings.



```ts
const rows = [
  { id: 'Solid', y: 0, dash: [] },
  { id: 'Short dashes', y: 75, dash: [4, 4] },
  { id: 'Long dashes', y: 150, dash: [8, 8] },
];
const edge: EdgeConfig = {
  type: 'line',
  style: {
    lineWidth: 3,
    endArrow: false,
    lineDash: (_source, _target, edge) => (edge.data?.dash as number[] | undefined) ?? [],
  },
};
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph, type EdgeConfig } from '@antv/g6-lite';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  // #region dash-options
  const rows = [
    { id: 'Solid', y: 0, dash: [] },
    { id: 'Short dashes', y: 75, dash: [4, 4] },
    { id: 'Long dashes', y: 150, dash: [8, 8] },
  ];
  const edge: EdgeConfig = {
    type: 'line',
    style: {
      lineWidth: 3,
      endArrow: false,
      lineDash: (_source, _target, edge) => (edge.data?.dash as number[] | undefined) ?? [],
    },
  };
  // #endregion dash-options
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: rows.flatMap(({ id, y }) => [
        { id: id + '-source', x: 0, y },
        { id: id + '-target', x: 320, y },
      ]),
      edges: rows.map(({ id, dash }) => ({
        id,
        source: id + '-source',
        target: id + '-target',
        data: { dash },
      })),
    },
    node: { style: { size: 16 } },
    edge: {
      ...edge,
      style: { ...edge.style, label: (_source, _target, edge) => edge.id ?? '', labelFontSize: 12 },
    },
    autoFit: { padding: 48, maxZoom: 1 },
    behaviors: [],
  });
  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}
```





### Arrows [#arrows]

Use `startArrow` and `endArrow` to control arrows at both ends and `arrowSize` to set their length.



```ts
edge: {
  type: 'line',
  style: {
    stroke: '#99ADD1',
    lineWidth: (_source, _target, edge) => Number(edge.data?.lw ?? 2),
    endArrow: (_source, _target, edge) => edge.data?.dir !== 'none',
    startArrow: (_source, _target, edge) => edge.data?.dir === 'both',
  },
},
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
/**
 * Demo: Arrow directions - none / forward / bidirectional
 */
import { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';

export async function runGraph(container: string | HTMLElement) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    autoFit: true,
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: [
        { id: 'n1', name: 'No arrow', x: 80, y: 120 },
        { id: 't1', name: '', x: 280, y: 120 },
        { id: 'n2', name: 'Forward', x: 400, y: 120 },
        { id: 't2', name: '', x: 600, y: 120 },
        { id: 'n3', name: 'Bidirectional', x: 80, y: 280 },
        { id: 't3', name: '', x: 280, y: 280 },
        { id: 'n4', name: 'Thick + arrow', x: 400, y: 280 },
        { id: 't4', name: '', x: 600, y: 280 },
      ],
      edges: [
        { source: 'n1', target: 't1', data: { dir: 'none' } },
        { source: 'n2', target: 't2', data: { dir: 'forward' } },
        { source: 'n3', target: 't3', data: { dir: 'both' } },
        { source: 'n4', target: 't4', data: { dir: 'forward', lw: 6 } },
      ],
    },
    node: { type: 'circle', style: { fill: '#5B8FF9', size: 24, label: (node) => node.name ?? '' } },
    // #region arrow-options
    edge: {
      type: 'line',
      style: {
        stroke: '#99ADD1',
        lineWidth: (_source, _target, edge) => Number(edge.data?.lw ?? 2),
        endArrow: (_source, _target, edge) => edge.data?.dir !== 'none',
        startArrow: (_source, _target, edge) => edge.data?.dir === 'both',
      },
    },
    // #endregion arrow-options
    theme: 'light',
  });

  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}

export async function run(container: string | HTMLElement) {
  const graph = await runGraph(container);
  return {
    getData: () => graph.getData(),
    fitView: () => graph.fitView({ padding: 64 }),
    destroy: () => graph.destroy(),
  };
}
```

## Hit area [#hit-area]

Use `hitAreaWidth` to widen the area that detects pointer input while keeping the stroke width. This example enables selection with `click-select`.



```ts
edge: {
  type: 'line',
  style: {
    stroke: '#64748b',
    lineWidth: 1.5,
    endArrow: false,
    hitAreaWidth: (_source, _target, edge) => edge.id === 'wide' ? 24 : 2,
  },
  stateStyles: { selected: { stroke: '#873bf4' } },
},
behaviors: ['click-select'],
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: [
        { id: 'narrow-source', x: 100, y: 80, data: { label: 'Width 2' } },
        { id: 'narrow-target', x: 440, y: 80 },
        { id: 'wide-source', x: 100, y: 200, data: { label: 'Width 24' } },
        { id: 'wide-target', x: 440, y: 200 },
      ],
      edges: [
        { id: 'narrow', source: 'narrow-source', target: 'narrow-target' },
        { id: 'wide', source: 'wide-source', target: 'wide-target' },
      ],
    },
    node: { style: { size: 20, label: (node) => String(node.data?.label ?? '') } },
    // #region hit-area
    edge: {
      type: 'line',
      style: {
        stroke: '#64748b',
        lineWidth: 1.5,
        endArrow: false,
        hitAreaWidth: (_source, _target, edge) => edge.id === 'wide' ? 24 : 2,
      },
      stateStyles: { selected: { stroke: '#873bf4' } },
    },
    behaviors: ['click-select'],
    // #endregion hit-area
    autoFit: { padding: 48, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}
```

edge: {

      edges: [
        { id: 'api-db', source: 'api', target: 'db', states: ['selected'] },
        { id: 'api-cache', source: 'api', target: 'cache' },
