<span id="parallel-edges" style="{ scrollMarginTop: '8rem' }" />

<span id="parallel-edges-and-self-loops" style="{ display: 'block', scrollMarginTop: '8rem' }" />

## Parallel-edge spacing [#parallel-edge-spacing]

Separate multiple relationships between the same two nodes with parallel edges. A self-loop connects a node to itself.

### Separate same-direction and reverse edges [#separate-same-direction-and-reverse-edges]

Use `edge.parallelEdges` to separate overlapping edges between the same two nodes. The top row shows three A→B edges and a purple self-loop on B. The bottom row shows a pair in opposite directions.



```ts
const selfLoop = { id: 'bb', source: 'B', target: 'B' };
const parallelEdges = { enabled: true, offset: 48, includeReverse: true, maxOffset: 100 };
const edge: EdgeConfig = {
  type: 'line',
  parallelEdges,
  style: {
    endArrow: true,
    lineWidth: 2,
    stroke: (_source, _target, edge) => {
      if (edge.source === edge.target) return '#7c3aed';
      return edge.source === 'D' ? '#f6903d' : '#1783ff';
    },
  },
};
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph, type EdgeConfig } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import GUI from 'lil-gui';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  // #region separation
  const selfLoop = { id: 'bb', source: 'B', target: 'B' };
  const parallelEdges = { enabled: true, offset: 48, includeReverse: true, maxOffset: 100 };
  const edge: EdgeConfig = {
    type: 'line',
    parallelEdges,
    style: {
      endArrow: true,
      lineWidth: 2,
      stroke: (_source, _target, edge) => {
        if (edge.source === edge.target) return '#7c3aed';
        return edge.source === 'D' ? '#f6903d' : '#1783ff';
      },
    },
  };
  // #endregion separation
  let { enabled, offset, includeReverse } = parallelEdges;
  const options = () => ({ ...parallelEdges, enabled, offset, includeReverse });
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: [
        { id: 'A', x: 0, y: 0 }, { id: 'B', x: 260, y: 0 },
        { id: 'C', x: 0, y: 150 }, { id: 'D', x: 260, y: 150 },
      ],
      edges: [
        { id: 'ab1', source: 'A', target: 'B' },
        { id: 'ab2', source: 'A', target: 'B' },
        { id: 'ab3', source: 'A', target: 'B' },
        selfLoop,
        { id: 'cd', source: 'C', target: 'D' },
        { id: 'dc', source: 'D', target: 'C' },
      ],
    },
    node: { style: { size: 26, label: (node) => node.id, labelPlacement: 'bottom' } },
    edge,
    behaviors: ['zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas', 'drag-node'],
    autoFit: { padding: [90, 64, 64, 64], maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  const ui = createDemoPanel(container);
  const status = document.createElement('div');
  status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
  status.style.cssText = 'position:absolute;left:12px;bottom:10px;background:#fff;color:#334155;padding:4px 8px;font:12px system-ui;pointer-events:none;';
  const applySeparationOptions = () => {
    // #region update
    graph.updateOptions({ edge: { parallelEdges: options() } });
    // #endregion update
  };
  const updateStatus = () => {
    status.textContent = `enabled: ${enabled} · offset: ${offset} · includeReverse: ${includeReverse} · A→B: ${graph.getEdges().filter((edge) => edge.source === 'A').length}`;
  };
  const actions: Array<[string, () => void]> = [
    ['Toggle separation', () => {
      enabled = !enabled;
      applySeparationOptions();
    }],
    ['Spacing 24 / 64', () => {
      offset = offset === 24 ? 64 : 24;
      applySeparationOptions();
    }],
    ['Toggle reverse group', () => {
      includeReverse = !includeReverse;
      applySeparationOptions();
    }],
    // #region mutation
    ['Add ab4', () => { if (!graph.getEdgeData('ab4')) graph.addEdge({ id: 'ab4', source: 'A', target: 'B' }); }],
    ['Remove ab4', () => { graph.removeEdge('ab4'); }],
    // #endregion mutation
  ];
  const destroy = graph.destroy.bind(graph);
  graph.destroy = () => {
    ui.destroy(); status.remove(); destroy();
  };
  try {
    await graph.render();
    if (graph.destroyed) return graph;
    for (const [label, action] of actions) {
      ui.addAction(label, () => { action(); updateStatus(); });
    }
    container.append(status);
    updateStatus();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}


export function createDemoPanel(container: string | HTMLElement, description = '') {
  const host = typeof container === 'string' ? document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(container)! : container;
  if (getComputedStyle(host).position === 'static') host.style.position = 'relative';

  let gui: GUI | undefined;
  const getGui = () => {
    if (!gui) {
      gui = new GUI({ container: host, width: 160 });
      gui.domElement.classList.add('g6lite-demo-controls');
      gui.domElement.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      Object.assign(gui.domElement.style, {
        position: 'absolute',
        top: '10px',
        right: '10px',
        zIndex: '30',
        maxWidth: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
        maxHeight: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
      });
    }
    return gui;
  };

  let status: HTMLDivElement | undefined;
  const setStatus = (message: string) => {
    if (!status) {
      status = document.createElement('div');
      status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
      status.dataset.role = 'status';
      status.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      status.style.cssText =
        'position:absolute;left:12px;bottom:10px;z-index:20;max-width:min(28rem,calc(100% - 24px));color:#64748b;font:12px/1.45 system-ui,sans-serif;pointer-events:none;white-space:pre-wrap;';
      host.append(status);
    }
    status.textContent = message;
  };
  if (description) setStatus(description);

  return {
    get gui() {
      return getGui();
    },
    addAction(label: string, action: () => void, folder = getGui()) {
      return folder.add({ [label]: action }, label);
    },
    addChoice<T extends string>(
      label: string,
      choices: readonly T[] | Record<string, T>,
      value: T,
      onChange: (value: T) => void,
    ) {
      const options = Array.isArray(choices) ? [...choices] : choices;
      return getGui().add({ value }, 'value', options).name(label).onChange(onChange);
    },
    setStatus,
    destroy() {
      gui?.destroy();
      status?.remove();
    },
  };
}
```



### Adjust parallel-edge spacing and grouping [#grouping-and-spacing]

Set `edge.parallelEdges` in `new Graph()` to enable separation and configure it. This works with `line` and `arc`.

```ts
const graph = new Graph({
  container,
  data,
  edge: {
    type: 'line',
    parallelEdges: { enabled: true, offset: 48, includeReverse: true },
  },
});
```

* **Spacing**. Click **Spacing 24 / 64** above and compare the three A→B edges. Increasing `offset` from `24` to `64` makes the two outer edges bend farther apart.
* **Grouping**. `includeReverse: true` puts C→D and D→C in the same group, separating them. Click **Toggle reverse group** to set it to `false`. Each edge forms its own group and the pair overlaps in the example.

After rendering, use `updateOptions()` to change the spacing. It replaces the entire `parallelEdges` object, so include the settings you want to keep.

```ts
graph.updateOptions({
  edge: { parallelEdges: { enabled: true, offset: 64, includeReverse: true } },
});
```

See [ParallelEdgesConfig](/en/docs/api/options#config-parallel-edge-fields) for units, offset limits, and grouping rules.

### Configure parallel edges in transforms [#entries-and-precedence]

If you configure data processing in `transforms`, `process-parallel-edges` gives you the same behavior. Either option works on its own.

```ts
const graph = new Graph({
  container,
  data,
  transforms: [
    { type: 'process-parallel-edges', options: { offset: 24 } },
  ],
});
```

If you set the same option in both places, `edge.parallelEdges` takes priority. With `offset: 48` in the edge config and `offset: 24` in the transform, the graph uses `48`. Set `edge.parallelEdges` to `false` to turn separation off.

### Add or remove parallel edges [#update-after-adding-or-removing-edges]

When parallel-edge separation is enabled, adding or removing an edge automatically rearranges the edges in its group. Click **Add ab4** above to add a fourth A→B edge. The existing edges move to make room.

```ts
graph.addEdge({ id: 'ab4', source: 'A', target: 'B' });
```

Click **Remove ab4** to delete the new edge and return to three A→B edges.

```ts
graph.removeEdge('ab4');
```

### Self-loops and labels [#self-loops-and-labels]

Set `source` and `target` to the same node to draw a loop. Drag a node to see its loops and labels move with it.



```ts
data: {
  nodes: [{ id: 'A', x: 0, y: 0 }, { id: 'B', x: 220, y: 0 }],
  edges: [
    { id: 'a1', source: 'A', target: 'A' },
    { id: 'b1', source: 'B', target: 'B' },
    { id: 'b2', source: 'B', target: 'B' },
    { id: 'b3', source: 'B', target: 'B' },
  ],
},
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    // #region loops
    data: {
      nodes: [{ id: 'A', x: 0, y: 0 }, { id: 'B', x: 220, y: 0 }],
      edges: [
        { id: 'a1', source: 'A', target: 'A' },
        { id: 'b1', source: 'B', target: 'B' },
        { id: 'b2', source: 'B', target: 'B' },
        { id: 'b3', source: 'B', target: 'B' },
      ],
    },
    // #endregion loops
    node: { style: { size: 32, label: (node) => node.id, labelPlacement: 'bottom' } },
    edge: {
      type: 'line',
      parallelEdges: false,
      style: {
        endArrow: true, stroke: '#7c3aed', lineWidth: 2,
        label: (_source, _target, edge) => edge.id ?? '',
        labelBackground: '#fff', labelBackgroundPadding: 3,
      },
    },
    behaviors: ['zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas', 'drag-node', 'click-select'],
    autoFit: { padding: 64, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}
```



The renderer sets loop sizes and levels. `parallelEdges` spacing applies to edges between distinct endpoints.

<span id="curves-and-polyline-routing" style="{ display: 'block', scrollMarginTop: '8rem' }" />

<span id="edge-polyline" style="{ display: 'block', scrollMarginTop: '8rem' }" />

## Polyline routing [#polyline-routing]

Set `edge.type: 'polyline'`, then choose a path with `router`. See [EdgeConfig.style](/en/docs/api/options#config-edge-style) for fields and defaults.

<span id="choosing-a-router" style="{ display: 'block', scrollMarginTop: '8rem' }" />

### Choose a router [#choose-a-router]

| Router     | Use                                                                                        |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `orth`     | Flowcharts. Connects endpoints with horizontal and vertical segments and supports `radius` |
| `tree`     | Hierarchies. Assigns ports to edges from the same source and draws smooth curves           |
| `indented` | Directory trees. Connects children to a parent trunk                                       |
| `fishbone` | Fishbone diagrams. Pair with the `fishbone` layout                                         |

### Orthogonal connections and rounding [#orthogonal-connections-and-rounding]

Orthogonal edges use horizontal and vertical segments. Set **Radius** to `0` for square corners or `16` for rounded corners.



```ts
const layout = {
  type: 'dagre', rankdir: 'LR',
  nodesep: 40, ranksep: 96, nodeSize: [84, 32],
} satisfies LayoutConfig;
const edge: EdgeConfig = {
  type: 'polyline',
  style: { router: 'orth', radius: 16, endArrow: true, lineWidth: 2 },
};
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph, type EdgeConfig, type LayoutConfig } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import GUI from 'lil-gui';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  // #region routing
  const layout = {
    type: 'dagre', rankdir: 'LR',
    nodesep: 40, ranksep: 96, nodeSize: [84, 32],
  } satisfies LayoutConfig;
  const edge: EdgeConfig = {
    type: 'polyline',
    style: { router: 'orth', radius: 16, endArrow: true, lineWidth: 2 },
  };
  // #endregion routing
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D'].map((id) => ({ id })),
      edges: [
        { id: 'A-B', source: 'A', target: 'B' },
        { id: 'A-C', source: 'A', target: 'C' },
        { id: 'B-D', source: 'B', target: 'D' },
        { id: 'C-D', source: 'C', target: 'D' },
      ],
    },
    node: {
      type: 'rect',
      style: { width: 84, height: 32, borderRadius: 5, label: (node) => node.id, labelPlacement: 'center', labelColor: '#fff' },
    },
    layout,
    edge,
    behaviors: ['zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas'],
    autoFit: { padding: 48, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  const ui = createDemoPanel(container);
  const destroy = graph.destroy.bind(graph);
  graph.destroy = () => { ui.destroy(); destroy(); };
  try {
    await graph.render();
    ui.addChoice('Radius', ['0', '16'], '16', (value) => {
      const radius = Number(value);
      // #region rounding
      graph.updateOptions({ edge: { style: { radius } } });
      // #endregion rounding
    });
    ui.addChoice<'LR' | 'TB'>('Direction', ['LR', 'TB'], 'LR', async (rankdir) => {
      try {
        graph.setLayout({ ...layout, rankdir });
        await graph.render();
      } catch {
        if (!graph.destroyed) ui.setStatus('Layout failed');
      }
    });
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}


export function createDemoPanel(container: string | HTMLElement, description = '') {
  const host = typeof container === 'string' ? document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(container)! : container;
  if (getComputedStyle(host).position === 'static') host.style.position = 'relative';

  let gui: GUI | undefined;
  const getGui = () => {
    if (!gui) {
      gui = new GUI({ container: host, width: 160 });
      gui.domElement.classList.add('g6lite-demo-controls');
      gui.domElement.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      Object.assign(gui.domElement.style, {
        position: 'absolute',
        top: '10px',
        right: '10px',
        zIndex: '30',
        maxWidth: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
        maxHeight: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
      });
    }
    return gui;
  };

  let status: HTMLDivElement | undefined;
  const setStatus = (message: string) => {
    if (!status) {
      status = document.createElement('div');
      status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
      status.dataset.role = 'status';
      status.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      status.style.cssText =
        'position:absolute;left:12px;bottom:10px;z-index:20;max-width:min(28rem,calc(100% - 24px));color:#64748b;font:12px/1.45 system-ui,sans-serif;pointer-events:none;white-space:pre-wrap;';
      host.append(status);
    }
    status.textContent = message;
  };
  if (description) setStatus(description);

  return {
    get gui() {
      return getGui();
    },
    addAction(label: string, action: () => void, folder = getGui()) {
      return folder.add({ [label]: action }, label);
    },
    addChoice<T extends string>(
      label: string,
      choices: readonly T[] | Record<string, T>,
      value: T,
      onChange: (value: T) => void,
    ) {
      const options = Array.isArray(choices) ? [...choices] : choices;
      return getGui().add({ value }, 'value', options).name(label).onChange(onChange);
    },
    setStatus,
    destroy() {
      gui?.destroy();
      status?.remove();
    },
  };
}
```



### Indented directory connections [#indented-directory-connections]

Pair the `indented` layout and router to connect children to a parent trunk. The example sets `direction: 'LR'`.



```ts
layout: { type: 'indented', direction: 'LR', indent: 160, rowHeight: 70 },
edge: {
  type: 'polyline',
  style: { router: 'indented', indentTarget: 'left', radius: 10, lineWidth: 2, hitAreaWidth: 12 },
  stateStyles: { selected: { stroke: '#873bf4' } },
},
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph, register } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import indented from '@antv/g6-lite/layouts/indented';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  register('layout', 'indented', indented);
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: ['Root', 'Group', 'Item', 'Other'].map((id) => ({ id })),
      edges: [
        { id: 'root-group', source: 'Root', target: 'Group' },
        { id: 'group-item', source: 'Group', target: 'Item' },
        { id: 'root-other', source: 'Root', target: 'Other' },
      ],
    },
    node: {
      type: 'rect',
      style: { width: 80, height: 28, borderRadius: 5, label: (node) => node.id, labelPlacement: 'center', labelColor: '#fff' },
    },
    // #region routing
    layout: { type: 'indented', direction: 'LR', indent: 160, rowHeight: 70 },
    edge: {
      type: 'polyline',
      style: { router: 'indented', indentTarget: 'left', radius: 10, lineWidth: 2, hitAreaWidth: 12 },
      stateStyles: { selected: { stroke: '#873bf4' } },
    },
    // #endregion routing
    behaviors: ['click-select'],
    autoFit: { padding: 48, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}
```



Adjust indentation and row spacing with `layout.indent` and `layout.rowHeight`.

<span id="indented-targets-and-trunks" style="{ display: 'block', scrollMarginTop: '8rem' }" />

#### Choose where edges meet child nodes [#choose-indenttarget]

In a horizontal directory tree, set `indentTarget` to `left` to connect to the side of the child rectangle closest to its parent, as shown above.

```ts
edge: {
  type: 'polyline',
  style: { router: 'indented', indentTarget: 'left' },
},
```

For text-only child nodes, use `right` to extend the line to the end of the text. Switch between **有背景** (with background) and **无样式** (text only) in the [indented tree example](/en/docs/examples/indented-tree) to see both options.

### Set the direction of polylines [#direction-and-updates]

Polylines follow the layout direction. For Dagre, `rankdir: 'LR'` goes left to right and `rankdir: 'TB'` goes top to bottom. Use **Direction** in the [orthogonal connections example](#orthogonal-connections-and-rounding) to compare them.

```ts
graph.setLayout({ type: 'dagre', rankdir: 'TB', nodeSize: [84, 32] });
await graph.render();
```

For the indented layout, `direction: 'LR'` indents to the right and `direction: 'RL'` indents to the left.

## Edge labels [#edge-labels]

Set the relationship name with `edge.style.label` and its position along the edge with `labelPlacement`. The preview compares labels near the start, in the middle, and near the end.



```ts
edge: {
  type: 'line',
  style: {
    lineWidth: 2,
    hitAreaWidth: 12,
    label: (_s, _t, edge) => String(edge.id),
    labelPlacement: (_s, _t, edge) => edge.data?.placement as EdgeLabelPlacement,
    labelFontSize: 12,
    labelColor: '#334155',
    labelBackground: (_s, _t, edge) => edge.id === 'start' ? false : '#eef2ff',
    labelBackgroundPadding: 4,
    labelAutoRotate: true,
  },
  stateStyles: { selected: { stroke: '#873bf4' } },
},
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph, type EdgeLabelPlacement } from '@antv/g6-lite';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const rows = ['start', 'center', 'end'] as const;
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: rows.flatMap((id, index) => [
        { id: id + '-s', x: 100, y: 50 + index * 90 },
        { id: id + '-t', x: 440, y: 80 + index * 90 },
      ]),
      edges: rows.map((id) => ({ id, source: id + '-s', target: id + '-t', data: { placement: id } })),
    },
    node: { style: { size: 20 } },
    // #region edge-label-options
    edge: {
      type: 'line',
      style: {
        lineWidth: 2,
        hitAreaWidth: 12,
        label: (_s, _t, edge) => String(edge.id),
        labelPlacement: (_s, _t, edge) => edge.data?.placement as EdgeLabelPlacement,
        labelFontSize: 12,
        labelColor: '#334155',
        labelBackground: (_s, _t, edge) => edge.id === 'start' ? false : '#eef2ff',
        labelBackgroundPadding: 4,
        labelAutoRotate: true,
      },
      stateStyles: { selected: { stroke: '#873bf4' } },
    },
    // #endregion edge-label-options
    label: { hideOnCollision: false, hideOnLowZoom: false },
    behaviors: ['click-select'],
    autoFit: { padding: 48, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}
```



| Field                    | Type                                           | Default and rules                                                                    |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `label`                  | `EdgeStyleValue<string \| false>`              | `false`; only nonempty strings render, while empty strings or `false` hide the label |
| `labelFontSize`          | `EdgeStyleValue<number>`                       | `10` screen pixels; use a finite positive value                                      |
| `labelFontFamily`        | `EdgeStyleValue<string>`                       | System sans-serif stack                                                              |
| `labelColor`             | `EdgeStyleValue<string>`                       | `'#666'`, independent of line color                                                  |
| `labelPlacement`         | `EdgeStyleValue<'start' \| 'center' \| 'end'>` | `'center'`; path parameters `t = 0.2 / 0.5 / 0.8`, not exact endpoints               |
| `labelBackground`        | `EdgeStyleValue<string \| false>`              | `'rgba(255,255,255,0.8)'`; `false` disables the background                           |
| `labelBackgroundPadding` | `EdgeStyleValue<number>`                       | `2` screen pixels around the background; use a finite nonnegative value              |
| `labelAutoRotate`        | `EdgeStyleValue<boolean>`                      | `true`; follow the tangent while keeping text upright. `false` keeps text horizontal |

### Label background styles [#edge-label-background]

Set the background with `labelBackground` and its padding with `labelBackgroundPadding`. The `start` label above has its background turned off.

### Position and visibility [#position-and-visibility]

Labels on `cubic` and `polyline` edges use the line between endpoints for position and rotation. Font size and visibility follow [global label policies](/en/docs/guides/label#global-label-policies). The `hidden` state of the edge and its endpoints also affects visibility.

### labelRenderer [#edge-label-renderer]

Set `edge.labelRenderer` to choose how labels are drawn. The `demo-multiline` renderer below draws the protocol and request type on separate lines.



```ts
edge: {
  type: 'arc',
  labelRenderer: 'demo-multiline',
  style: {
    label: (_source, _target, edge) => String(edge.data?.label ?? ''),
    labelFontSize: 10,
    labelBackground: 'rgba(255,255,255,0.9)',
    labelBackgroundPadding: 3,
    labelAutoRotate: true,
  },
},
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
/**
 * Demo: unified custom node/edge LabelRenderer lifecycle.
 * The multiline behavior lives entirely in this demo, not in G6Lite core.
 */
import { Graph, register, type LabelRenderer } from '@antv/g6-lite';

interface MultilineLayoutData {
  lines: string[];
  lineHeight: number;
  contentWidth: number;
}

// #region renderer
const multilineRenderer: LabelRenderer<MultilineLayoutData> = {
  measure({ ctx, text, style }) {
    ctx.font = `${style.labelFontWeight} ${style.labelFontSize}px ${style.labelFontFamily}`;
    const lines = text.split('\n');
    const lineHeight = style.labelFontSize * 1.2;
    const contentWidth = Math.max(...lines.map((line) => ctx.measureText(line).width));
    const padding = style.labelBackgroundPadding;
    return {
      width: contentWidth + padding * 2,
      height: lines.length * lineHeight + padding * 2,
      data: { lines, lineHeight, contentWidth },
    };
  },
  draw({ ctx, style, layout }) {
    const data = layout.data;
    if (!data) return;
    if (style.labelBackground) {
      ctx.fillStyle = style.labelBackground;
      ctx.fillRect(-layout.width / 2, -layout.height / 2, layout.width, layout.height);
    }
    ctx.font = `${style.labelFontWeight} ${style.labelFontSize}px ${style.labelFontFamily}`;
    ctx.fillStyle = style.labelColor;
    ctx.textAlign = 'center';
    ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';
    data.lines.forEach((line, index) => {
      const y = (index - (data.lines.length - 1) / 2) * data.lineHeight;
      ctx.fillText(line, 0, y);
    });
  },
};

register('label', 'demo-multiline', multilineRenderer);
// #endregion renderer

export async function run(container: string | HTMLElement) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    // Labels are two lines and hang below nodes (labelPlacement: 'bottom');
    // the bottom padding reserves their height so they stay inside the view.
    autoFit: { padding: [24, 48, 64, 48] },
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: [
        { id: 'source', data: { label: 'Source Service\nShanghai' } },
        { id: 'gateway', data: { label: 'API Gateway\nPrimary' } },
        { id: 'target', data: { label: 'Target Store\nHangzhou' } },
      ],
      edges: [
        { source: 'source', target: 'gateway', data: { label: 'HTTPS\nrequest' } },
        { source: 'gateway', target: 'target', data: { label: 'RPC\nresponse' } },
      ],
    },
    layout: { type: 'dagre', rankdir: 'LR', nodeSize: 32, ranksep: 180 },
    behaviors: ['zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas', 'drag-node'],
    // #region node-label
    node: {
      labelRenderer: 'demo-multiline',
      style: {
        size: 32,
        label: (node) => String(node.data?.label ?? node.id),
        labelPlacement: 'bottom',
        labelFontSize: 12,
        labelBackground: 'rgba(255,255,255,0.92)',
        labelBackgroundPadding: 4,
      },
    },
    // #endregion node-label
    // #region edge-label
    edge: {
      type: 'arc',
      labelRenderer: 'demo-multiline',
      style: {
        label: (_source, _target, edge) => String(edge.data?.label ?? ''),
        labelFontSize: 10,
        labelBackground: 'rgba(255,255,255,0.9)',
        labelBackgroundPadding: 3,
        labelAutoRotate: true,
      },
    },
    // #endregion edge-label
  });
  await graph.render();
  return graph;
}
```



See [Custom Label Renderer](/en/docs/guides/custom-label-renderer) to implement and register a renderer.

## Develop a custom edge [#custom-edge]

Use an `EdgeExtension` to package a reusable path and appearance. See [Custom edges](/en/docs/guides/custom-edge) for registration, configuration, and a runnable example.

## Update edges dynamically [#update-edges-dynamically]

<span id="runtime-updates" style="{ display: 'block', scrollMarginTop: '8rem' }" />

<span id="options-edge-runtime-updates" style="{ display: 'block', scrollMarginTop: '8rem' }" />

Update one edge’s data or change the graph-wide style after rendering. **Lower SQL latency** updates the SQL edge, and **Set edge color** recolors both edges.



```ts
panel.addAction('Lower SQL latency', () => {
  graph.updateEdgeData('api-db', { latency: 60 });
});
panel.addAction('Set edge color', () => {
  graph.updateOptions({ edge: { style: { stroke: '#1783FF' } } });
});
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import GUI from 'lil-gui';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: [
        { id: 'API', x: 0, y: 0 },
        { id: 'DB', x: 230, y: -55 },
        { id: 'Cache', x: 230, y: 55 },
      ],
      edges: [
        { id: 'api-db', source: 'API', target: 'DB', data: { protocol: 'SQL', latency: 120 } },
        { id: 'api-cache', source: 'API', target: 'Cache', data: { protocol: 'TCP', latency: 24 } },
      ],
    },
    node: { style: { size: 24, label: (node) => node.id } },
    edge: {
      style: {
        stroke: '#64748B',
        lineWidth: (_source, _target, edge) => Number(edge.data?.latency ?? 0) >= 100 ? 4 : 2,
        label: (_source, _target, edge) => `${edge.data?.protocol} · ${edge.data?.latency} ms`,
        labelAutoRotate: false,
      },
    },
    autoFit: { padding: 56, maxZoom: 1 },
    behaviors: [],
  });
  const panel = createDemoPanel(container);
  const destroy = graph.destroy.bind(graph);
  graph.destroy = () => {
    panel.destroy();
    destroy();
  };
  try {
    await graph.render();
    // #region edge-updates
    panel.addAction('Lower SQL latency', () => {
      graph.updateEdgeData('api-db', { latency: 60 });
    });
    panel.addAction('Set edge color', () => {
      graph.updateOptions({ edge: { style: { stroke: '#1783FF' } } });
    });
    // #endregion edge-updates
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}


export function createDemoPanel(container: string | HTMLElement, description = '') {
  const host = typeof container === 'string' ? document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(container)! : container;
  if (getComputedStyle(host).position === 'static') host.style.position = 'relative';

  let gui: GUI | undefined;
  const getGui = () => {
    if (!gui) {
      gui = new GUI({ container: host, width: 160 });
      gui.domElement.classList.add('g6lite-demo-controls');
      gui.domElement.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      Object.assign(gui.domElement.style, {
        position: 'absolute',
        top: '10px',
        right: '10px',
        zIndex: '30',
        maxWidth: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
        maxHeight: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
      });
    }
    return gui;
  };

  let status: HTMLDivElement | undefined;
  const setStatus = (message: string) => {
    if (!status) {
      status = document.createElement('div');
      status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
      status.dataset.role = 'status';
      status.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      status.style.cssText =
        'position:absolute;left:12px;bottom:10px;z-index:20;max-width:min(28rem,calc(100% - 24px));color:#64748b;font:12px/1.45 system-ui,sans-serif;pointer-events:none;white-space:pre-wrap;';
      host.append(status);
    }
    status.textContent = message;
  };
  if (description) setStatus(description);

  return {
    get gui() {
      return getGui();
    },
    addAction(label: string, action: () => void, folder = getGui()) {
      return folder.add({ [label]: action }, label);
    },
    addChoice<T extends string>(
      label: string,
      choices: readonly T[] | Record<string, T>,
      value: T,
      onChange: (value: T) => void,
    ) {
      const options = Array.isArray(choices) ? [...choices] : choices;
      return getGui().add({ value }, 'value', options).name(label).onChange(onChange);
    },
    setStatus,
    destroy() {
      gui?.destroy();
      status?.remove();
    },
  };
}
```



See [`updateEdgeData()`](/en/docs/api/graph#updateedgedata) and [`updateOptions()`](/en/docs/api/graph#updateoptions) for more operations.

## Common questions [#common-questions]

### Why do parallel edges still overlap? [#why-do-parallel-edges-still-overlap]

Check that `enabled` is `true` and the type is `line` or `arc`, then check `maxOffset` and `includeReverse`.

### Why does offset not resize self-loops? [#why-does-offset-not-resize-self-loops]

The renderer sizes self-loops. `offset` controls parallel-edge spacing.

### Why is a thin line still difficult to select? [#why-is-a-thin-line-still-difficult-to-select]

Use `hitAreaWidth` with an interaction such as `click-select`.

### Why is a label missing? [#why-is-a-label-missing]

Check that `edge.style.label` returns text, then check zoom, collisions, and whether the edge or an endpoint is hidden.

### Why doesn't changing the router at runtime work? [#why-do-router-or-trunkgap-changes-do-nothing]

After setting a new `router` with `updateOptions()`, call `render()` to rebuild the polyline paths.

### Why does an edge cross another node? [#why-does-an-edge-cross-another-node]

`orth` routes from the two endpoints. Adjust layout or node spacing to keep edges clear of other nodes.

### Why does a configured state not activate? [#why-does-a-configured-state-not-activate]

Activate the state with a behavior or `setItemState(edgeId, state, true)`.

### Why does a line miss the node boundary? [#why-does-a-line-miss-the-node-boundary]

Check node dimensions, layout `nodeSize`, and direction. Use `indentTarget: 'left'` for rectangles in horizontal directory trees.

### Why does the label not follow the polyline? [#why-does-the-label-not-follow-the-polyline]

`polyline` labels use the line between endpoints for position and rotation.

<span id="other-configuration" style="{ display: 'block', scrollMarginTop: '8rem' }" />

# Event basics (/en/docs/guides/events)





Graph events tell you what was clicked or selected and which data operation completed. Start with the click example, then follow the links below for other event use cases.

## Element events [#element-events]

### Listen to a node click [#listen-to-a-node-click]

On an existing Graph, register a handler; click-select is not required.

```ts
import type { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';

declare const graph: Graph;
graph.on('node:click', ({ nodeId }) => {
  console.log('Clicked node', nodeId);
});
```

Listening does not select nodes or change styles. Click a node, edge, or empty space below to see its target and coordinates.



```ts
const onClick = (event: GraphElementEvent) => {
  latest = [
    `${event.targetType}: ${event.targetId ?? 'empty'}`,
    `client (${point(event.client)})`,
    `canvas (${point(event.canvas)})`,
    `graph (${point(event.graph)})`,
  ].join(' | ');
  update();
};
const clickEvents = ['node:click', 'edge:click', 'canvas:click'] as const;
for (const event of clickEvents) graph.on(event, onClick);
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph, type GraphElementEvent, type GraphEventMap } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import GUI from 'lil-gui';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: [{ id: 'A', x: 0, y: 0 }, { id: 'B', x: 160, y: 0 }, { id: 'C', x: 320, y: 0 }],
      edges: [{ id: 'A-B', source: 'A', target: 'B' }],
    },
    node: { style: { size: 32, label: (node) => node.id, labelOffsetY: 8 } },
    edge: { style: { hitAreaWidth: 12 } },
    behaviors: [],
    autoFit: { padding: 60, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  const ui = createDemoPanel(container);
  const status = document.createElement('div');
  status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
  status.style.cssText = 'position:absolute;bottom:12px;left:12px;right:12px;padding:8px;background:white;color:#334155;font:12px/1.6 system-ui;white-space:pre-line;pointer-events:none;z-index:20;';
  let latest = 'Click a node, edge, or empty canvas';
  let onceResult = 'once: not armed';
  const update = () => { status.textContent = `${latest}\n${onceResult}`; };
  const point = ({ x, y }: { x: number; y: number }) => `${Math.round(x)}, ${Math.round(y)}`;
  // #region listeners
  const onClick = (event: GraphElementEvent) => {
    latest = [
      `${event.targetType}: ${event.targetId ?? 'empty'}`,
      `client (${point(event.client)})`,
      `canvas (${point(event.canvas)})`,
      `graph (${point(event.graph)})`,
    ].join(' | ');
    update();
  };
  const clickEvents = ['node:click', 'edge:click', 'canvas:click'] as const;
  for (const event of clickEvents) graph.on(event, onClick);
  // #endregion listeners
  const onOnce = ({ nodeId }: GraphEventMap['node:click'][0]) => {
    onceResult = `once: ${nodeId} (consumed)`;
    update();
  };
  const destroy = graph.destroy.bind(graph);
  graph.destroy = () => {
    for (const event of clickEvents) graph.off(event, onClick);
    graph.off('node:click', onOnce);
    ui.destroy();
    status.remove();
    destroy();
  };
  try {
    await graph.render();
    update();
    ui.gui.add({ listening: true }, 'listening').name('Listening').onChange((listening: boolean) => {
      for (const event of clickEvents) {
        if (listening) graph.on(event, onClick);
        else graph.off(event, onClick);
      }
    });
    ui.addAction('Arm once', () => {
      graph.off('node:click', onOnce);
      graph.once('node:click', onOnce);
      onceResult = 'once: waiting for a node click';
      update();
    });
    container.append(status);
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}


export function createDemoPanel(container: string | HTMLElement, description = '') {
  const host = typeof container === 'string' ? document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(container)! : container;
  if (getComputedStyle(host).position === 'static') host.style.position = 'relative';

  let gui: GUI | undefined;
  const getGui = () => {
    if (!gui) {
      gui = new GUI({ container: host, width: 160 });
      gui.domElement.classList.add('g6lite-demo-controls');
      gui.domElement.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      Object.assign(gui.domElement.style, {
        position: 'absolute',
        top: '10px',
        right: '10px',
        zIndex: '30',
        maxWidth: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
        maxHeight: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
      });
    }
    return gui;
  };

  let status: HTMLDivElement | undefined;
  const setStatus = (message: string) => {
    if (!status) {
      status = document.createElement('div');
      status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
      status.dataset.role = 'status';
      status.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      status.style.cssText =
        'position:absolute;left:12px;bottom:10px;z-index:20;max-width:min(28rem,calc(100% - 24px));color:#64748b;font:12px/1.45 system-ui,sans-serif;pointer-events:none;white-space:pre-wrap;';
      host.append(status);
    }
    status.textContent = message;
  };
  if (description) setStatus(description);

  return {
    get gui() {
      return getGui();
    },
    addAction(label: string, action: () => void, folder = getGui()) {
      return folder.add({ [label]: action }, label);
    },
    addChoice<T extends string>(
      label: string,
      choices: readonly T[] | Record<string, T>,
      value: T,
      onChange: (value: T) => void,
    ) {
      const options = Array.isArray(choices) ? [...choices] : choices;
      return getGui().add({ value }, 'value', options).name(label).onChange(onChange);
    },
    setStatus,
    destroy() {
      gui?.destroy();
      status?.remove();
    },
  };
}
```



### Read data and positions [#read-data-and-positions]

* data is optional business data attached to the node or edge.
* client is the viewport position, useful for menus.
* canvas is CSS pixels from the canvas top-left.
* graph is the graph position, useful for creating or moving elements.

For edges, read edgeId / source / target; for group backgrounds, read comboId. Find all fields and mouse events in [element events](/en/docs/api/graph/events#event-element).

### Listen for Combo hover [#listen-for-combo-hover]

Use `combo:pointerover` to show a group hint and `combo:pointerleave` to hide it. Moving from the group background onto one of its nodes also triggers the leave event. See [Combo events](/en/docs/api/graph/events#combos).

## Removing listeners [#removing-listeners]

Retain the registered function and remove it on unmount or subscription replacement. A new arrow function with similar text is a different reference.

```ts
import type { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';

export function observeClicks(graph: Graph, onClick: () => void) {
  graph.on('node:click', onClick);
  return () => graph.off('node:click', onClick);
}
```

Use once when you need only the next occurrence. Arm once registers the next node click; Listening controls the independent persistent subscription. See [on / off / once](/en/docs/api/graph#on) for parameters.

## Selection and drag events [#selection-and-drag-events]

To synchronize selected nodes, observe selection results. To persist moved positions, observe drag completion. Enable the corresponding Behavior first.

Continue with [selection and dragging](/en/docs/guides/events/selection-drag): try the canvas, then connect selection, persistence, and cleanup.

## Lifecycle and data events [#lifecycle-and-data-events]

Initial rendering, incremental changes, replacement, and relayout emit different events. afterrender does not repeat for every data update.

See when to update the graph, read node positions, or respond to data replacement. [Rendering, layout, and data updates](/en/docs/guides/events/lifecycle)

## Common questions [#common-questions]

### Why is nativeEvent undefined? [#why-is-nativeevent-undefined]

Element clicks, hover, and wheel expose nativeEvent. Selection and some drag stages use event; drag completion and region selection may have no native-event field. Look up the event in the [event reference](/en/docs/api/graph/events).

### Why are positions still old when layout finishes? [#why-are-positions-still-old-when-layout-finishes]

layout:end / afterlayout precede write-back. Await graph.layout() before querying; see the [lifecycle guide](/en/docs/guides/events/lifecycle).

### Why does a listener fire repeatedly or never fire? [#why-does-a-listener-fire-repeatedly-or-never-fire]

Check duplicate registration, handler identity for off, whether once was consumed, and whether the required Behavior is enabled.

## Custom events [#custom-event-typing]

Use `graph.emit()` to dispatch application events, such as a reset-view notification from a toolbar button. [See the custom event example](/en/docs/guides/events/custom)

Continue with the [event reference](/en/docs/api/graph/events), [interaction combinations](/en/docs/guides/behaviors), and [event panel](/en/docs/examples/event-log).

**Related runnable examples**

* [Event log](/en/docs/examples/event-log)
* [Context menu](/en/docs/examples/context-menu)


# Extension system (/en/docs/guides/extensions)



Prefer configuration before developing an extension. Extension covers eight categories; Plugin means independent DOM and peripheral state, not all extension types.

## Choosing a category [#choosing-a-category]

| Task                                         | Tutorial                                                | Contract                                                              |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Reusable nodes, overlays, decoration anchors | [Custom nodes](/en/docs/guides/custom-node)             | [NodeExtension](/en/docs/api/extensions#nodeextension)                |
| Edge bases, business styles, states          | [Custom edges](/en/docs/guides/custom-edge)             | [EdgeExtension](/en/docs/api/extensions#edgeextension)                |
| Node or edge label content                   | [Label Renderer](/en/docs/guides/custom-label-renderer) | [LabelRenderer](/en/docs/api/extensions#labelrenderer)                |
| Node decoration content                      | [Decoration](/en/docs/guides/custom-decoration)         | [DecorationRenderer](/en/docs/api/extensions#decorationrenderer)      |
| Graph event-driven interaction               | [Custom interactions](/en/docs/guides/custom-behavior)  | [Behavior contract](/en/docs/api/options#custom-interaction-contract) |
| Position calculations                        | [Custom layouts](/en/docs/guides/custom-layout)         | [LayoutExtension](/en/docs/api/extensions#layoutextension)            |
| Whole-input preprocessing                    | [Transforms](/en/docs/guides/transform-overview)        | [TransformExtension](/en/docs/api/extensions#transformextension)      |
| Independent DOM, subscriptions, state        | [Plugins](/en/docs/guides/custom-plugin)                | [PluginExtension](/en/docs/api/extensions#pluginextension)            |

Tutorials pair code with live canvases. See the [combined example](/en/docs/examples/extension-system), or [built-in badges](/en/docs/examples/decoration-badges) before implementing common content.

## Registration and activation [#registration-and-activation]

Registration defines a name; Graph configuration activates it. Register before first use. See [registration](/en/docs/api/extensions#extension-types) for overloads, replacement, and compatibility inputs.

## Lifecycle by category [#lifecycle-by-category]

Drawing descriptors are cached and stateless. Runtime factories return fresh instances by category and configuration position, not exactly once per Graph. See [instance scope](/en/docs/api/extensions#instance-scope).

Layout cancellation and standalone execution are in [Custom layouts](/en/docs/guides/custom-layout). To rerun an existing graph, use [layout methods](/en/docs/api/graph#graph-layout).

## Public capability boundary [#public-capability-boundary]

Use [ExtensionContext](/en/docs/api/extensions#extensioncontext) for snapshots, states, coordinates, and cleanup. Avoid context.graph and internal Renderer / DataModel. Drawing extensions retain supported bases, picking, and engine positioning rather than taking over rendering.

Runtime extensions release owned DOM, subscriptions, timers, and asynchronous work. Explicitly injected application capabilities can provide controlled host collaboration, as shown in the Plugin tutorial.

## Decoration visibility [#decoration-visibility]

Follow [Custom decorations](/en/docs/guides/custom-decoration) for measuring, drawing, stacking, overflow, and collisions. See [DecorationRenderer](/en/docs/api/extensions#decorationrenderer) for callbacks and [decoration configuration](/en/docs/api/options#config-node-decoration) for placement fields.

For simple styles, labels, states, or Tooltip, prefer [node](/en/docs/guides/node), [edge](/en/docs/guides/edge), [label](/en/docs/guides/label), and [interaction](/en/docs/guides/behaviors) configuration first. See [Transform / Plugin options](/en/docs/api/options#options-transforms-plugins) for constructor-option boundaries. Import public types from the package root, not source internals.

**Related runnable examples**

* [Extension system showcase](/en/docs/examples/extension-system)


# Labels and icons (/en/docs/guides/label)





Configure text and placement first, then choose visibility policies. Find full fields in [node labels and icons](/en/docs/guides/node#labels), [edge labels](/en/docs/guides/edge#edge-labels), and the [label policy reference](/en/docs/api/options#options-label).

## Node labels [#node-labels]

1. Set `node.style.label`, or read node data in a callback. data.name does not display automatically.
2. Choose labelPlacement, then fine-tune with labelOffsetX/Y.
3. Set labelFontSize and labelColor. The default renderer handles DPR conversion.

The example places labels to the left, below, and to the right, and hides the fourth node's label.



```ts
import { Graph, type LabelPlacement } from '@antv/g6-lite';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: [
        { id: 'api', name: 'API', x: 100, y: 100, data: { placement: 'left' } },
        { id: 'Database', x: 260, y: 100 },
        { id: 'cache', name: 'Cache', x: 420, y: 100, data: { placement: 'right' } },
        { id: 'worker', name: 'Worker', x: 580, y: 100, data: { hideLabel: true } },
      ],
      edges: [],
    },
    // #region label-style
    node: {
      style: {
        size: 40,
        fill: '#1783FF',
        label: (node) => node.data?.hideLabel ? false : (node.name ?? node.id),
        labelPlacement: (node) => (node.data?.placement as LabelPlacement | undefined) ?? 'bottom',
        labelFontSize: 14,
        labelFontWeight: '600',
      },
    },
    // #endregion label-style
    autoFit: { padding: 48, maxZoom: 1 },
    behaviors: [],
  });
  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}
```



## Node icons [#node-icons]

The left node below uses a text icon, and the right node uses an image icon.

* Text/font icons: set `iconType: 'text'`, then iconFontSize and iconColor. Load the font in your application.
* Images: set `iconType: 'image'` and an image URL, then iconWidth/Height. Loading is asynchronous; cross-origin resources need anonymous CORS.

Text icons follow the global font-size policy. Image icons scale with their nodes. Neither uses the label visibility thresholds or collision rules. See the [icon reference](/en/docs/guides/node#icons) for fields.



```ts
node: {
  style: {
    size: 56,
    fill: (node) => node.id === 'image' ? '#e6f4ff' : '#1783ff',
    iconType: (node) => node.id === 'image' ? 'image' : 'text',
    icon: (node) => node.id === 'image' ? imageUrl : 'A',
    iconWidth: 24,
    iconHeight: 21,
    iconOffsetY: -4,
    iconFontSize: 24,
    iconColor: '#fff',
    label: (node) => node.name ?? node.id,
    labelOffsetY: 6,
  },
},
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';

const imageUrl = new URL('../src/app/icon.svg', import.meta.url).href;

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: [
        { id: 'text', name: 'Text', x: 100, y: 100 },
        { id: 'image', name: 'Image', x: 260, y: 100 },
      ],
      edges: [],
    },
    // #region icon-style
    node: {
      style: {
        size: 56,
        fill: (node) => node.id === 'image' ? '#e6f4ff' : '#1783ff',
        iconType: (node) => node.id === 'image' ? 'image' : 'text',
        icon: (node) => node.id === 'image' ? imageUrl : 'A',
        iconWidth: 24,
        iconHeight: 21,
        iconOffsetY: -4,
        iconFontSize: 24,
        iconColor: '#fff',
        label: (node) => node.name ?? node.id,
        labelOffsetY: 6,
      },
    },
    // #endregion icon-style
    autoFit: { padding: 48, maxZoom: 1 },
    behaviors: [],
  });
  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}
```



## Long text and backgrounds [#long-text-and-backgrounds]

Use labelMaxWidth to truncate default node labels, and labelBackground/labelBackgroundPadding for a background and spacing. The long name below is limited to 120.



```ts
import { Graph, type NodeConfig } from '@antv/g6-lite';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  // #region node-label
  const node: NodeConfig = {
    style: {
      size: 40,
      label: (item) => String(item.data?.name ?? item.id),
      labelPlacement: 'bottom',
      labelMaxWidth: 120,
      labelBackground: (item) => item.id === 'db' ? '#fff1b8' : '#e6f4ff',
      labelBackgroundPadding: 6,
      labelFontWeight: '600',
    },
  };
  // #endregion node-label
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: [
        { id: 'api', x: 120, y: 100, data: { name: 'API Server' } },
        { id: 'db', x: 360, y: 100, data: { name: 'Database with a very long name' } },
      ],
      edges: [],
    },
    node,
    autoFit: { padding: 48, maxZoom: 1 },
    behaviors: [],
  });
  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}
```



For special layouts, use a [custom Label Renderer](/en/docs/guides/custom-label-renderer): register it, set node.labelRenderer or edge.labelRenderer, and keep nonempty style.label. Custom drawing handles truncation itself.

## Edge labels [#edge-labels]

Set text in `edge.style.label`. The callback is `(source, target, edge) => text`; its third argument is edge data. Use labelColor independently of the edge stroke.

Compare start, center, and end below, with labelAutoRotate enabled. Low-zoom and collision hiding are disabled for this comparison.



```ts
import { Graph, type EdgeLabelPlacement } from '@antv/g6-lite';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const rows = ['start', 'center', 'end'] as const;
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: rows.flatMap((id, index) => [
        { id: id + '-s', x: 100, y: 50 + index * 90 },
        { id: id + '-t', x: 440, y: 80 + index * 90 },
      ]),
      edges: rows.map((id) => ({ id, source: id + '-s', target: id + '-t', data: { placement: id } })),
    },
    node: { style: { size: 20 } },
    // #region edge-label-options
    edge: {
      type: 'line',
      style: {
        lineWidth: 2,
        hitAreaWidth: 12,
        label: (_s, _t, edge) => String(edge.id),
        labelPlacement: (_s, _t, edge) => edge.data?.placement as EdgeLabelPlacement,
        labelFontSize: 12,
        labelColor: '#334155',
        labelBackground: (_s, _t, edge) => edge.id === 'start' ? false : '#eef2ff',
        labelBackgroundPadding: 4,
        labelAutoRotate: true,
      },
      stateStyles: { selected: { stroke: '#873bf4' } },
    },
    // #endregion edge-label-options
    label: { hideOnCollision: false, hideOnLowZoom: false },
    behaviors: ['click-select'],
    autoFit: { padding: 48, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}
```



See [position and visibility](/en/docs/guides/edge#position-and-visibility) for label positioning limitations on curved and polyline edges.

## Global label policies [#global-label-policies]

Configure the top-level Graph `label` option for your goal:

* Set `scaleWithZoom: false` to keep node, edge, and Combo labels, text icons, and built-in text badges at a fixed screen size. When enabled, text grows with the graph and stays at or above 0.25× its base size when zooming out.
* Adjust when labels appear: set nodeMinZoom and edgeMinZoom. Set one threshold to 0 to bypass it independently.
* Diagnose hidden/overlapping labels: temporarily disable hideOnCollision or hideOnLowZoom, then restore the policies you need.

### Try the visibility controls [#options-label-code-and-matching-result]

The example starts at zoom 0.4 with scaleWithZoom explicitly disabled for readable text. Node labels pass their threshold, while the Request edge label is below 0.5 and hidden. Two nearby node labels collide, retaining the earlier one.

* Disable hideOnCollision to reveal overlapping labels.
* Disable hideOnLowZoom to show the edge label at the current zoom.
* Enable scaleWithZoom, then zoom in/out to compare node and edge text sizes.



```ts
import { Graph, type LabelOptions } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import GUI from 'lil-gui';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  // #region label-options
  const policy: Required<LabelOptions> = {
    scaleWithZoom: false,
    hideOnLowZoom: true,
    hideOnCollision: true,
    nodeMinZoom: 0.3,
    edgeMinZoom: 0.5,
  };
  // #endregion label-options
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: [
        { id: 'Client alpha', x: 0, y: 100 },
        { id: 'Client beta', x: 100, y: 100 },
        { id: 'API gateway', x: 900, y: 100 },
      ],
      edges: [{ id: 'Request', source: 'Client beta', target: 'API gateway' }],
    },
    node: { style: { size: 48, label: (node) => node.id, labelFontSize: 14 } },
    edge: { style: { label: (_s, _t, edge) => edge.id ?? '', labelFontSize: 14 } },
    label: policy,
    behaviors: [],
    autoFit: { minZoom: 0.4, maxZoom: 0.4 },
  });
  const ui = createDemoPanel(container);
  const destroy = graph.destroy.bind(graph);
  graph.destroy = () => { ui.destroy(); destroy(); };
  try {
    await graph.render();
    const settings = { ...policy };
    for (const key of ['scaleWithZoom', 'hideOnLowZoom', 'hideOnCollision'] as const) {
      ui.gui.add(settings, key).onChange((checked: boolean) => {
        graph.updateOptions({ label: { [key]: checked } });
      });
    }
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}


export function createDemoPanel(container: string | HTMLElement, description = '') {
  const host = typeof container === 'string' ? document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(container)! : container;
  if (getComputedStyle(host).position === 'static') host.style.position = 'relative';

  let gui: GUI | undefined;
  const getGui = () => {
    if (!gui) {
      gui = new GUI({ container: host, width: 160 });
      gui.domElement.classList.add('g6lite-demo-controls');
      gui.domElement.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      Object.assign(gui.domElement.style, {
        position: 'absolute',
        top: '10px',
        right: '10px',
        zIndex: '30',
        maxWidth: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
        maxHeight: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
      });
    }
    return gui;
  };

  let status: HTMLDivElement | undefined;
  const setStatus = (message: string) => {
    if (!status) {
      status = document.createElement('div');
      status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
      status.dataset.role = 'status';
      status.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      status.style.cssText =
        'position:absolute;left:12px;bottom:10px;z-index:20;max-width:min(28rem,calc(100% - 24px));color:#64748b;font:12px/1.45 system-ui,sans-serif;pointer-events:none;white-space:pre-wrap;';
      host.append(status);
    }
    status.textContent = message;
  };
  if (description) setStatus(description);

  return {
    get gui() {
      return getGui();
    },
    addAction(label: string, action: () => void, folder = getGui()) {
      return folder.add({ [label]: action }, label);
    },
    addChoice<T extends string>(
      label: string,
      choices: readonly T[] | Record<string, T>,
      value: T,
      onChange: (value: T) => void,
    ) {
      const options = Array.isArray(choices) ? [...choices] : choices;
      return getGui().add({ value }, 'value', options).name(label).onChange(onChange);
    },
    setStatus,
    destroy() {
      gui?.destroy();
      status?.remove();
    },
  };
}
```



### Zoom thresholds [#zoom-thresholds]

With default low-zoom hiding, labels passing the threshold check are listed below. Content, hidden states, and collisions still determine final visibility.

| Camera zoom      | Node labels          | Edge labels          |
| ---------------- | -------------------- | -------------------- |
| Below 0.3        | Hidden               | Hidden               |
| 0.3 to below 0.5 | Rendering candidates | Hidden               |
| At least 0.5     | Rendering candidates | Rendering candidates |

Set one MinZoom to 0 to bypass only that label type's threshold. Disabling hideOnLowZoom does not disable collision hiding.

Thresholds accept finite nonnegative numbers, including `0`. Negative values, `NaN`, and `Infinity` fall back to the corresponding defaults. Thresholds compare directly against the camera's `zoom`.

### Collision order [#collision-order]

Each frame processes node labels before edge labels, following rendering-data order within each type. Earlier labels reserve space; later overlapping labels are hidden. Recalculation on each frame means zoom or order changes can change the survivors. selected/highlight receive no automatic priority.

#### Collision bounds and custom renderers [#collision-bounds-and-custom-renderers]

Built-in labels use unrotated text rectangles, excluding extra background padding. Custom labelRenderer bounds come from measure's width/height. The policy hides overlaps without moving labels or avoiding node bodies.

Custom node and edge label renderers also pass low-zoom and collision checks. The supplied style already includes font scaling and the device pixel ratio. Custom decorations can use `labelScale` to convert a base font size to Canvas pixels.

### Scope [#scope]

* Labels need nonempty text; `label: false` or an empty string draws nothing. Business data alone does not create labels.
* Low-zoom and collision policies apply to node and edge labels. Text icons, built-in text badges, and Combo labels share the font-size policy and control their own visibility.
* Element hidden states, hidden edge endpoints, and viewport culling still affect visibility. Disabling both hiding policies does not guarantee every label appears.

See [node labels](/en/docs/guides/node#labels), [edge labels](/en/docs/guides/edge#edge-labels), or [Combo labels](/en/docs/guides/combo#padding-bounds-and-labels) for content and appearance.

<span id="options-label-runtime-updates" />

## Runtime updates [#runtime-updates]

After the first `await graph.render()`, update appearance and visibility without recreating the instance:

```ts
graph.updateOptions({ node: { style: { labelColor: '#334155' } } });
graph.updateOptions({ edge: { style: { labelColor: '#475569' } } });
graph.updateOptions({ label: { hideOnCollision: false } });
graph.updateOptions({ label: { nodeMinZoom: 0.6 } });
```

The two `label` updates set collision hiding and the node threshold separately. Omitted fields keep their current values, and `label: {}` keeps the current policy. Set a field explicitly to `undefined` to restore its default.

Updates reprocess styles and configured transforms while retaining the current layout and view. Use `updateNodeData()` or `updateEdgeData()` to change business data read by label callbacks. See [configuration updates](/en/docs/api/graph#updateoptions).

## Performance tips [#performance-tips]

* Show important nodes and relationships first in large graphs; business filtering can return false from label callbacks.
* Use global policies for zoom-based hiding. Label callbacks receive element data, not camera zoom; keep them inexpensive.

## Common questions [#common-questions]

### Why is a label missing? [#why-is-a-label-missing]

Check nonempty label, zoom thresholds, collisions, and hidden states on the element or edge endpoints. Business data alone does not generate text. Disabling thresholds does not disable collision hiding.

### Why is a text icon or image missing? [#why-is-a-text-icon-or-image-missing]

Text icons require iconType: 'text' and a loaded font. Check image URLs and anonymous CORS. Node hidden states and viewport bounds still apply.

### Why is long text not truncated? [#why-is-long-text-not-truncated]

labelMaxWidth applies to default node labels and must be positive. Edges do not expose it; custom renderers handle truncation themselves. Default node labels do not wrap automatically.

### Why did the text color not change? [#why-did-the-text-color-not-change]

Use labelColor; labelFill is not supported. Edge stroke, text-icon iconColor, and label colors are configured independently.

<span id="options-label-related-entries" />

## Related [#related]

# Grid, circular, and layered layouts (/en/docs/guides/layout-arrangements)





## Choose a layout [#choose-a-layout]

| Type                                          | Description                                   | Example configuration                |
| --------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| [`grid`](/en/docs/guides/layout-grid)         | Arrange nodes in two rows and three columns.  | `{ type: 'grid', rows: 2, cols: 3 }` |
| [`circular`](/en/docs/guides/layout-circular) | Arrange nodes in a ring with radius 100.      | `{ type: 'circular', radius: 100 }`  |
| [`dagre`](/en/docs/guides/layout-dagre)       | Arrange dependency layers from left to right. | `{ type: 'dagre', rankdir: 'LR' }`   |

## Compare layouts [#compare-layouts]

Use **Layout** to switch between `grid`, `circular`, and `dagre` on the same graph. The code shows the full configuration for all three.



```ts
const layouts: Record<string, LayoutConfig> = {
  grid: { type: 'grid', rows: 2, cols: 3, width: 360, height: 160 },
  circular: { type: 'circular', radius: 100 },
  dagre: { type: 'dagre', rankdir: 'LR', nodesep: 64, ranksep: 96, nodeSize: 28 },
};
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph, type LayoutConfig } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import GUI from 'lil-gui';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  // #region layout-options
  const layouts: Record<string, LayoutConfig> = {
    grid: { type: 'grid', rows: 2, cols: 3, width: 360, height: 160 },
    circular: { type: 'circular', radius: 100 },
    dagre: { type: 'dagre', rankdir: 'LR', nodesep: 64, ranksep: 96, nodeSize: 28 },
  };
  // #endregion layout-options
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E', 'F'].map((id) => ({ id })),
      edges: [
        { source: 'A', target: 'B' }, { source: 'A', target: 'C' },
        { source: 'B', target: 'D' }, { source: 'C', target: 'E' },
        { source: 'D', target: 'F' }, { source: 'E', target: 'F' },
      ],
    },
    layout: layouts.grid,
    node: { style: { size: 28, label: (node) => node.id, labelOffsetY: 8 } },
    behaviors: [],
    autoFit: { padding: 56, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  const ui = createDemoPanel(container);
  let generation = 0;
  const destroy = graph.destroy.bind(graph);
  graph.destroy = () => { generation++; ui.destroy(); destroy(); };
  try {
    await graph.render();
    ui.setStatus('grid ready');
    ui.addChoice('Layout', Object.keys(layouts), 'grid', async (value) => {
      const current = ++generation;
      ui.setStatus('Running…');
      graph.setLayout(layouts[value]);
      try {
        await graph.layout();
        if (current !== generation || graph.destroyed) return;
        graph.fitView({ padding: 56, maxZoom: 1 });
        ui.setStatus(`${value} ready`);
      } catch {
        if (current === generation && !graph.destroyed) ui.setStatus('Layout failed');
      }
    });
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}


export function createDemoPanel(container: string | HTMLElement, description = '') {
  const host = typeof container === 'string' ? document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(container)! : container;
  if (getComputedStyle(host).position === 'static') host.style.position = 'relative';

  let gui: GUI | undefined;
  const getGui = () => {
    if (!gui) {
      gui = new GUI({ container: host, width: 160 });
      gui.domElement.classList.add('g6lite-demo-controls');
      gui.domElement.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      Object.assign(gui.domElement.style, {
        position: 'absolute',
        top: '10px',
        right: '10px',
        zIndex: '30',
        maxWidth: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
        maxHeight: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
      });
    }
    return gui;
  };

  let status: HTMLDivElement | undefined;
  const setStatus = (message: string) => {
    if (!status) {
      status = document.createElement('div');
      status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
      status.dataset.role = 'status';
      status.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      status.style.cssText =
        'position:absolute;left:12px;bottom:10px;z-index:20;max-width:min(28rem,calc(100% - 24px));color:#64748b;font:12px/1.45 system-ui,sans-serif;pointer-events:none;white-space:pre-wrap;';
      host.append(status);
    }
    status.textContent = message;
  };
  if (description) setStatus(description);

  return {
    get gui() {
      return getGui();
    },
    addAction(label: string, action: () => void, folder = getGui()) {
      return folder.add({ [label]: action }, label);
    },
    addChoice<T extends string>(
      label: string,
      choices: readonly T[] | Record<string, T>,
      value: T,
      onChange: (value: T) => void,
    ) {
      const options = Array.isArray(choices) ? [...choices] : choices;
      return getGui().add({ value }, 'value', options).name(label).onChange(onChange);
    },
    setStatus,
    destroy() {
      gui?.destroy();
      status?.remove();
    },
  };
}
```



## Adjust layer spacing [#adjust-layer-spacing]

In Dagre, `nodesep` sets the spacing within a layer, and `ranksep` sets the spacing between layers. Set `rankdir` to `LR` for left to right or `TB` for top to bottom.

See the [layout reference](/en/docs/api/options#config-library-layout-fields) for more parameters, or try the [flowchart example](/en/docs/examples/flowchart).


# Circular layout (/en/docs/guides/layout-circular)





## Overview [#overview]

Arrange nodes around a circle or vary the radius to form a spiral.

## When to use it [#when-to-use-it]

Use a circle for networks without a hierarchy, or a spiral for ordered nodes.

## Basic usage [#basic-usage]

Set the layout type with `layout.type`.

```ts
const graph = new Graph({
  container,
  data,
  layout: { type: 'circular' },
});
```

## Options [#options]

| Option                     | Description                                                             | Type                                                | Default                           |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `radius`                   | Fixed circle radius. Set only the start and end radii to make a spiral. | `number`                                            | Half the smaller layout dimension |
| `startRadius`, `endRadius` | Spiral start and end radii, used when `radius` is omitted.              | `number`                                            | —                                 |
| `clockwise`                | Whether to arrange nodes clockwise.                                     | `boolean`                                           | `true`                            |
| `ordering`                 | Node order by topology, directed topology, or degree.                   | `'topology'` \| `'topology-directed'` \| `'degree'` | Input order                       |

[Common layout options](/en/docs/guides/layout) · [Layout reference](/en/docs/api/options#config-library-layout-fields)

## Code example [#code-example]

Eight nodes sit on a circle with a radius of 100.



```ts
import { Graph, register, type GraphOptions, type LayoutConfig } from '@antv/g6-lite';

type ExampleOptions = Pick<GraphOptions, 'data' | 'node' | 'edge'>;

function arrangement(type: string): ExampleOptions {
  if (type === 'dagre') {
    return {
      data: {
        nodes: ['Input', 'Review', 'Check', 'Publish'].map((id) => ({ id })),
        edges: [
          { source: 'Input', target: 'Review' },
          { source: 'Input', target: 'Check' },
          { source: 'Review', target: 'Publish' },
          { source: 'Check', target: 'Publish' },
        ],
      },
      node: {
        type: 'rect',
        style: {
          width: 80, height: 32, borderRadius: 6,
          label: (node) => node.id, labelColor: '#fff', labelPlacement: 'center',
        },
      },
      edge: { type: 'polyline', style: { router: 'orth', radius: 12, endArrow: true } },
    };
  }

  const ids = Array.from({ length: type === 'grid' ? 6 : 8 }, (_, i) => String.fromCharCode(65 + i));
  return {
    data: {
      nodes: ids.map((id) => ({ id })),
      edges: type === 'grid' ? [] : ids.map((source, i) => ({ source, target: ids[(i + 2) % ids.length] })),
    },
    node: { style: { size: 24, label: (node) => node.id, labelColor: '#fff', labelPlacement: 'center' } },
  };
}

async function render(container: HTMLElement, layout: LayoutConfig, options: ExampleOptions) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    ...options,
    layout,
    behaviors: ['drag-canvas', 'zoom-canvas'],
    autoFit: { padding: 36, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}

export function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const layout: LayoutConfig = { type: 'circular', radius: 100 };
  return render(container, layout, arrangement(layout.type));
}
```



### Spiral arrangement [#spiral-arrangement]

Set `startRadius` and `endRadius` to different values and omit `radius`.

```ts
const layout = { type: 'circular', startRadius: 30, endRadius: 140 };
```

[Compare Grid, Circular, and Dagre](/en/docs/guides/layout-arrangements)


# Concentric layout (/en/docs/guides/layout-concentric)





## Overview [#overview]

Place nodes in rings by a ranking metric, with higher values near the center.

## When to use it [#when-to-use-it]

Use it to emphasize hubs by their number of connections.

## Basic usage [#basic-usage]

Set the layout type with `layout.type`.

```ts
const graph = new Graph({
  container,
  data,
  layout: { type: 'concentric' },
});
```

## Options [#options]

| Option           | Description                                                         | Type                             | Default                |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| `sortBy`         | Ranking metric. `'degree'` ranks by node degree.                    | `'degree'` \| `(node) => number` | `'degree'`             |
| `maxLevelDiff`   | Ranking values in the same ring differ by less than this threshold. | `number`                         | Computed automatically |
| `preventOverlap` | Whether to space nodes to avoid overlap.                            | `boolean`                        | `false`                |
| `nodeSpacing`    | Gap reserved between nodes when preventing overlap.                 | `number`                         | `10`                   |

[Common layout options](/en/docs/guides/layout) · [Layout reference](/en/docs/api/options#config-library-layout-fields)

## Code example [#code-example]

Nodes are grouped by degree. The purple hub has five connections and sits at the center. Each blue node has three connections and sits on the inner ring. Each green node has one connection and sits on the outer ring.



```ts
import { Graph, register, type GraphOptions, type LayoutConfig } from '@antv/g6-lite';

type ExampleOptions = Pick<GraphOptions, 'data' | 'node' | 'edge'>;

function concentric(): ExampleOptions {
  const hub = 'Hub';
  const inner = ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E'];
  const edges = inner.flatMap((id) => [
    { source: hub, target: id },
    { source: id, target: `${id}1` },
    { source: id, target: `${id}2` },
  ]);
  return {
    data: {
      nodes: [{ id: hub }, ...edges.map(({ target }) => ({ id: target }))],
      edges,
    },
    node: {
      style: {
        size: 24,
        fill: (node) => node.id === hub ? '#6d28d9' : inner.includes(node.id) ? '#1677ff' : '#0f766e',
      },
    },
    edge: { style: { endArrow: false, stroke: '#91a5c1', lineWidth: 1.5 } },
  };
}

async function render(container: HTMLElement, layout: LayoutConfig, options: ExampleOptions) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    ...options,
    layout,
    behaviors: ['drag-canvas', 'zoom-canvas'],
    autoFit: { padding: 36, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}

export function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const layout: LayoutConfig = {
    type: 'concentric',
    sortBy: 'degree',
    maxLevelDiff: 1,
    preventOverlap: true,
    nodeSize: 24,
    nodeSpacing: 28,
  };
  return render(container, layout, concentric());
}
```



[Compare network layouts](/en/docs/guides/layout-networks)


# D3 force layout (/en/docs/guides/layout-d3-force)





## Overview [#overview]

Use D3’s force simulation to position nodes.

## When to use it [#when-to-use-it]

Use it when a network needs control over repulsion, link distance, or cooling speed.

## Basic usage [#basic-usage]

Set the layout type with `layout.type`.

```ts
const graph = new Graph({
  container,
  data,
  layout: { type: 'd3-force' },
});
```

## Options [#options]

| Option           | Description                                      | Type                 | Default                     |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------- | --------------------------- |
| `linkDistance`   | Target distance between linked nodes.            | `number` or function | `max(200, √nodeCount × 80)` |
| `nodeStrength`   | Force between nodes. Negative values repel.      | `number` or function | `-30`                       |
| `alphaDecay`     | Rate at which the simulation cools on each step. | `number`             | `0.1`                       |
| `preventOverlap` | Whether to enable node collision detection.      | `boolean`            | `false`                     |

[Common layout options](/en/docs/guides/layout) · [Layout reference](/en/docs/api/options#config-library-layout-fields)

## Code example [#code-example]

The target link distance is 100, and negative `nodeStrength` repels nodes.



```ts
import { Graph, register, type GraphOptions, type LayoutConfig } from '@antv/g6-lite';

type ExampleOptions = Pick<GraphOptions, 'data' | 'node' | 'edge'>;

function network(type: string): ExampleOptions {
  const links = [
    [0, 1], [0, 2], [0, 3], [1, 2], [1, 4], [1, 5],
    [2, 5], [2, 6], [3, 7], [3, 8], [3, 9],
    [7, 8], [8, 9], [4, 10], [4, 11], [10, 11],
  ];
  return {
    data: {
      nodes: Array.from({ length: 12 }, (_, index) => ({ id: String(index) })),
      edges: links.map(([source, target]) => ({ source: String(source), target: String(target) })),
    },
    node: {
      style: {
        size: 24,
        label: (node) => node.id,
        labelColor: '#fff',
        labelPlacement: 'center',
        fill: (node) => type === 'radial' && node.id === '0' ? '#6d28d9' : '#1677ff',
      },
    },
    edge: { style: { lineWidth: 2 } },
  };
}

async function render(container: HTMLElement, layout: LayoutConfig, options: ExampleOptions) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    ...options,
    layout,
    behaviors: ['drag-canvas', 'zoom-canvas'],
    autoFit: { padding: 36, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}

export function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const layout: LayoutConfig = { type: 'd3-force', linkDistance: 100, nodeStrength: -120, preventOverlap: true, nodeSize: 24 };
  return render(container, layout, network(layout.type));
}
```



[Compare network layouts](/en/docs/guides/layout-networks)


# Dagre layout (/en/docs/guides/layout-dagre)





## Overview [#overview]

Arrange nodes in layers based on directed edges.

## When to use it [#when-to-use-it]

Use it for workflows, call chains, and dependency graphs.

## Basic usage [#basic-usage]

Set the layout type with `layout.type`.

```ts
const graph = new Graph({
  container,
  data,
  layout: { type: 'dagre' },
});
```

## Options [#options]

| Option     | Description                                                               | Type                                 | Default  |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | -------- |
| `rankdir`  | Layer direction. `'LR'` goes left to right and `'TB'` goes top to bottom. | `'TB'` \| `'BT'` \| `'LR'` \| `'RL'` | `'TB'`   |
| `nodesep`  | Gap between nodes on the same layer.                                      | `number`                             | `50`     |
| `ranksep`  | Gap between layers.                                                       | `number`                             | `50`     |
| `nodeSize` | Node dimensions used by the layout.                                       | `number` \| `[number, number]`       | `[0, 0]` |

[Common layout options](/en/docs/guides/layout) · [Layout reference](/en/docs/api/options#config-library-layout-fields)

## Code example [#code-example]
