The workflow runs left to right, with Review and Check on the same layer.



```ts
import { Graph, register, type GraphOptions, type LayoutConfig } from '@antv/g6-lite';

type ExampleOptions = Pick<GraphOptions, 'data' | 'node' | 'edge'>;

function arrangement(type: string): ExampleOptions {
  if (type === 'dagre') {
    return {
      data: {
        nodes: ['Input', 'Review', 'Check', 'Publish'].map((id) => ({ id })),
        edges: [
          { source: 'Input', target: 'Review' },
          { source: 'Input', target: 'Check' },
          { source: 'Review', target: 'Publish' },
          { source: 'Check', target: 'Publish' },
        ],
      },
      node: {
        type: 'rect',
        style: {
          width: 80, height: 32, borderRadius: 6,
          label: (node) => node.id, labelColor: '#fff', labelPlacement: 'center',
        },
      },
      edge: { type: 'polyline', style: { router: 'orth', radius: 12, endArrow: true } },
    };
  }

  const ids = Array.from({ length: type === 'grid' ? 6 : 8 }, (_, i) => String.fromCharCode(65 + i));
  return {
    data: {
      nodes: ids.map((id) => ({ id })),
      edges: type === 'grid' ? [] : ids.map((source, i) => ({ source, target: ids[(i + 2) % ids.length] })),
    },
    node: { style: { size: 24, label: (node) => node.id, labelColor: '#fff', labelPlacement: 'center' } },
  };
}

async function render(container: HTMLElement, layout: LayoutConfig, options: ExampleOptions) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    ...options,
    layout,
    behaviors: ['drag-canvas', 'zoom-canvas'],
    autoFit: { padding: 36, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}

export function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const layout: LayoutConfig = { type: 'dagre', rankdir: 'LR', nodesep: 32, ranksep: 80, nodeSize: [80, 32] };
  return render(container, layout, arrangement(layout.type));
}
```



[Compare Grid, Circular, and Dagre](/en/docs/guides/layout-arrangements)


# Fishbone layout (/en/docs/guides/layout-fishbone)





## Overview [#overview]

Place the problem at the end of the spine. Each cause category joins the spine with a diagonal branch, and shorter horizontal lines attach individual causes to that branch.

## When to use it [#when-to-use-it]

Use it for three-level structures such as a problem, cause categories, and specific causes.

## Basic usage [#basic-usage]

This layout is optional. Import and register it before setting `layout.type`. For CDN usage, see [Optional layouts](/en/docs/guides/layout-overview#optional-layouts).

```ts
import { Graph, register } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import fishbone from '@antv/g6-lite/layouts/fishbone';

register('layout', 'fishbone', fishbone);

const graph = new Graph({
  container,
  data,
  layout: { type: 'fishbone' },
  edge: { type: 'polyline', style: { router: 'fishbone', endArrow: false } },
});
```

## Options [#options]

| Option             | Description                                                    | Type                       | Default      |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------ |
| `categoryGap`      | Gap between categories along the spine.                        | `number`                   | `180`        |
| `categoryDistance` | Vertical distance from a category to the spine.                | `number`                   | `200`        |
| `itemHStep`        | Additional horizontal offset for item nodes.                   | `number`                   | `20`         |
| `getWidth`         | Node width used by the layout. Match it to the rendered width. | Function returning a width | Returns `80` |
| `direction`        | `'RL'` mirrors the `'LR'` arrangement horizontally.            | `'LR'` \| `'RL'`           | `'LR'`       |

[Common layout options](/en/docs/guides/layout) · [Layout reference](/en/docs/api/options#config-tree-layout-fields)

## Code example [#code-example]

Define parent-child relationships as edges. Use the parent ID as `source` and the child ID as `target`.

This diagram breaks down a late release into four categories. People, Tools, Process, and Scope each have two specific causes.



```ts
import { Graph, register, type GraphOptions, type LayoutConfig } from '@antv/g6-lite';

import fishboneLayout from '@antv/g6-lite/layouts/fishbone';

type ExampleOptions = Pick<GraphOptions, 'data' | 'node' | 'edge'>;

function fishbone(): ExampleOptions {
  const head = 'Late release';
  const causes = [
    { category: 'People', items: ['Staff shortage', 'Late handoff'] },
    { category: 'Tools', items: ['Slow build', 'Test outages'] },
    { category: 'Process', items: ['Review queue', 'Manual checks'] },
    { category: 'Scope', items: ['New requests', 'Rework'] },
  ];
  const edges = causes.flatMap(({ category, items }) => [
    { source: head, target: category },
    ...items.map((item) => ({ source: category, target: item })),
  ]);
  const categories = new Set(causes.map(({ category }) => category));
  // #region edge-router
  const edge = {
    type: 'polyline',
    style: { router: 'fishbone', endArrow: false, stroke: '#7086a8', lineWidth: 2 },
  } as const;
  // #endregion edge-router
  return {
    data: { nodes: [{ id: head }, ...edges.map(({ target }) => ({ id: target }))], edges },
    node: {
      type: 'rect',
      style: {
        width: 96,
        height: (node) => node.id === head || categories.has(node.id) ? 30 : 22,
        borderRadius: 5,
        fill: (node) => node.id === head ? '#3730a3' : categories.has(node.id) ? '#1d4ed8' : '#eff6ff',
        label: (node) => node.id,
        labelPlacement: 'center',
        labelColor: (node) => node.id === head || categories.has(node.id) ? '#fff' : '#1e3a5f',
      },
    },
    edge,
  };
}

async function render(container: HTMLElement, layout: LayoutConfig, options: ExampleOptions) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    ...options,
    layout,
    behaviors: ['drag-canvas', 'zoom-canvas'],
    autoFit: { padding: 36, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}

export function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  register('layout', 'fishbone', fishboneLayout);
  const layout: LayoutConfig = {
    type: 'fishbone',
    direction: 'LR',
    categoryGap: 200,
    categoryDistance: 138,
    itemHStep: 26,
    getWidth: () => 96,
  };
  return render(container, layout, fishbone());
}
```



[Compare tree layouts](/en/docs/guides/layout-trees)


# ForceAtlas2 layout (/en/docs/guides/layout-force-atlas2)





## Overview [#overview]

Connected nodes attract while repulsion and gravity shape the network.

## When to use it [#when-to-use-it]

Use it to see densely connected groups and the links between them.

## Basic usage [#basic-usage]

Set the layout type with `layout.type`.

```ts
const graph = new Graph({
  container,
  data,
  layout: { type: 'force-atlas2' },
});
```

## Options [#options]

| Option         | Description                                             | Type      | Default                          |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | --------- | -------------------------------- |
| `kr`           | Repulsion coefficient between nodes.                    | `number`  | `5`                              |
| `kg`           | Gravity coefficient that pulls nodes toward the center. | `number`  | `1`                              |
| `barnesHut`    | Whether to approximate repulsion with Barnes–Hut.       | `boolean` | `true`                           |
| `maxIteration` | Maximum number of iterations.                           | `number`  | `100`, or `50` above 5,000 nodes |

[Common layout options](/en/docs/guides/layout) · [Layout reference](/en/docs/api/options#config-library-layout-fields)

## Code example [#code-example]

Stronger repulsion and gravity reveal three connected groups.



```ts
import { Graph, register, type GraphOptions, type LayoutConfig } from '@antv/g6-lite';

type ExampleOptions = Pick<GraphOptions, 'data' | 'node' | 'edge'>;

function network(type: string): ExampleOptions {
  const links = [
    [0, 1], [0, 2], [0, 3], [1, 2], [1, 4], [1, 5],
    [2, 5], [2, 6], [3, 7], [3, 8], [3, 9],
    [7, 8], [8, 9], [4, 10], [4, 11], [10, 11],
  ];
  return {
    data: {
      nodes: Array.from({ length: 12 }, (_, index) => ({ id: String(index) })),
      edges: links.map(([source, target]) => ({ source: String(source), target: String(target) })),
    },
    node: {
      style: {
        size: 24,
        label: (node) => node.id,
        labelColor: '#fff',
        labelPlacement: 'center',
        fill: (node) => type === 'radial' && node.id === '0' ? '#6d28d9' : '#1677ff',
      },
    },
    edge: { style: { lineWidth: 2 } },
  };
}

async function render(container: HTMLElement, layout: LayoutConfig, options: ExampleOptions) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    ...options,
    layout,
    behaviors: ['drag-canvas', 'zoom-canvas'],
    autoFit: { padding: 36, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}

export function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const layout: LayoutConfig = { type: 'force-atlas2', kr: 8, kg: 2 };
  return render(container, layout, network(layout.type));
}
```



[Compare network layouts](/en/docs/guides/layout-networks)


# Force layout (/en/docs/guides/layout-force)





## Overview [#overview]

Attraction pulls linked nodes together and repulsion keeps nodes apart.

## When to use it [#when-to-use-it]

Use it to explore connections in social or service dependency networks.

## Basic usage [#basic-usage]

Set the layout type with `layout.type`.

```ts
const graph = new Graph({
  container,
  data,
  layout: { type: 'force' },
});
```

## Options [#options]

| Option         | Description                           | Type     | Default               |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------- | -------- | --------------------- |
| `linkDistance` | Target distance between linked nodes. | `number` | `200`                 |
| `nodeStrength` | Repulsion strength between nodes.     | `number` | `1000`                |
| `edgeStrength` | Attraction strength along an edge.    | `number` | `50`                  |
| `maxIteration` | Maximum number of iterations.         | `number` | Depends on node count |

[Common layout options](/en/docs/guides/layout) · [Layout reference](/en/docs/api/options#config-library-layout-fields)

## Code example [#code-example]

The example sets the target distance between connected nodes to 100.



```ts
import { Graph, register, type GraphOptions, type LayoutConfig } from '@antv/g6-lite';

type ExampleOptions = Pick<GraphOptions, 'data' | 'node' | 'edge'>;

function network(type: string): ExampleOptions {
  const links = [
    [0, 1], [0, 2], [0, 3], [1, 2], [1, 4], [1, 5],
    [2, 5], [2, 6], [3, 7], [3, 8], [3, 9],
    [7, 8], [8, 9], [4, 10], [4, 11], [10, 11],
  ];
  return {
    data: {
      nodes: Array.from({ length: 12 }, (_, index) => ({ id: String(index) })),
      edges: links.map(([source, target]) => ({ source: String(source), target: String(target) })),
    },
    node: {
      style: {
        size: 24,
        label: (node) => node.id,
        labelColor: '#fff',
        labelPlacement: 'center',
        fill: (node) => type === 'radial' && node.id === '0' ? '#6d28d9' : '#1677ff',
      },
    },
    edge: { style: { lineWidth: 2 } },
  };
}

async function render(container: HTMLElement, layout: LayoutConfig, options: ExampleOptions) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    ...options,
    layout,
    behaviors: ['drag-canvas', 'zoom-canvas'],
    autoFit: { padding: 36, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}

export function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const layout: LayoutConfig = { type: 'force', linkDistance: 100 };
  return render(container, layout, network(layout.type));
}
```



[Compare network layouts](/en/docs/guides/layout-networks)


# Fruchterman layout (/en/docs/guides/layout-fruchterman)





## Overview [#overview]

Balance edge attraction and node repulsion, with gravity pulling the graph inward.

## When to use it [#when-to-use-it]

Use it for networks without a clear center or hierarchy.

## Basic usage [#basic-usage]

Set the layout type with `layout.type`.

```ts
const graph = new Graph({
  container,
  data,
  layout: { type: 'fruchterman' },
});
```

## Options [#options]

| Option         | Description                                       | Type     | Default               |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | -------- | --------------------- |
| `gravity`      | Strength of the pull toward the layout center.    | `number` | `10`                  |
| `speed`        | Speed factor for node movement in the simulation. | `number` | `5`                   |
| `maxIteration` | Maximum number of iterations.                     | `number` | Depends on node count |

[Common layout options](/en/docs/guides/layout) · [Layout reference](/en/docs/api/options#config-library-layout-fields)

## Code example [#code-example]

The example sets gravity to 12.



```ts
import { Graph, register, type GraphOptions, type LayoutConfig } from '@antv/g6-lite';

type ExampleOptions = Pick<GraphOptions, 'data' | 'node' | 'edge'>;

function network(type: string): ExampleOptions {
  const links = [
    [0, 1], [0, 2], [0, 3], [1, 2], [1, 4], [1, 5],
    [2, 5], [2, 6], [3, 7], [3, 8], [3, 9],
    [7, 8], [8, 9], [4, 10], [4, 11], [10, 11],
  ];
  return {
    data: {
      nodes: Array.from({ length: 12 }, (_, index) => ({ id: String(index) })),
      edges: links.map(([source, target]) => ({ source: String(source), target: String(target) })),
    },
    node: {
      style: {
        size: 24,
        label: (node) => node.id,
        labelColor: '#fff',
        labelPlacement: 'center',
        fill: (node) => type === 'radial' && node.id === '0' ? '#6d28d9' : '#1677ff',
      },
    },
    edge: { style: { lineWidth: 2 } },
  };
}

async function render(container: HTMLElement, layout: LayoutConfig, options: ExampleOptions) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    ...options,
    layout,
    behaviors: ['drag-canvas', 'zoom-canvas'],
    autoFit: { padding: 36, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}

export function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const layout: LayoutConfig = { type: 'fruchterman', gravity: 12 };
  return render(container, layout, network(layout.type));
}
```



[Compare network layouts](/en/docs/guides/layout-networks)


# Grid layout (/en/docs/guides/layout-grid)





## Overview [#overview]

Arrange nodes in a grid of rows and columns.

## When to use it [#when-to-use-it]

Use it for device panels or resource lists that need aligned nodes.

## Basic usage [#basic-usage]

Set the layout type with `layout.type`.

```ts
const graph = new Graph({
  container,
  data,
  layout: { type: 'grid' },
});
```

## Options [#options]

| Option            | Description                                         | Type                               | Default                |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| `rows`            | Number of rows.                                     | `number`                           | Computed automatically |
| `cols`            | Number of columns.                                  | `number`                           | Computed automatically |
| `width`, `height` | Width and height of the layout area.                | `number`                           | Canvas dimensions      |
| `sortBy`          | Sort nodes by ID or degree, or supply a comparator. | `'id'` \| `'degree'` \| comparator | `'degree'`             |

[Common layout options](/en/docs/guides/layout) · [Layout reference](/en/docs/api/options#config-library-layout-fields)

## Code example [#code-example]

Six nodes form two rows of three.



```ts
import { Graph, register, type GraphOptions, type LayoutConfig } from '@antv/g6-lite';

type ExampleOptions = Pick<GraphOptions, 'data' | 'node' | 'edge'>;

function arrangement(type: string): ExampleOptions {
  if (type === 'dagre') {
    return {
      data: {
        nodes: ['Input', 'Review', 'Check', 'Publish'].map((id) => ({ id })),
        edges: [
          { source: 'Input', target: 'Review' },
          { source: 'Input', target: 'Check' },
          { source: 'Review', target: 'Publish' },
          { source: 'Check', target: 'Publish' },
        ],
      },
      node: {
        type: 'rect',
        style: {
          width: 80, height: 32, borderRadius: 6,
          label: (node) => node.id, labelColor: '#fff', labelPlacement: 'center',
        },
      },
      edge: { type: 'polyline', style: { router: 'orth', radius: 12, endArrow: true } },
    };
  }

  const ids = Array.from({ length: type === 'grid' ? 6 : 8 }, (_, i) => String.fromCharCode(65 + i));
  return {
    data: {
      nodes: ids.map((id) => ({ id })),
      edges: type === 'grid' ? [] : ids.map((source, i) => ({ source, target: ids[(i + 2) % ids.length] })),
    },
    node: { style: { size: 24, label: (node) => node.id, labelColor: '#fff', labelPlacement: 'center' } },
  };
}

async function render(container: HTMLElement, layout: LayoutConfig, options: ExampleOptions) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    ...options,
    layout,
    behaviors: ['drag-canvas', 'zoom-canvas'],
    autoFit: { padding: 36, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}

export function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const layout: LayoutConfig = { type: 'grid', rows: 2, cols: 3, width: 360, height: 160 };
  return render(container, layout, arrangement(layout.type));
}
```



[Compare Grid, Circular, and Dagre](/en/docs/guides/layout-arrangements)


# Indented tree layout (/en/docs/guides/layout-indented)





## Overview [#overview]

List nodes in traversal order and indent them by depth.

## When to use it [#when-to-use-it]

Use it for file directories, navigation menus, and taxonomies.

## Basic usage [#basic-usage]

This layout is optional. Import and register it before setting `layout.type`. For CDN usage, see [Optional layouts](/en/docs/guides/layout-overview#optional-layouts).

```ts
import { Graph, register } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import indented from '@antv/g6-lite/layouts/indented';

register('layout', 'indented', indented);

const graph = new Graph({
  container,
  data,
  layout: { type: 'indented' },
});
```

## Options [#options]

| Option      | Description                                   | Type             | Default                     |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------- | ---------------- | --------------------------- |
| `indent`    | Horizontal indent per level.                  | `number`         | `80`                        |
| `rowHeight` | Vertical distance between adjacent rows.      | `number`         | `40`                        |
| `direction` | `'LR'` indents right and `'RL'` indents left. | `'LR'` \| `'RL'` | `'LR'`                      |
| `rootId`    | Root node ID.                                 | `string`         | First node without a parent |

[Common layout options](/en/docs/guides/layout) · [Layout reference](/en/docs/api/options#config-tree-layout-fields)

## Code example [#code-example]

Define parent-child relationships as edges. Use the parent ID as `source` and the child ID as `target`.

Each level indents by 72. The `indented` router draws the directory-style connectors.



```ts
import { Graph, register, type GraphOptions, type LayoutConfig } from '@antv/g6-lite';

import indented from '@antv/g6-lite/layouts/indented';

type ExampleOptions = Pick<GraphOptions, 'data' | 'node' | 'edge'>;

function tree(type: string): ExampleOptions {
  const edges = ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D'].flatMap((branch) => [
    { source: 'Root', target: branch },
    { source: branch, target: `${branch}1` },
    { source: branch, target: `${branch}2` },
  ]);
  return {
    data: {
      nodes: [{ id: 'Root' }, ...edges.map(({ target }) => ({ id: target }))],
      edges,
    },
    node: {
      style: {
        size: 16,
        label: (node) => node.id,
        labelPlacement: type === 'indented' ? 'right' : 'bottom',
      },
    },
    edge: type === 'indented'
      ? { type: 'polyline', style: { router: type, endArrow: false } }
      : { style: { endArrow: false } },
  };
}

async function render(container: HTMLElement, layout: LayoutConfig, options: ExampleOptions) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    ...options,
    layout,
    behaviors: ['drag-canvas', 'zoom-canvas'],
    autoFit: { padding: 36, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}

export function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  register('layout', 'indented', indented);
  const layout: LayoutConfig = { type: 'indented', direction: 'LR', indent: 72, rowHeight: 30 };
  return render(container, layout, tree(layout.type));
}
```



[Compare tree layouts](/en/docs/guides/layout-trees)


# MDS layout (/en/docs/guides/layout-mds)





## Overview [#overview]

Multidimensional scaling (MDS) approximates shortest-path distances in two dimensions.

## When to use it [#when-to-use-it]

Use it to examine how close or far apart nodes are in a network.

## Basic usage [#basic-usage]

This layout is optional. Import and register it before setting `layout.type`. For CDN usage, see [Optional layouts](/en/docs/guides/layout-overview#optional-layouts).

```ts
import { Graph, register } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import mds from '@antv/g6-lite/layouts/mds';

register('layout', 'mds', mds);

const graph = new Graph({
  container,
  data,
  layout: { type: 'mds' },
});
```

## Options [#options]

| Option         | Description                                     | Type               | Default                   |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------- |
| `linkDistance` | Reference length used to scale graph distances. | `number`           | `50`                      |
| `center`       | Center of the layout in graph coordinates.      | `[number, number]` | Center of the layout area |

[Common layout options](/en/docs/guides/layout) · [Layout reference](/en/docs/api/options#config-library-layout-fields)

## Code example [#code-example]

The example uses a scale of 80. Nodes farther apart in the network generally appear farther apart on the canvas.



```ts
import { Graph, register, type GraphOptions, type LayoutConfig } from '@antv/g6-lite';

import mds from '@antv/g6-lite/layouts/mds';

type ExampleOptions = Pick<GraphOptions, 'data' | 'node' | 'edge'>;

function network(type: string): ExampleOptions {
  const links = [
    [0, 1], [0, 2], [0, 3], [1, 2], [1, 4], [1, 5],
    [2, 5], [2, 6], [3, 7], [3, 8], [3, 9],
    [7, 8], [8, 9], [4, 10], [4, 11], [10, 11],
  ];
  return {
    data: {
      nodes: Array.from({ length: 12 }, (_, index) => ({ id: String(index) })),
      edges: links.map(([source, target]) => ({ source: String(source), target: String(target) })),
    },
    node: {
      style: {
        size: 24,
        label: (node) => node.id,
        labelColor: '#fff',
        labelPlacement: 'center',
        fill: (node) => type === 'radial' && node.id === '0' ? '#6d28d9' : '#1677ff',
      },
    },
    edge: { style: { lineWidth: 2 } },
  };
}

async function render(container: HTMLElement, layout: LayoutConfig, options: ExampleOptions) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    ...options,
    layout,
    behaviors: ['drag-canvas', 'zoom-canvas'],
    autoFit: { padding: 36, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}

export function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  register('layout', 'mds', mds);
  const layout: LayoutConfig = { type: 'mds', linkDistance: 80 };
  return render(container, layout, network(layout.type));
}
```



[Compare network layouts](/en/docs/guides/layout-networks)


# Mind map layout (/en/docs/guides/layout-mindmap)





## Overview [#overview]

Expand branches to one or both sides of a central topic.

## When to use it [#when-to-use-it]

Use it to organize ideas, knowledge, and categories.

## Basic usage [#basic-usage]

This layout is optional. Import and register it before setting `layout.type`. For CDN usage, see [Optional layouts](/en/docs/guides/layout-overview#optional-layouts).

```ts
import { Graph, register } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import mindmap from '@antv/g6-lite/layouts/mindmap';

register('layout', 'mindmap', mindmap);

const graph = new Graph({
  container,
  data,
  layout: { type: 'mindmap' },
});
```

## Options [#options]

| Option      | Description                                                            | Type                                     | Default           |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `direction` | `'LR'` goes right, `'RL'` goes left, and `'H'` uses `getSide`.         | `'H'` \| `'LR'` \| `'RL'`                | `'H'`             |
| `getSide`   | Select a side using the node, its branch index, and its parent’s side. | Function returning `'left'` or `'right'` | Returns `'right'` |
| `levelGap`  | Horizontal gap between a parent and its child.                         | `number`                                 | `120`             |
| `nodeGap`   | Vertical gap between siblings on the same side.                        | `number`                                 | `30`              |

[Common layout options](/en/docs/guides/layout) · [Layout reference](/en/docs/api/options#config-tree-layout-fields)

## Code example [#code-example]

Define parent-child relationships as edges. Use the parent ID as `source` and the child ID as `target`.

`getSide` places branches A and C on the left and B and D on the right.



```ts
import { Graph, register, type GraphNode, type GraphOptions, type LayoutConfig } from '@antv/g6-lite';

import mindmap from '@antv/g6-lite/layouts/mindmap';

type ExampleOptions = Pick<GraphOptions, 'data' | 'node' | 'edge'>;

function tree(type: string): ExampleOptions {
  const edges = ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D'].flatMap((branch) => [
    { source: 'Root', target: branch },
    { source: branch, target: `${branch}1` },
    { source: branch, target: `${branch}2` },
  ]);
  return {
    data: {
      nodes: [{ id: 'Root' }, ...edges.map(({ target }) => ({ id: target }))],
      edges,
    },
    node: {
      style: {
        size: 16,
        label: (node) => node.id,
        labelPlacement: type === 'indented' ? 'right' : 'bottom',
      },
    },
    edge: type === 'indented'
      ? { type: 'polyline', style: { router: type, endArrow: false } }
      : { style: { endArrow: false } },
  };
}

async function render(container: HTMLElement, layout: LayoutConfig, options: ExampleOptions) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    ...options,
    layout,
    behaviors: ['drag-canvas', 'zoom-canvas'],
    autoFit: { padding: 36, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}

export function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  register('layout', 'mindmap', mindmap);
  const layout: LayoutConfig = {
    type: 'mindmap',
    direction: 'H',
    levelGap: 100,
    nodeGap: 24,
    getWidth: () => 16,
    getHeight: (node: GraphNode) => node.id.length === 1 ? 64 : 16,
    getSide: (node: GraphNode) => /^[AC]/.test(node.id) ? 'left' : 'right',
  };
  return render(container, layout, tree(layout.type));
}
```



[Compare tree layouts](/en/docs/guides/layout-trees)


# Network layouts (/en/docs/guides/layout-networks)





## Choose a layout [#choose-a-layout]

| Goal                                  | Layout                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Bring connected nodes closer          | [`force`](/en/docs/guides/layout-force), [`d3-force`](/en/docs/guides/layout-d3-force), [`force-atlas2`](/en/docs/guides/layout-force-atlas2), [`fruchterman`](/en/docs/guides/layout-fruchterman) |
| Explore connections around one node   | [`radial`](/en/docs/guides/layout-radial), with `focusNode` identifying the center                                                                                                                 |
| Group nodes into rings by degree      | [`concentric`](/en/docs/guides/layout-concentric), with `sortBy: 'degree'`                                                                                                                         |
| Show graph distance in two dimensions | [`mds`](/en/docs/guides/layout-mds), with `linkDistance` setting the distance scale                                                                                                                |

## Configuration and example [#configuration-and-example]

The example starts with a radial layout. Set `focusNode` to `0` to choose its center and `unitRadius` to 68 to space the rings. Use **Layout** to compare all seven layouts on the same network.

Register Radial and MDS before using them. [Optional layouts](/en/docs/guides/layout-overview#optional-layouts)



```ts
const layouts: Record<string, LayoutConfig> = {
  radial: { type: 'radial', focusNode: '0', unitRadius: 68 },
  concentric: { type: 'concentric', sortBy: 'degree', nodeSize: 24 },
  force: { type: 'force', linkDistance: 100 },
  'd3-force': { type: 'd3-force', linkDistance: 100 },
  'force-atlas2': { type: 'force-atlas2', kr: 8, kg: 2 },
  fruchterman: { type: 'fruchterman', gravity: 12 },
  mds: { type: 'mds', linkDistance: 80 },
};
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph, register, type LayoutConfig } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import mds from '@antv/g6-lite/layouts/mds';
import radial from '@antv/g6-lite/layouts/radial';
import GUI from 'lil-gui';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  register('layout', 'mds', mds);
  register('layout', 'radial', radial);
  // #region network-options
  const layouts: Record<string, LayoutConfig> = {
    radial: { type: 'radial', focusNode: '0', unitRadius: 68 },
    concentric: { type: 'concentric', sortBy: 'degree', nodeSize: 24 },
    force: { type: 'force', linkDistance: 100 },
    'd3-force': { type: 'd3-force', linkDistance: 100 },
    'force-atlas2': { type: 'force-atlas2', kr: 8, kg: 2 },
    fruchterman: { type: 'fruchterman', gravity: 12 },
    mds: { type: 'mds', linkDistance: 80 },
  };
  // #endregion network-options
  const connections = [
    ['0', '1'], ['0', '2'], ['0', '3'], ['1', '2'], ['1', '4'], ['1', '5'],
    ['2', '5'], ['2', '6'], ['3', '7'], ['3', '8'], ['3', '9'],
    ['7', '8'], ['8', '9'], ['4', '10'], ['4', '11'], ['10', '11'],
  ];
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: Array.from({ length: 12 }, (_, index) => ({ id: String(index) })),
      edges: connections.map(([source, target]) => ({ source, target })),
    },
    layout: layouts.radial,
    node: {
      style: {
        size: 24,
        label: (node) => node.id,
        labelPlacement: 'center',
        labelColor: '#fff',
        fill: (node) => node.id === '0' ? '#6d28d9' : '#1677ff',
      },
    },
    edge: { style: { lineWidth: 2 } },
    behaviors: ['zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas'],
    autoFit: { padding: 48, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  const panel = createDemoPanel(container);
  let revision = 0;
  const destroy = graph.destroy.bind(graph);
  graph.destroy = () => {
    revision++;
    panel.destroy();
    destroy();
  };

  try {
    await graph.render();
    panel.setStatus('radial ready');
    panel.addChoice('Layout', Object.keys(layouts), 'radial', async (type) => {
      const current = ++revision;
      panel.setStatus('Running…');
      graph.setLayout(layouts[type]);
      try {
        await graph.layout();
        if (current !== revision || graph.destroyed) return;
        graph.fitView({ padding: 48, maxZoom: 1 });
        panel.setStatus(`${type} ready`);
      } catch {
        if (current === revision && !graph.destroyed) panel.setStatus('Layout failed');
      }
    });
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}


export function createDemoPanel(container: string | HTMLElement, description = '') {
  const host = typeof container === 'string' ? document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(container)! : container;
  if (getComputedStyle(host).position === 'static') host.style.position = 'relative';

  let gui: GUI | undefined;
  const getGui = () => {
    if (!gui) {
      gui = new GUI({ container: host, width: 160 });
      gui.domElement.classList.add('g6lite-demo-controls');
      gui.domElement.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      Object.assign(gui.domElement.style, {
        position: 'absolute',
        top: '10px',
        right: '10px',
        zIndex: '30',
        maxWidth: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
        maxHeight: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
      });
    }
    return gui;
  };

  let status: HTMLDivElement | undefined;
  const setStatus = (message: string) => {
    if (!status) {
      status = document.createElement('div');
      status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
      status.dataset.role = 'status';
      status.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      status.style.cssText =
        'position:absolute;left:12px;bottom:10px;z-index:20;max-width:min(28rem,calc(100% - 24px));color:#64748b;font:12px/1.45 system-ui,sans-serif;pointer-events:none;white-space:pre-wrap;';
      host.append(status);
    }
    status.textContent = message;
  };
  if (description) setStatus(description);

  return {
    get gui() {
      return getGui();
    },
    addAction(label: string, action: () => void, folder = getGui()) {
      return folder.add({ [label]: action }, label);
    },
    addChoice<T extends string>(
      label: string,
      choices: readonly T[] | Record<string, T>,
      value: T,
      onChange: (value: T) => void,
    ) {
      const options = Array.isArray(choices) ? [...choices] : choices;
      return getGui().add({ value }, 'value', options).name(label).onChange(onChange);
    },
    setStatus,
    destroy() {
      gui?.destroy();
      status?.remove();
    },
  };
}
```



See the [layout reference](/en/docs/api/options#config-library-layout-fields) for force options, the [Worker guide](/en/docs/guides/layout-worker) for background computation, and the [layout gallery](/en/docs/examples/layout-gallery) for more examples.


# Layout overview (/en/docs/guides/layout-overview)





## What is a layout? [#what-is-a-layout]

A layout determines where nodes go. A workflow can run left to right, while a force-directed layout can bring connected nodes together. Omit `layout` to use the nodes’ existing `x` and `y` coordinates.

## Choose a layout [#choose-a-layout]

| Type                                                  | Description                                                               | Example configuration                                             |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`grid`](/en/docs/guides/layout-grid)                 | Arrange nodes in rows and columns.                                        | `{ type: 'grid', cols: 3 }`                                       |
| [`circular`](/en/docs/guides/layout-circular)         | Arrange nodes along a circle.                                             | `{ type: 'circular', radius: 100 }`                               |
| [`dagre`](/en/docs/guides/layout-dagre)               | Arrange steps or dependencies in layers.                                  | `{ type: 'dagre', rankdir: 'LR', ranksep: 80 }`                   |
| [`force`](/en/docs/guides/layout-force)               | Bring linked nodes closer while spacing nodes apart.                      | `{ type: 'force', linkDistance: 100 }`                            |
| [`d3-force`](/en/docs/guides/layout-d3-force)         | Arrange a network with D3 force simulation.                               | `{ type: 'd3-force', linkDistance: 100 }`                         |
| [`force-atlas2`](/en/docs/guides/layout-force-atlas2) | Use force simulation to reveal network clusters.                          | `{ type: 'force-atlas2', kr: 8, kg: 2 }`                          |
| [`fruchterman`](/en/docs/guides/layout-fruchterman)   | Spread nodes using attraction and repulsion.                              | `{ type: 'fruchterman', gravity: 12 }`                            |
| [`radial`](/en/docs/guides/layout-radial)             | **Optional.** Arrange nodes in rings by graph distance from a focal node. | `{ type: 'radial', focusNode: '0', unitRadius: 68 }`              |
| [`concentric`](/en/docs/guides/layout-concentric)     | Arrange nodes in concentric rings by degree.                              | `{ type: 'concentric', sortBy: 'degree' }`                        |
| [`mds`](/en/docs/guides/layout-mds)                   | **Optional.** Approximate graph distances in two dimensions.              | `{ type: 'mds', linkDistance: 80 }`                               |
| [`indented`](/en/docs/guides/layout-indented)         | **Optional.** Arrange a tree as an indented list.                         | `{ type: 'indented', indent: 80, rowHeight: 40 }`                 |
| [`mindmap`](/en/docs/guides/layout-mindmap)           | **Optional.** Arrange a tree as mind map branches.                        | `{ type: 'mindmap', levelGap: 120, nodeGap: 30 }`                 |
| [`fishbone`](/en/docs/guides/layout-fishbone)         | **Optional.** Arrange categories and items along a fishbone spine.        | `{ type: 'fishbone', categoryGap: 180 }`                          |
| [`random`](/en/docs/guides/layout-random)             | **Optional.** Scatter nodes randomly within an area.                      | `{ type: 'random', width: 800, height: 600, center: [400, 300] }` |

Pass these configuration objects to `layout`. See [Common layout options](/en/docs/guides/layout) for more parameters and previews.

## Optional layouts [#optional-layouts]

Indented, Mindmap, Fishbone, Radial, MDS, and Random require registration. With npm, import the layout from its own subpath, register it, and set `layout.type`.

```ts
import { register } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import radial from '@antv/g6-lite/layouts/radial';

register('layout', 'radial', radial);

const layout = { type: 'radial', focusNode: '0', unitRadius: 68 };
```

When using UMD from a CDN, load the same version of `dist/g6-lite-layouts.min.js` after the main script. The layout extensions are available on `G6LiteLayouts`.

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@antv/g6-lite@0.1.0/dist/g6-lite.min.js"></script>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@antv/g6-lite@0.1.0/dist/g6-lite-layouts.min.js"></script>
<script>
  G6Lite.register('layout', 'radial', G6LiteLayouts.radial);
</script>
```

Registered layouts run on the main thread.

## Configuration and example [#configuration-and-example]

Set the algorithm with `layout.type`. This example uses Dagre to arrange three steps from left to right.

```ts
import { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';

const graph = new Graph({
  container: '#container',
  data: {
    nodes: [{ id: 'Submit' }, { id: 'Review' }, { id: 'Publish' }],
    edges: [
      { source: 'Submit', target: 'Review' },
      { source: 'Review', target: 'Publish' },
    ],
  },
  layout: { type: 'dagre', rankdir: 'LR', ranksep: 80 },
  node: { style: { label: (node) => node.id } },
});

await graph.render();
```

Use **Layout** below to compare Grid, Circular, and Dagre on the same data. See [Network layouts](/en/docs/guides/layout-networks) for force-directed layouts.



```ts
const layouts: Record<string, LayoutConfig> = {
  grid: { type: 'grid', rows: 2, cols: 3, width: 360, height: 160 },
  circular: { type: 'circular', radius: 100 },
  dagre: { type: 'dagre', rankdir: 'LR', nodesep: 64, ranksep: 96, nodeSize: 28 },
};
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph, type LayoutConfig } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import GUI from 'lil-gui';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  // #region layout-options
  const layouts: Record<string, LayoutConfig> = {
    grid: { type: 'grid', rows: 2, cols: 3, width: 360, height: 160 },
    circular: { type: 'circular', radius: 100 },
    dagre: { type: 'dagre', rankdir: 'LR', nodesep: 64, ranksep: 96, nodeSize: 28 },
  };
  // #endregion layout-options
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E', 'F'].map((id) => ({ id })),
      edges: [
        { source: 'A', target: 'B' }, { source: 'A', target: 'C' },
        { source: 'B', target: 'D' }, { source: 'C', target: 'E' },
        { source: 'D', target: 'F' }, { source: 'E', target: 'F' },
      ],
    },
    layout: layouts.grid,
    node: { style: { size: 28, label: (node) => node.id, labelOffsetY: 8 } },
    behaviors: [],
    autoFit: { padding: 56, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  const ui = createDemoPanel(container);
  let generation = 0;
  const destroy = graph.destroy.bind(graph);
  graph.destroy = () => { generation++; ui.destroy(); destroy(); };
  try {
    await graph.render();
    ui.setStatus('grid ready');
    ui.addChoice('Layout', Object.keys(layouts), 'grid', async (value) => {
      const current = ++generation;
      ui.setStatus('Running…');
      graph.setLayout(layouts[value]);
      try {
        await graph.layout();
        if (current !== generation || graph.destroyed) return;
        graph.fitView({ padding: 56, maxZoom: 1 });
        ui.setStatus(`${value} ready`);
      } catch {
        if (current === generation && !graph.destroyed) ui.setStatus('Layout failed');
      }
    });
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}


export function createDemoPanel(container: string | HTMLElement, description = '') {
  const host = typeof container === 'string' ? document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(container)! : container;
  if (getComputedStyle(host).position === 'static') host.style.position = 'relative';

  let gui: GUI | undefined;
  const getGui = () => {
    if (!gui) {
      gui = new GUI({ container: host, width: 160 });
      gui.domElement.classList.add('g6lite-demo-controls');
      gui.domElement.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      Object.assign(gui.domElement.style, {
        position: 'absolute',
        top: '10px',
        right: '10px',
        zIndex: '30',
        maxWidth: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
        maxHeight: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
      });
    }
    return gui;
  };

  let status: HTMLDivElement | undefined;
  const setStatus = (message: string) => {
    if (!status) {
      status = document.createElement('div');
      status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
      status.dataset.role = 'status';
      status.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      status.style.cssText =
        'position:absolute;left:12px;bottom:10px;z-index:20;max-width:min(28rem,calc(100% - 24px));color:#64748b;font:12px/1.45 system-ui,sans-serif;pointer-events:none;white-space:pre-wrap;';
      host.append(status);
    }
    status.textContent = message;
  };
  if (description) setStatus(description);

  return {
    get gui() {
      return getGui();
    },
    addAction(label: string, action: () => void, folder = getGui()) {
      return folder.add({ [label]: action }, label);
    },
    addChoice<T extends string>(
      label: string,
      choices: readonly T[] | Record<string, T>,
      value: T,
      onChange: (value: T) => void,
    ) {
      const options = Array.isArray(choices) ? [...choices] : choices;
      return getGui().add({ value }, 'value', options).name(label).onChange(onChange);
    },
    setStatus,
    destroy() {
      gui?.destroy();
      status?.remove();
    },
  };
}
```



See [Common layout options](/en/docs/guides/layout) for parameters and runtime changes, or [Custom layouts](/en/docs/guides/custom-layout) to calculate your own coordinates.


# Radial layout (/en/docs/guides/layout-radial)





## Overview [#overview]

Place nodes in rings by shortest-path distance from a focal node.

## When to use it [#when-to-use-it]

Use it to see the direct and indirect relationships of an account, service, or device.

## Basic usage [#basic-usage]

This layout is optional. Import and register it before setting `layout.type`. For CDN usage, see [Optional layouts](/en/docs/guides/layout-overview#optional-layouts).

```ts
import { Graph, register } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import radial from '@antv/g6-lite/layouts/radial';

register('layout', 'radial', radial);

const graph = new Graph({
  container,
  data,
  layout: { type: 'radial' },
});
```

## Options [#options]

| Option           | Description                                                 | Type      | Default                |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | --------- | ---------------------- |
| `focusNode`      | ID of the focal node.                                       | `string`  | First node             |
| `unitRadius`     | Distance between neighboring rings.                         | `number`  | Computed automatically |
| `linkDistance`   | Reference edge length used by the layout.                   | `number`  | `50`                   |
| `preventOverlap` | Whether to try to prevent nodes in a ring from overlapping. | `boolean` | `false`                |

[Common layout options](/en/docs/guides/layout) · [Layout reference](/en/docs/api/options#config-library-layout-fields)

## Code example [#code-example]

The purple node `0` sits at the center, with 68 units between rings.



```ts
import { Graph, register, type GraphOptions, type LayoutConfig } from '@antv/g6-lite';

import radial from '@antv/g6-lite/layouts/radial';

type ExampleOptions = Pick<GraphOptions, 'data' | 'node' | 'edge'>;

function network(type: string): ExampleOptions {
  const links = [
    [0, 1], [0, 2], [0, 3], [1, 2], [1, 4], [1, 5],
    [2, 5], [2, 6], [3, 7], [3, 8], [3, 9],
    [7, 8], [8, 9], [4, 10], [4, 11], [10, 11],
  ];
  return {
    data: {
      nodes: Array.from({ length: 12 }, (_, index) => ({ id: String(index) })),
      edges: links.map(([source, target]) => ({ source: String(source), target: String(target) })),
    },
    node: {
      style: {
        size: 24,
        label: (node) => node.id,
        labelColor: '#fff',
        labelPlacement: 'center',
        fill: (node) => type === 'radial' && node.id === '0' ? '#6d28d9' : '#1677ff',
      },
    },
    edge: { style: { lineWidth: 2 } },
  };
}

async function render(container: HTMLElement, layout: LayoutConfig, options: ExampleOptions) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    ...options,
    layout,
    behaviors: ['drag-canvas', 'zoom-canvas'],
    autoFit: { padding: 36, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}

export function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  register('layout', 'radial', radial);
  const layout: LayoutConfig = { type: 'radial', focusNode: '0', unitRadius: 68 };
  return render(container, layout, network(layout.type));
}
```



[Compare network layouts](/en/docs/guides/layout-networks)


# Random layout (/en/docs/guides/layout-random)





## Overview [#overview]

Scatter nodes randomly around the layout center.

## When to use it [#when-to-use-it]

Use it for a quick preview of graph data. Each run samples new positions.

## Basic usage [#basic-usage]

This layout is optional. Import and register it before setting `layout.type`. For CDN usage, see [Optional layouts](/en/docs/guides/layout-overview#optional-layouts).

```ts
import { Graph, register } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import random from '@antv/g6-lite/layouts/random';

register('layout', 'random', random);

const graph = new Graph({
  container,
  data,
  layout: { type: 'random' },
});
```

## Options [#options]

| Option   | Description                                | Type               | Default                   |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------ | ------------------------- |
| `width`  | Controls the horizontal spread.            | `number`           | Canvas width              |
| `height` | Controls the vertical spread.              | `number`           | Canvas height             |
| `center` | Center of the spread in graph coordinates. | `[number, number]` | Center of the layout area |

[Common layout options](/en/docs/guides/layout) · [Layout reference](/en/docs/api/options#config-library-layout-fields)

## Code example [#code-example]

Nodes are scattered around `[200, 120]`. Reset the example to sample new positions.



```ts
import { Graph, register, type GraphOptions, type LayoutConfig } from '@antv/g6-lite';

import random from '@antv/g6-lite/layouts/random';

type ExampleOptions = Pick<GraphOptions, 'data' | 'node' | 'edge'>;

function arrangement(type: string): ExampleOptions {
  if (type === 'dagre') {
    return {
      data: {
        nodes: ['Input', 'Review', 'Check', 'Publish'].map((id) => ({ id })),
        edges: [
          { source: 'Input', target: 'Review' },
          { source: 'Input', target: 'Check' },
          { source: 'Review', target: 'Publish' },
          { source: 'Check', target: 'Publish' },
        ],
      },
      node: {
        type: 'rect',
        style: {
          width: 80, height: 32, borderRadius: 6,
          label: (node) => node.id, labelColor: '#fff', labelPlacement: 'center',
        },
      },
      edge: { type: 'polyline', style: { router: 'orth', radius: 12, endArrow: true } },
    };
  }

  const ids = Array.from({ length: type === 'grid' ? 6 : 8 }, (_, i) => String.fromCharCode(65 + i));
  return {
    data: {
      nodes: ids.map((id) => ({ id })),
      edges: type === 'grid' ? [] : ids.map((source, i) => ({ source, target: ids[(i + 2) % ids.length] })),
    },
    node: { style: { size: 24, label: (node) => node.id, labelColor: '#fff', labelPlacement: 'center' } },
  };
}

async function render(container: HTMLElement, layout: LayoutConfig, options: ExampleOptions) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    ...options,
    layout,
    behaviors: ['drag-canvas', 'zoom-canvas'],
    autoFit: { padding: 36, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}

export function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  register('layout', 'random', random);
  const layout: LayoutConfig = { type: 'random', width: 400, height: 240, center: [200, 120] };
  return render(container, layout, arrangement(layout.type));
}
```



[Browse the layout gallery](/en/docs/examples/layout-gallery)


# Tree layouts (/en/docs/guides/layout-trees)





## Choose a layout [#choose-a-layout]

Express parent-child relationships as edges with the parent as `source` and the child as `target`. Use one connected tree with a single root and no cycles.

| Goal                        | Layout and common options                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Mind map branches           | [`mindmap`](/en/docs/guides/layout-mindmap), with `levelGap` between levels and `nodeGap` between neighbors on the same side |
| Directory listing           | [`indented`](/en/docs/guides/layout-indented), with `indent` for indentation and `rowHeight` for row spacing                 |
| Root, categories, and items | [`fishbone`](/en/docs/guides/layout-fishbone), with `categoryGap` between categories along the spine                         |

## Configuration and example [#configuration-and-example]

Use **Tree layout** to compare the three arrangements. The example also changes the edge routing. Indented trees use elbow connectors, while the fishbone layout uses angled branches.

Register each tree layout before using it. [Optional layouts](/en/docs/guides/layout-overview#optional-layouts)



```ts
const layouts = {
  mindmap: {
    layout: {
      type: 'mindmap',
      direction: 'H',
      levelGap: 100,
      nodeGap: 24,
      getWidth: () => nodeSize,
      getHeight: (node: GraphNode) => node.id.length === 1 ? 64 : nodeSize,
      getSide: (node: GraphNode) => leftBranches.has(node.id[0]) ? 'left' : 'right',
    },
    edge: { type: 'line', style: { endArrow: false } },
  },
  indented: {
    layout: { type: 'indented', direction: 'LR', indent: 72, rowHeight: 30 },
    edge: { type: 'polyline', style: { router: 'indented', endArrow: false } },
  },
  fishbone: {
    layout: {
      type: 'fishbone',
      direction: 'LR',
      categoryGap: 156,
      categoryDistance: 130,
      itemHStep: 54,
      getWidth: () => nodeSize,
    },
    edge: { type: 'polyline', style: { router: 'fishbone', endArrow: false } },
  },
} satisfies Record<string, { layout: LayoutConfig; edge: EdgeConfig }>;
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph, register, type EdgeConfig, type GraphNode, type LayoutConfig } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import indented from '@antv/g6-lite/layouts/indented';
import mindmap from '@antv/g6-lite/layouts/mindmap';
import fishbone from '@antv/g6-lite/layouts/fishbone';
import GUI from 'lil-gui';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  register('layout', 'indented', indented);
  register('layout', 'mindmap', mindmap);
  register('layout', 'fishbone', fishbone);
  const nodeSize = 16;
  const leftBranches = new Set(['A', 'C']);
  // #region tree-layouts
  const layouts = {
    mindmap: {
      layout: {
        type: 'mindmap',
        direction: 'H',
        levelGap: 100,
        nodeGap: 24,
        getWidth: () => nodeSize,
        getHeight: (node: GraphNode) => node.id.length === 1 ? 64 : nodeSize,
        getSide: (node: GraphNode) => leftBranches.has(node.id[0]) ? 'left' : 'right',
      },
      edge: { type: 'line', style: { endArrow: false } },
    },
    indented: {
      layout: { type: 'indented', direction: 'LR', indent: 72, rowHeight: 30 },
      edge: { type: 'polyline', style: { router: 'indented', endArrow: false } },
    },
    fishbone: {
      layout: {
        type: 'fishbone',
        direction: 'LR',
        categoryGap: 156,
        categoryDistance: 130,
        itemHStep: 54,
        getWidth: () => nodeSize,
      },
      edge: { type: 'polyline', style: { router: 'fishbone', endArrow: false } },
    },
  } satisfies Record<string, { layout: LayoutConfig; edge: EdgeConfig }>;
  // #endregion tree-layouts
  const edges = ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D'].flatMap((branch) => [
    { source: 'Root', target: branch },
    { source: branch, target: `${branch}1` },
    { source: branch, target: `${branch}2` },
  ]);
  const edgeStyle = {
    stroke: '#8a9db7',
    lineWidth: 1.5,
  };
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: [{ id: 'Root' }, ...edges.map(({ target }) => ({ id: target }))],
      edges,
    },
    layout: layouts.mindmap.layout,
    edge: { ...layouts.mindmap.edge, style: { ...edgeStyle, ...layouts.mindmap.edge.style } },
    node: {
      style: {
        size: nodeSize,
        fill: (node) => node.id === 'Root' ? '#9860cf' : '#4c78db',
        label: (node) => node.id,
        labelOffsetY: 4,
      },
    },
    label: { hideOnLowZoom: false },
    behaviors: [],
    autoFit: { padding: 48, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  const ui = createDemoPanel(container);
  let generation = 0;
  const destroy = graph.destroy.bind(graph);
  graph.destroy = () => { generation++; ui.destroy(); destroy(); };
  try {
    await graph.render();
    ui.setStatus('mindmap ready');
    ui.addChoice('Tree layout', ['mindmap', 'indented', 'fishbone'] as const, 'mindmap', async (value) => {
      const current = ++generation;
      try {
        const { layout, edge } = layouts[value];
        graph.setLayout(layout);
        graph.updateOptions({
          edge,
          node: { style: { labelPlacement: value === 'indented' ? 'right' : 'bottom' } },
        });
        // Rebuild the render data so the router receives the new layout direction.
        await graph.render();
        if (current !== generation || graph.destroyed) return;
        ui.setStatus(`${value} ready`);
      } catch {
        if (current === generation && !graph.destroyed) ui.setStatus('Layout failed');
      }
    });
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}


export function createDemoPanel(container: string | HTMLElement, description = '') {
  const host = typeof container === 'string' ? document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(container)! : container;
  if (getComputedStyle(host).position === 'static') host.style.position = 'relative';

  let gui: GUI | undefined;
  const getGui = () => {
    if (!gui) {
      gui = new GUI({ container: host, width: 160 });
      gui.domElement.classList.add('g6lite-demo-controls');
      gui.domElement.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      Object.assign(gui.domElement.style, {
        position: 'absolute',
        top: '10px',
        right: '10px',
        zIndex: '30',
        maxWidth: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
        maxHeight: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
      });
    }
    return gui;
  };

  let status: HTMLDivElement | undefined;
  const setStatus = (message: string) => {
    if (!status) {
      status = document.createElement('div');
      status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
      status.dataset.role = 'status';
      status.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      status.style.cssText =
        'position:absolute;left:12px;bottom:10px;z-index:20;max-width:min(28rem,calc(100% - 24px));color:#64748b;font:12px/1.45 system-ui,sans-serif;pointer-events:none;white-space:pre-wrap;';
      host.append(status);
    }
    status.textContent = message;
  };
  if (description) setStatus(description);

  return {
    get gui() {
      return getGui();
    },
    addAction(label: string, action: () => void, folder = getGui()) {
      return folder.add({ [label]: action }, label);
    },
    addChoice<T extends string>(
      label: string,
      choices: readonly T[] | Record<string, T>,
      value: T,
      onChange: (value: T) => void,
    ) {
      const options = Array.isArray(choices) ? [...choices] : choices;
      return getGui().add({ value }, 'value', options).name(label).onChange(onChange);
    },
    setStatus,
    destroy() {
      gui?.destroy();
      status?.remove();
    },
  };
}
```



See the [tree layout reference](/en/docs/api/options#config-tree-layout-fields) for defaults and other options.


# Worker layout guide (/en/docs/guides/layout-worker)





A Worker moves layout computation off the main thread so the canvas can stay responsive. See [Common layout options](/en/docs/guides/layout) for algorithm parameters.

## Enable a Worker [#enable-a-worker]

```ts
layout: { type: 'force-atlas2', worker: true, maxIteration: 100 },
```

| layout.worker | Graph behavior                                                                                                                      |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Omitted       | Attempts a Worker at ≥ 1000 nodes; main thread below that threshold                                                                 |
| true          | Attempts a Worker for library layouts; registered extensions and three built-in tree layouts still execute on the main thread first |
| false         | Explicitly disables Workers, including for large graphs                                                                             |

Standalone runLayout has no node-count-based automatic switch. Worker failures fall back to the same main-thread algorithm. See the [layout reference](/en/docs/guides/layout#worker) for execution order and iteration defaults.

## Code and rendered result [#code-and-rendered-result]

The initial grid has 160 nodes. Run Worker requests ForceAtlas2; Grid restores the grid. Start + cancel starts a longer task, cancels after 20ms, then rearranges as a grid. The final status should remain cancelled → grid ready without being overwritten by stale results.



```ts
import { Graph, type LayoutConfig } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import GUI from 'lil-gui';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const grid: LayoutConfig = { type: 'grid', rows: 10, cols: 16, width: 400, height: 200, worker: false };
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: Array.from({ length: 160 }, (_, i) => ({ id: String(i) })),
      edges: Array.from({ length: 320 }, (_, i) => ({
        source: String(i % 160), target: String((i * 17 + 11) % 160),
      })).filter((edge) => edge.source !== edge.target),
    },
    layout: grid,
    node: { style: { size: 6 } },
    edge: { style: { endArrow: false, opacity: 0.2 } },
    behaviors: [],
    autoFit: { padding: 48, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  const ui = createDemoPanel(container);
  let generation = 0;
  let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
  const arrange = async (config: LayoutConfig, name: string) => {
    const current = ++generation;
    ui.setStatus(`${name} running`);
    graph.setLayout(config);
    try {
      await graph.layout();
      if (current !== generation || graph.destroyed) return;
      graph.fitView({ padding: 48, maxZoom: 1 });
      ui.setStatus(`${name} ready`);
    } catch {
      if (current === generation && !graph.destroyed) ui.setStatus('layout failed');
    }
  };
  const force = (maxIteration: number): LayoutConfig => ({
    type: 'force-atlas2', worker: true, maxIteration, barnesHut: true, prune: false,
  });
  const destroy = graph.destroy.bind(graph);
  graph.destroy = () => { generation++; clearTimeout(timer); ui.destroy(); destroy(); };
  try {
    await graph.render();
    ui.setStatus('grid ready');
    ui.addAction('Run Worker', () => {
      clearTimeout(timer);
      void arrange(force(80), 'worker requested');
    });
    ui.addAction('Start + cancel', () => {
      clearTimeout(timer);
      void arrange(force(2000), 'worker requested');
      timer = setTimeout(() => {
        graph.cancelLayout();
        void arrange(grid, 'cancelled → grid');
      }, 20);
    });
    ui.addAction('Grid', () => {
      clearTimeout(timer);
      graph.cancelLayout();
      void arrange(grid, 'grid');
    });
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}


export function createDemoPanel(container: string | HTMLElement, description = '') {
  const host = typeof container === 'string' ? document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(container)! : container;
  if (getComputedStyle(host).position === 'static') host.style.position = 'relative';

  let gui: GUI | undefined;
  const getGui = () => {
    if (!gui) {
      gui = new GUI({ container: host, width: 160 });
      gui.domElement.classList.add('g6lite-demo-controls');
      gui.domElement.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      Object.assign(gui.domElement.style, {
        position: 'absolute',
        top: '10px',
        right: '10px',
        zIndex: '30',
        maxWidth: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
        maxHeight: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
      });
    }
    return gui;
  };

  let status: HTMLDivElement | undefined;
  const setStatus = (message: string) => {
    if (!status) {
      status = document.createElement('div');
      status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
      status.dataset.role = 'status';
      status.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      status.style.cssText =
        'position:absolute;left:12px;bottom:10px;z-index:20;max-width:min(28rem,calc(100% - 24px));color:#64748b;font:12px/1.45 system-ui,sans-serif;pointer-events:none;white-space:pre-wrap;';
      host.append(status);
    }
    status.textContent = message;
  };
  if (description) setStatus(description);

  return {
    get gui() {
      return getGui();
    },
    addAction(label: string, action: () => void, folder = getGui()) {
      return folder.add({ [label]: action }, label);
    },
    addChoice<T extends string>(
      label: string,
      choices: readonly T[] | Record<string, T>,
      value: T,
      onChange: (value: T) => void,
    ) {
      const options = Array.isArray(choices) ? [...choices] : choices;
      return getGui().add({ value }, 'value', options).name(label).onChange(onChange);
    },
    setStatus,
    destroy() {
      gui?.destroy();
      status?.remove();
    },
  };
}
```



Completion indicates that the layout call finished. Check assets and threads below to establish whether a Worker actually ran.

## Transfer and fallback [#transfer-and-fallback]

Worker layout configuration, node data, and edge data must be structured-cloneable. Functions, DOM nodes, and similar values can make transfer fail. Explicitly use worker: false for algorithm callbacks. Node and edge style functions are not part of this transfer and can still control rendering.

The Worker receives only node id/x/y/data and edge source/target/data. Graph handles fx/fy when applying results; do not depend on omitted fields inside the Worker algorithm.

Creation, asset loading, postMessage cloning, or computation failures can trigger main-thread fallback. worker: true, layout:end, or a resolved await alone does not establish which thread performed computation.

## Cancellation and cleanup [#cancellation-and-cleanup]

After rendering, graph.cancelLayout() can terminate that instance's active Worker and discard results. It neither rolls back completed layouts nor affects another Graph's Worker. To continue, setLayout again and await layout.

The example's generation check also protects application-side completion messages and fitView from stale calls. Call graph.destroy() on unmount, and clean up your own controls, timers, and subscriptions.

## Deploy and verify [#deploy-and-verify]

1. npm ESM output includes layoutWorker.js and dependencies. Preserve their relative paths rather than deploying index.js alone.
2. Your bundler must recognize the module Worker's new URL entry. In Network, check successful Worker and algorithm asset requests with JavaScript responses, not an HTML fallback page.
3. Confirm a Worker in developer tools' thread list. For CSP-restricted applications, configure worker-src and script policy for actual asset origins; successful layout alone is insufficient.
4. The current UMD entry does not guarantee usable standalone Worker assets and can fall back. Prefer ESM and verify emitted assets when off-thread execution is required.

## Common questions [#common-questions]

### Why does the page still stall? [#why-does-the-page-still-stall]

Check for main-thread fallback, then measure computation and drawing separately. Transfer, rendering, and many labels are not eliminated by the worker option. Limit iterations and test representative data.

### Why do callbacks behave differently on small and large graphs? [#why-do-callbacks-behave-differently-on-small-and-large-graphs]

Large graphs can automatically attempt a Worker. Functions in layout configuration cannot be cloned, causing fallback. Explicitly disable Workers when callbacks are required to keep the path predictable.

### Does cancelLayout throw AbortError? [#does-cancellayout-throw-aborterror]

Graph discards cancelled task results; ordinary cancellation usually does not surface as an AbortError. A resolved Promise does not prove positions were applied. Check application task generations or destroyed state too.

Continue with the [Layout guide](/en/docs/guides/layout), [layout methods](/en/docs/api/graph#layout), or [Performance tuning](/en/docs/metrics/performance#performance-tuning).

**Related runnable examples**

* [Worker layout](/en/docs/examples/layout-worker)


# Common layout options (/en/docs/guides/layout)

































Configure the layout in `new Graph()` through `layout`. See the [Layout overview](/en/docs/guides/layout-overview) to choose an algorithm.

## LayoutConfig [#choose-a-layout]

| Field             | Purpose                                             |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `type`            | Algorithm name, such as `dagre`                     |
| `width`, `height` | Computation bounds, defaulting to canvas dimensions |
| `center`          | Layout center for algorithms that use it            |
| `worker`          | Whether to try computing in a Worker                |

Direction and spacing depend on the algorithm. See the [layout reference](/en/docs/api/options#options-layout) for defaults and types.

<span id="supported-layout-types" />

## Supported layouts [#supported-layouts]

The thumbnails show 11 layouts on the same data. Try them in the [layout gallery](/en/docs/examples/layout-gallery) or see the [AntV Layout documentation](https://layout.antv.vision/) for more options.

Layouts marked **Optional** must be imported and registered. See [Optional layouts](/en/docs/guides/layout-overview#optional-layouts).

<div className="effect-table">
  | type                                                  | Preview                                                                                  | Purpose                                      | Common algorithm options                                                       |
  | ----------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
  | [`circular`](/en/docs/guides/layout-circular)         |   <img alt="Nodes are evenly spaced on a circle" src="__img0" />                         | Circle or spiral                             | radius, startRadius, endRadius, startAngle, endAngle, clockwise                |
  | [`concentric`](/en/docs/guides/layout-concentric)     |   <img alt="Nodes are arranged in rings by degree" src="__img1" />                       | Rings by importance                          | sortBy, maxLevelDiff, nodeSize, nodeSpacing, preventOverlap                    |
  | [`grid`](/en/docs/guides/layout-grid)                 |   <img alt="Nodes align in rows and columns" src="__img2" />                             | Rows and columns                             | rows, cols, begin, sortBy, nodeSize, nodeSpacing, preventOverlap               |
  | [`random`](/en/docs/guides/layout-random)             |   <img alt="Nodes are scattered across the canvas" src="__img3" />                       | **Optional.** Random positions               | width, height, center                                                          |
  | [`dagre`](/en/docs/guides/layout-dagre)               |   <img alt="The directed graph is layered from left to right" src="__img4" />            | Directed layers                              | rankdir: TB/BT/LR/RL, nodesep, ranksep, edgesep, nodeSize, ranker              |
  | [`force`](/en/docs/guides/layout-force)               |   <img alt="Connected nodes are drawn together by the force simulation" src="__img5" />  | Force-directed network                       | linkDistance, nodeStrength, edgeStrength, maxIteration, minMovement            |
  | [`d3-force`](/en/docs/guides/layout-d3-force)         |   <img alt="Node positions from the D3 force simulation" src="__img6" />                 | D3 simulation                                | linkDistance, nodeStrength, alphaDecay, alphaMin; use nodeStrength, not charge |
  | [`force-atlas2`](/en/docs/guides/layout-force-atlas2) |   <img alt="Node positions from ForceAtlas2" src="__img7" />                             | ForceAtlas2 network                          | kr, kg, barnesHut, prune, maxIteration                                         |
  | [`fruchterman`](/en/docs/guides/layout-fruchterman)   |   <img alt="Node positions from Fruchterman" src="__img8" />                             | Fruchterman network                          | gravity, speed, maxIteration, minMovement                                      |
  | [`radial`](/en/docs/guides/layout-radial)             |   <img alt="Nodes form rings by graph distance from the focus" src="__img9" />           | **Optional.** Rings around a focus           | focusNode, unitRadius, linkDistance, preventOverlap                            |
  | [`mds`](/en/docs/guides/layout-mds)                   |   <img alt="Graph distances determine node positions in two dimensions" src="__img10" /> | **Optional.** Positions from graph distances | linkDistance, center                                                           |
</div>

Rendered node sizes are not automatically passed to algorithms. For overlap avoidance, also set the algorithm's nodeSize/nodeSpacing or equivalent options; preventOverlap alone does not ensure agreement with drawn sizes.

### Computation defaults [#computation-defaults]

G6Lite injects or rewrites the following options; explicit values win. These rules apply to library layouts, not the three functional tree layouts.

| Algorithm / option                         | Default or rule                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| All library layouts: `animate`             | false when omitted; Graph applies positions after computation rather than drawing every iteration                                  |
| `iterations`                               | Mapped to maxIteration only when maxIteration is absent, then removed. It is not a universal iteration control for every algorithm |
| force / fruchterman, fewer than 1000 nodes | maxIteration: 100, minMovement: 1                                                                                                  |
| force / fruchterman, 1000–5000 nodes       | maxIteration: 200, minMovement: 1.5                                                                                                |
| force / fruchterman, more than 5000 nodes  | maxIteration: 50, minMovement: 2                                                                                                   |
| force-atlas2                               | barnesHut: true; prune defaults to false above 200 nodes; maxIteration: 100, or 50 above 5000 nodes                                |
| d3-force                                   | alphaDecay: 0.1; linkDistance: max(200, √node count × 80)                                                                          |

Main-thread d3-force is ticked manually up to 300 times, checking alphaMin (default 0.001). The Worker path awaits the algorithm's completion; the paths do not guarantee identical positions. Other internal defaults belong to the installed algorithm version.

<span id="preview" />

## Preview [#options-layout-code-and-rendered-result]

Use **Layout** to compare Grid, Circular, and Dagre on the same data. The code shows the parameters for each layout.



```ts
const layouts: Record<string, LayoutConfig> = {
  grid: { type: 'grid', rows: 2, cols: 3, width: 360, height: 160 },
  circular: { type: 'circular', radius: 100 },
  dagre: { type: 'dagre', rankdir: 'LR', nodesep: 64, ranksep: 96, nodeSize: 28 },
};
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph, type LayoutConfig } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import GUI from 'lil-gui';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  // #region layout-options
  const layouts: Record<string, LayoutConfig> = {
    grid: { type: 'grid', rows: 2, cols: 3, width: 360, height: 160 },
    circular: { type: 'circular', radius: 100 },
    dagre: { type: 'dagre', rankdir: 'LR', nodesep: 64, ranksep: 96, nodeSize: 28 },
  };
  // #endregion layout-options
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E', 'F'].map((id) => ({ id })),
      edges: [
        { source: 'A', target: 'B' }, { source: 'A', target: 'C' },
        { source: 'B', target: 'D' }, { source: 'C', target: 'E' },
        { source: 'D', target: 'F' }, { source: 'E', target: 'F' },
      ],
    },
    layout: layouts.grid,
    node: { style: { size: 28, label: (node) => node.id, labelOffsetY: 8 } },
    behaviors: [],
    autoFit: { padding: 56, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  const ui = createDemoPanel(container);
  let generation = 0;
  const destroy = graph.destroy.bind(graph);
  graph.destroy = () => { generation++; ui.destroy(); destroy(); };
  try {
    await graph.render();
    ui.setStatus('grid ready');
    ui.addChoice('Layout', Object.keys(layouts), 'grid', async (value) => {
      const current = ++generation;
      ui.setStatus('Running…');
      graph.setLayout(layouts[value]);
      try {
        await graph.layout();
        if (current !== generation || graph.destroyed) return;
        graph.fitView({ padding: 56, maxZoom: 1 });
        ui.setStatus(`${value} ready`);
      } catch {
        if (current === generation && !graph.destroyed) ui.setStatus('Layout failed');
      }
    });
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}


export function createDemoPanel(container: string | HTMLElement, description = '') {
  const host = typeof container === 'string' ? document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(container)! : container;
  if (getComputedStyle(host).position === 'static') host.style.position = 'relative';

  let gui: GUI | undefined;
  const getGui = () => {
    if (!gui) {
      gui = new GUI({ container: host, width: 160 });
      gui.domElement.classList.add('g6lite-demo-controls');
      gui.domElement.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      Object.assign(gui.domElement.style, {
        position: 'absolute',
        top: '10px',
        right: '10px',
        zIndex: '30',
        maxWidth: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
        maxHeight: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
      });
    }
    return gui;
  };

  let status: HTMLDivElement | undefined;
  const setStatus = (message: string) => {
    if (!status) {
      status = document.createElement('div');
      status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
      status.dataset.role = 'status';
      status.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      status.style.cssText =
        'position:absolute;left:12px;bottom:10px;z-index:20;max-width:min(28rem,calc(100% - 24px));color:#64748b;font:12px/1.45 system-ui,sans-serif;pointer-events:none;white-space:pre-wrap;';
      host.append(status);
    }
```
