# Plugin overview (/en/docs/guides/plugins)





## What is a plugin? [#what-is-a-plugin]

A plugin adds a separate feature to a graph, such as a statistics panel or an application toolbar.

## Built-in plugins [#built-in-plugins]

G6Lite has no built-in plugins. Use the [`tooltip` behavior](/en/docs/guides/behaviors#tooltip) for tooltips and the [theme](/en/docs/guides/theme) for the canvas background. To add your own panel, [write a custom plugin](/en/docs/guides/custom-plugin).

## Configuration [#configure-a-plugin]

### Basic configuration [#basic-configuration]

Register the plugin and use its registered name as `type` in `plugins`. The [custom plugin guide](/en/docs/guides/custom-plugin) implements the `createCounter` factory used here.

```ts
import { Graph, register } from '@antv/g6-lite';

register('plugin', 'docs-counter', createCounter);

const graph = new Graph({
  container,
  data,
  plugins: [{ type: 'docs-counter' }],
});

await graph.render();
```

### Configure plugin options [#configure-plugin-options]

Put plugin options alongside `type`. This example uses `caption` to set the counter title. Click a node or **Plugin +1** to increment the count.



```ts
plugins: [{
  type: NAME, caption: 'Clicks',
  subscribe(listener: () => void) {
    graph.on('node:click', listener);
    return () => graph.off('node:click', listener);
  },
  onRenderAgain() { void graph.render().catch(console.error); },
} satisfies CounterOptions],
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph, register, type PluginExtension, type PluginOptions } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import GUI from 'lil-gui';

const NAME = 'docs-counter' as const;
interface CounterOptions extends PluginOptions<typeof NAME> {
  caption?: string;
  subscribe?: (listener: () => void) => () => void;
  onRenderAgain?: () => void;
}
// #region plugin
export function createCounter(): PluginExtension<CounterOptions> {
  let ui: ReturnType<typeof createDemoPanel> | undefined;
  let unsubscribe: (() => void) | undefined;
  let settings: CounterOptions | undefined;
  let count = 0;
  const report = () => ui?.setStatus(`${settings?.caption ?? 'Clicks'}: ${count}`);
  const increment = () => { count++; report(); };
  return {
    init(_context, options) { settings = options; },
    mount(container) {
      ui = createDemoPanel(container);
      ui.addAction('Plugin +1', increment);
      if (settings?.onRenderAgain) ui.addAction('Render again', settings.onRenderAgain);
      report();
      unsubscribe = settings?.subscribe?.(increment);
    },
    destroy() {
      unsubscribe?.(); unsubscribe = undefined;
      ui?.destroy();
      ui = undefined;
      settings = undefined;
    },
  };
}
register('plugin', NAME, () => createCounter());
// #endregion plugin

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: { nodes: [{ id: 'A', x: 0, y: 0 }, { id: 'B', x: 200, y: 0 }], edges: [] },
    node: { style: { size: 32, label: (node) => node.id } },
    // #region activate
    plugins: [{
      type: NAME, caption: 'Clicks',
      subscribe(listener: () => void) {
        graph.on('node:click', listener);
        return () => graph.off('node:click', listener);
      },
      onRenderAgain() { void graph.render().catch(console.error); },
    } satisfies CounterOptions],
    // #endregion activate
    behaviors: ['zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas'],
    autoFit: { padding: 64, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  try { await graph.render(); return graph; }
  catch (error) { graph.destroy(); throw error; }
}


export function createDemoPanel(container: string | HTMLElement, description = '') {
  const host = typeof container === 'string' ? document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(container)! : container;
  if (getComputedStyle(host).position === 'static') host.style.position = 'relative';

  let gui: GUI | undefined;
  const getGui = () => {
    if (!gui) {
      gui = new GUI({ container: host, width: 160 });
      gui.domElement.classList.add('g6lite-demo-controls');
      gui.domElement.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      Object.assign(gui.domElement.style, {
        position: 'absolute',
        top: '10px',
        right: '10px',
        zIndex: '30',
        maxWidth: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
        maxHeight: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
      });
    }
    return gui;
  };

  let status: HTMLDivElement | undefined;
  const setStatus = (message: string) => {
    if (!status) {
      status = document.createElement('div');
      status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
      status.dataset.role = 'status';
      status.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      status.style.cssText =
        'position:absolute;left:12px;bottom:10px;z-index:20;max-width:min(28rem,calc(100% - 24px));color:#64748b;font:12px/1.45 system-ui,sans-serif;pointer-events:none;white-space:pre-wrap;';
      host.append(status);
    }
    status.textContent = message;
  };
  if (description) setStatus(description);

  return {
    get gui() {
      return getGui();
    },
    addAction(label: string, action: () => void, folder = getGui()) {
      return folder.add({ [label]: action }, label);
    },
    addChoice<T extends string>(
      label: string,
      choices: readonly T[] | Record<string, T>,
      value: T,
      onChange: (value: T) => void,
    ) {
      const options = Array.isArray(choices) ? [...choices] : choices;
      return getGui().add({ value }, 'value', options).name(label).onChange(onChange);
    },
    setStatus,
    destroy() {
      gui?.destroy();
      status?.remove();
    },
  };
}
```



### Replace a plugin or its options [#replace-a-plugin-or-its-options]

Set `plugins` when you create the graph. To replace a plugin or change its options, destroy the old graph and create a graph with the new configuration.

### Mount and unmount [#mount-and-unmount]

| Operation                       | What happens to plugins                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `await graph.render()`          | Mounts plugins on first render and remounts them on subsequent calls. Click **Render again** in the example to reset the count. |
| `await graph.setData(nextData)` | Updates graph data while plugins keep running.                                                                                  |
| `graph.destroy()`               | Destroys the graph and calls each plugin's `destroy()` to release its resources.                                                |

## Custom plugins [#custom-plugins]

The [custom plugin guide](/en/docs/guides/custom-plugin) uses the same counter to show how to create the panel, listen for node clicks, and clean up on unmount. For configuration fields, see the [plugin options reference](/en/docs/api/options#plugins).


# Element states (/en/docs/guides/states)





States record whether an element is selected, highlighted, or marked by your application. One element can have several states, such as selected and awaiting review.

## States, Behaviors, and styles [#states-behaviors-and-styles]

* A **state** records a current flag, such as selected.
* A **Behavior** decides when to change it, such as click-select responding to clicks.
* A **state style** decides its appearance, such as a purple selected outline.

Listening to node:click does not select nodes; defining stateStyles does not create an interaction. Behaviors and application code can both change states.

## Built-in states [#names-and-data]

| State       | Meaning             | Use case                                                                       |
| ----------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `default`   | Base appearance     | Display an element with its base styles                                        |
| `selected`  | Selection           | Mark nodes, edges, or Combos the user has selected                             |
| `active`    | Activation          | Emphasize the element currently being interacted with                          |
| `highlight` | Highlighting        | Emphasize search results or related paths                                      |
| `inactive`  | De-emphasis         | Dim elements outside the current focus                                         |
| `disabled`  | Disabled appearance | Show an unavailable element and enforce interaction limits in application code |
| `hidden`    | Visibility          | Hide an element temporarily                                                    |

Clear the states to restore base styling. To show elements hidden by a collapsed Combo, expand the Combo. See the [side-by-side state examples](/en/docs/elements/overview#element-states).

## Configure state styles [#where-state-styles-belong]

### Basic configuration [#basic-configuration]

Use `node.stateStyles` for nodes, `edge.stateStyles` for edges, and `combo.style.stateStyles` for Combos. In the `new Graph()` options, set the fields each named state overrides. Other fields keep their base values or values from other applied states.

```ts
const stateOptions = {
  node: { stateStyles: { selected: { stroke: '#6d28d9', strokeWidth: 3 } } },
  edge: { stateStyles: { highlight: { stroke: '#008765', lineWidth: 3 } } },
  combo: { style: { stateStyles: { selected: { stroke: '#6d28d9', strokeWidth: 2 } } } },
};
```

### Custom states [#try-state-changes]

Set `fill` in `node.stateStyles.review` to mark nodes awaiting review in orange. A starts selected. Click **Toggle review** to add an orange fill while keeping its purple outline. **Replace with highlight** switches A to green highlighting. **Clear A** removes its states.



```ts
const toggle = (state: ElementState) => {
  const enabled = graph.getItemStates('A').includes(state);
  graph.setItemState('A', state, !enabled);
};
const replace = () => graph.setElementStates('A', ['highlight']);
const clear = () => graph.clearItemStates('A');
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph, type ElementState } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import GUI from 'lil-gui';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: [{ id: 'A', x: 0, y: 0, states: ['selected'] }, { id: 'B', x: 220, y: 0 }],
      edges: [{ id: 'A-B', source: 'A', target: 'B' }],
    },
    node: {
      style: { size: 34, label: (node) => node.id, labelOffsetY: 10 },
      // #region state-styles
      stateStyles: {
        selected: { stroke: '#6D28D9', strokeWidth: 3 },
        review: { fill: '#F59E0B' },
        highlight: { fill: '#00A876', stroke: '#005C41', strokeWidth: 2 },
      },
      // #endregion state-styles
    },
    behaviors: [],
    autoFit: { padding: 60, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  // #region states
  const toggle = (state: ElementState) => {
    const enabled = graph.getItemStates('A').includes(state);
    graph.setItemState('A', state, !enabled);
  };
  const replace = () => graph.setElementStates('A', ['highlight']);
  const clear = () => graph.clearItemStates('A');
  // #endregion states
  const ui = createDemoPanel(container);
  const status = document.createElement('div');
  status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
  status.style.cssText = 'position:absolute;left:12px;bottom:12px;right:12px;padding:8px;background:white;color:#334155;font:12px/1.6 system-ui;pointer-events:none;z-index:20;';
  const update = () => {
    status.textContent = `A: [${graph.getItemStates('A').join(', ')}] | B: [${graph.getItemStates('B').join(', ')}]`;
  };
  const actions: Array<[string, () => void]> = [
    ['Toggle selected', () => toggle('selected')],
    ['Toggle review', () => toggle('review')],
    ['Replace with highlight', replace],
    ['Clear A', clear],
  ];
  const destroy = graph.destroy.bind(graph);
  graph.destroy = () => {
    ui.destroy();
    status.remove();
    destroy();
  };
  try {
    await graph.render();
    update();
    for (const [label, action] of actions) {
      ui.addAction(label, () => { action(); update(); });
    }
    container.append(status);
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}


export function createDemoPanel(container: string | HTMLElement, description = '') {
  const host = typeof container === 'string' ? document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(container)! : container;
  if (getComputedStyle(host).position === 'static') host.style.position = 'relative';

  let gui: GUI | undefined;
  const getGui = () => {
    if (!gui) {
      gui = new GUI({ container: host, width: 160 });
      gui.domElement.classList.add('g6lite-demo-controls');
      gui.domElement.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      Object.assign(gui.domElement.style, {
        position: 'absolute',
        top: '10px',
        right: '10px',
        zIndex: '30',
        maxWidth: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
        maxHeight: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
      });
    }
    return gui;
  };

  let status: HTMLDivElement | undefined;
  const setStatus = (message: string) => {
    if (!status) {
      status = document.createElement('div');
      status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
      status.dataset.role = 'status';
      status.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      status.style.cssText =
        'position:absolute;left:12px;bottom:10px;z-index:20;max-width:min(28rem,calc(100% - 24px));color:#64748b;font:12px/1.45 system-ui,sans-serif;pointer-events:none;white-space:pre-wrap;';
      host.append(status);
    }
    status.textContent = message;
  };
  if (description) setStatus(description);

  return {
    get gui() {
      return getGui();
    },
    addAction(label: string, action: () => void, folder = getGui()) {
      return folder.add({ [label]: action }, label);
    },
    addChoice<T extends string>(
      label: string,
      choices: readonly T[] | Record<string, T>,
      value: T,
      onChange: (value: T) => void,
    ) {
      const options = Array.isArray(choices) ? [...choices] : choices;
      return getGui().add({ value }, 'value', options).name(label).onChange(onChange);
    },
    setStatus,
    destroy() {
      gui?.destroy();
      status?.remove();
    },
  };
}
```



Nodes and edges can use custom state names for styling. Combo style overrides use the supported built-in states. See [Combo state styles](/en/docs/guides/combo#options-combo-state-styles).

## Set element states [#set-element-states]

### Set initial states in data [#set-initial-states-in-data]

Declare initial states in the `states` array on a node, edge, or Combo. In this example, A and Storage start selected, and the A–B edge starts highlighted.

```ts
const data = {
  nodes: [
    { id: 'A', x: 0, y: 0, states: ['selected'] },
    { id: 'B', x: 160, y: 0, comboId: 'storage' },
  ],
  edges: [{ id: 'A-B', source: 'A', target: 'B', states: ['highlight'] }],
  combos: [{ id: 'storage', states: ['selected'] }],
};
```

### Update states at runtime [#add-business-flags-without-losing-selection]

After the initial `await graph.render()`, use `setItemState()` to add one state and preserve the others. Use `setElementStates()` to replace the complete state set for each supplied element.

```ts
graph.setItemState('A', 'review', true);
graph.setElementStates('A', ['selected', 'review']);
graph.setElementStates({ A: ['selected'], 'A-B': ['highlight'], storage: ['selected'] });
```

### Add or remove states in a batch [#batch-changes-and-combos]

Use `batchSetState()` to update specific states on several elements in one operation. The remaining states stay in place.

```ts
graph.batchSetState([
  { id: 'A', state: 'review', value: true },
  { id: 'A-B', state: 'highlight', value: true },
  { id: 'storage', state: 'selected', value: true },
]);
```

### Combine state styles [#combine-state-styles]

Nodes and edges apply styles in state order. When multiple states define the same field, the later one wins. For example, `['selected', 'review']` can apply a selection outline and a review fill together. Combos use the fixed order `active → highlight → selected → disabled → inactive`. See the [node](/en/docs/guides/node#options-node-state-styles), [edge](/en/docs/guides/edge#options-edge-state-styles), and [Combo](/en/docs/guides/combo#options-combo-state-styles) options.

### Combine click selection and hover highlighting [#combine-click-selection-and-hover-highlighting]

The next example uses `click-select` for selection and `hover-highlight` to emphasize related elements. Click selection uses a purple outline, and hover highlighting uses green. Use a custom state such as `review` for a persistent business flag. See [selection synchronization](/en/docs/guides/events/selection-drag#synchronize-selection) to connect application panels.

### Preserve selection when replacing data [#preserve-selection-when-replacing-data]

Click A, then Shift-click B and the horizontal A–C edge. Choose **Keep selected**. A and A–C stay selected, B is removed with the old data, and the new node D uses its base style. Reset the example, select elements again, and choose **Reload data** to compare a direct replacement.



```ts
const reload = async (keepSelected: boolean) => {
  const nodes = new Set(keepSelected ? graph.findNodesByState('selected') : []);
  const edges = new Set(keepSelected ? graph.findEdgesByState('selected') : []);
  const next = nextData();
  await graph.setData({
    ...next,
    nodes: next.nodes.map((node) => ({
      ...node, states: nodes.has(node.id) ? ['selected'] : [],
    })),
    edges: next.edges.map((edge) => ({
      ...edge, states: edge.id && edges.has(edge.id) ? ['selected'] : [],
    })),
  }, { fitView: false });
};
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph, type GraphData } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import GUI from 'lil-gui';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: [{ id: 'A', x: 0, y: 0 }, { id: 'B', x: 160, y: 80 }, { id: 'C', x: 320, y: 0 }],
      edges: [{ id: 'A-B', source: 'A', target: 'B' }, { id: 'A-C', source: 'A', target: 'C' }],
    },
    node: {
      style: { size: 32, label: (node) => node.id, labelOffsetY: 10 },
      stateStyles: {
        selected: { stroke: '#6D28D9', strokeWidth: 3 },
        highlight: { fill: '#00A876' },
      },
    },
    edge: {
      style: { hitAreaWidth: 12 },
      stateStyles: {
        selected: { stroke: '#6D28D9', lineWidth: 3 },
        highlight: { stroke: '#00A876', lineWidth: 2 },
      },
    },
    behaviors: [
      { type: 'click-select', multiple: true, trigger: 'shift' },
      { type: 'hover-highlight', degree: 1 },
    ],
    autoFit: { padding: 60, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  const nextData = (): GraphData => ({
    nodes: [{ id: 'A', x: 0, y: 0 }, { id: 'C', x: 320, y: 0 }, { id: 'D', x: 160, y: 80 }],
    edges: [{ id: 'A-C', source: 'A', target: 'C' }, { id: 'C-D', source: 'C', target: 'D' }],
  });
  // #region preserve-selection
  const reload = async (keepSelected: boolean) => {
    const nodes = new Set(keepSelected ? graph.findNodesByState('selected') : []);
    const edges = new Set(keepSelected ? graph.findEdgesByState('selected') : []);
    const next = nextData();
    await graph.setData({
      ...next,
      nodes: next.nodes.map((node) => ({
        ...node, states: nodes.has(node.id) ? ['selected'] : [],
      })),
      edges: next.edges.map((edge) => ({
        ...edge, states: edge.id && edges.has(edge.id) ? ['selected'] : [],
      })),
    }, { fitView: false });
  };
  // #endregion preserve-selection
  const ui = createDemoPanel(container);
  const status = document.createElement('div');
  status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
  status.style.cssText = 'position:absolute;left:12px;bottom:12px;right:12px;padding:8px;background:white;color:#334155;font:12px/1.6 system-ui;white-space:pre-line;pointer-events:none;z-index:20;';
  let version = 1;
  let disposed = false;
  const update = () => {
    status.textContent = `data v${version} | selected nodes: ${graph.findNodesByState('selected').join(', ') || 'none'}\nselected edges: ${graph.findEdgesByState('selected').join(', ') || 'none'}`;
  };
  const events = ['node:selectchange', 'edge:selectchange', 'selection:clear'] as const;
  for (const event of events) graph.on(event, update);
  const destroy = graph.destroy.bind(graph);
  graph.destroy = () => {
    disposed = true;
    for (const event of events) graph.off(event, update);
    ui.destroy();
    status.remove();
    destroy();
  };
  try {
    await graph.render();
    update();
    const buttons = [false, true].map((keep) => ui.addAction(keep ? 'Keep selected' : 'Reload data', async () => {
        for (const item of buttons) item.disable();
        try {
          await reload(keep);
          if (!disposed) { version++; update(); }
        } catch {
          if (!disposed) status.textContent = 'Reload failed';
        } finally {
          if (!disposed) for (const item of buttons) item.enable();
        }
    }));
    container.append(status);
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}


export function createDemoPanel(container: string | HTMLElement, description = '') {
  const host = typeof container === 'string' ? document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(container)! : container;
  if (getComputedStyle(host).position === 'static') host.style.position = 'relative';

  let gui: GUI | undefined;
  const getGui = () => {
    if (!gui) {
      gui = new GUI({ container: host, width: 160 });
      gui.domElement.classList.add('g6lite-demo-controls');
      gui.domElement.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      Object.assign(gui.domElement.style, {
        position: 'absolute',
        top: '10px',
        right: '10px',
        zIndex: '30',
        maxWidth: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
        maxHeight: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
      });
    }
    return gui;
  };

  let status: HTMLDivElement | undefined;
  const setStatus = (message: string) => {
    if (!status) {
      status = document.createElement('div');
      status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
      status.dataset.role = 'status';
      status.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      status.style.cssText =
        'position:absolute;left:12px;bottom:10px;z-index:20;max-width:min(28rem,calc(100% - 24px));color:#64748b;font:12px/1.45 system-ui,sans-serif;pointer-events:none;white-space:pre-wrap;';
      host.append(status);
    }
    status.textContent = message;
  };
  if (description) setStatus(description);

  return {
    get gui() {
      return getGui();
    },
    addAction(label: string, action: () => void, folder = getGui()) {
      return folder.add({ [label]: action }, label);
    },
    addChoice<T extends string>(
      label: string,
      choices: readonly T[] | Record<string, T>,
      value: T,
      onChange: (value: T) => void,
    ) {
      const options = Array.isArray(choices) ? [...choices] : choices;
      return getGui().add({ value }, 'value', options).name(label).onChange(onChange);
    },
    setStatus,
    destroy() {
      gui?.destroy();
      status?.remove();
    },
  };
}
```



Before calling `setData()`, query the selected node and edge IDs separately, then write matching selections to `states` in the incoming data. Edges need explicit stable IDs. The example restores only `selected` and uses `fitView: false` to keep the camera view.

## Clear element states [#clear-element-states]

### Clear all states [#clear-all-states]

Use `clearItemStates()` to clear one element. To clear several elements at once, supply an empty array for each.

```ts
graph.clearItemStates('A');
graph.setElementStates({ A: [], 'A-B': [], storage: [] });
```

### Clear a specific state [#clear-a-specific-state]

Pass `false` as the third argument to `setItemState()` to remove a single state. This example removes `review` and keeps A's selection.

```ts
graph.setItemState('A', 'review', false);
```

### Clear the same state from multiple elements [#clear-the-same-state-from-multiple-elements]

Find the highlighted edges, then use `batchSetState()` to clear their highlights.

```ts
graph.batchSetState(
  graph.findEdgesByState('highlight').map((id) => ({ id, state: 'highlight', value: false })),
);
```

## Query element states [#query-element-states]

### Read and check an element's states [#read-and-check-an-elements-states]

`getItemStates()` returns the states of a node, edge, or Combo as an array. The array is empty when the element has no states. Use `includes()` to check for a particular state.

```ts
const states = graph.getItemStates('A');
const isSelected = states.includes('selected');
```

### Find elements with a specific state [#find-elements-with-a-specific-state]

Query nodes, edges, or Combos by state. Each method returns matching element IDs.

```ts
const selectedNodeIds = graph.findNodesByState('selected');
const highlightedEdgeIds = graph.findEdgesByState('highlight');
const selectedComboIds = graph.findCombosByState('selected');
```

## Common questions [#common-questions]

### Why did adding a state not change appearance? [#why-did-adding-a-state-not-change-appearance]

Check that supported style fields are configured. The node whole-object style function currently skips stateStyles; use per-field configuration for state appearance. See [style functions](/en/docs/guides/node#options-node-style-callbacks).

### Why did setting selected emit no selection event? [#why-did-setting-selected-emit-no-selection-event]

Programmatic state changes do not synthesize node:selectchange; click-select emits it. Synchronize business UI explicitly after programmatic writes. See [selection synchronization](/en/docs/guides/events/selection-drag#synchronize-selection).

### Why is an element still hidden after clearing states? [#why-is-an-element-still-hidden-after-clearing-states]

Check whether it belongs to a collapsed Combo. Expand that structure, then check the business hidden flag.

### Why did clearing highlighting also remove selection? [#why-did-clearing-highlighting-also-remove-selection]

Check for clearItemStates or full replacement without selected. Remove only the state your code owns to preserve others.

### Why were some selected elements not restored? [#why-were-some-selected-elements-not-restored]

Check whether the new dataset still contains their IDs and whether edge IDs are stable. The example deliberately drops removed elements and preserves only selected.

### Do state updates need another render? [#do-state-updates-need-another-render]

No. State methods schedule drawing after initialization; update application UI through queries or your own synchronization logic.

Continue with [state and visibility methods](/en/docs/api/graph#graph-states), [node styles](/en/docs/guides/node#options-node-state-styles), [edge styles](/en/docs/guides/edge#options-edge-state-styles), and [interaction combinations](/en/docs/guides/behaviors).

**Related runnable examples**

* [Click, brush, and lasso selection](/en/docs/examples/selection-behaviors)


# Themes (/en/docs/guides/theme)





Use `theme` for default node, edge, and canvas colors. Choose light / dark, then override brand tokens; assign style functions to fields in `node.style` or `edge.style` for data-driven colors. All fields and defaults are in the [Theme reference](/en/docs/api/options#options-theme).

## Use a preset [#use-a-preset]

The complete code below renders the canvas above it. Choose light, dark, or brand to compare backgrounds, node sizes, and selection. Reset restores light. Switching calls updateOptions on the same graph instance.



```ts
import { Graph, resolveTheme, type ThemeOption } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import GUI from 'lil-gui';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  // #region theme-options
  const themes: Record<string, ThemeOption> = {
    light: 'light',
    dark: 'dark',
    brand: {
      type: 'light', nodeFill: '#00A876', nodeSize: 36,
      edgeStroke: '#00A876', edgeLineWidth: 2, canvasBackground: '#F1F8F5',
      nodeStateStyles: {
        ...resolveTheme('light').nodeStateStyles,
        selected: { stroke: '#005C41', strokeWidth: 3, haloWidth: 12 },
      },
    },
  };
  // #endregion theme-options
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    theme: themes.light,
    data: {
      nodes: [
        { id: 'Default', x: 0, y: 0 },
        { id: 'Selected', x: 160, y: 0, states: ['selected'] },
        { id: 'Disabled', x: 320, y: 0, states: ['disabled'] },
      ],
      edges: [{ source: 'Default', target: 'Selected' }, { source: 'Selected', target: 'Disabled' }],
    },
    node: { style: { label: (node) => node.id, labelColor: '#334155', labelOffsetY: 8 } },
    behaviors: [],
    autoFit: { padding: 56, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  const ui = createDemoPanel(container);
  const destroy = graph.destroy.bind(graph);
  graph.destroy = () => { ui.destroy(); destroy(); };
  try {
    await graph.render();
    ui.addChoice('Theme', Object.keys(themes), 'light', (value) => {
      graph.updateOptions({
        theme: themes[value],
        node: { style: { labelColor: value === 'dark' ? '#E2E8F0' : '#334155' } },
      });
      // Keep non-white theme backgrounds accurate inside the dotted docs canvas.
      graph.getCanvas().style.mixBlendMode = value === 'light' ? 'multiply' : 'normal';
    });
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}


export function createDemoPanel(container: string | HTMLElement, description = '') {
  const host = typeof container === 'string' ? document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(container)! : container;
  if (getComputedStyle(host).position === 'static') host.style.position = 'relative';

  let gui: GUI | undefined;
  const getGui = () => {
    if (!gui) {
      gui = new GUI({ container: host, width: 160 });
      gui.domElement.classList.add('g6lite-demo-controls');
      gui.domElement.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      Object.assign(gui.domElement.style, {
        position: 'absolute',
        top: '10px',
        right: '10px',
        zIndex: '30',
        maxWidth: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
        maxHeight: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
      });
    }
    return gui;
  };

  let status: HTMLDivElement | undefined;
  const setStatus = (message: string) => {
    if (!status) {
      status = document.createElement('div');
      status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
      status.dataset.role = 'status';
      status.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      status.style.cssText =
        'position:absolute;left:12px;bottom:10px;z-index:20;max-width:min(28rem,calc(100% - 24px));color:#64748b;font:12px/1.45 system-ui,sans-serif;pointer-events:none;white-space:pre-wrap;';
      host.append(status);
    }
    status.textContent = message;
  };
  if (description) setStatus(description);

  return {
    get gui() {
      return getGui();
    },
    addAction(label: string, action: () => void, folder = getGui()) {
      return folder.add({ [label]: action }, label);
    },
    addChoice<T extends string>(
      label: string,
      choices: readonly T[] | Record<string, T>,
      value: T,
      onChange: (value: T) => void,
    ) {
      const options = Array.isArray(choices) ? [...choices] : choices;
      return getGui().add({ value }, 'value', options).name(label).onChange(onChange);
    },
    setStatus,
    destroy() {
      gui?.destroy();
      status?.remove();
    },
  };
}
```



## Override tokens [#override-tokens]

Map application brand colors to a ThemeOption and pass it as new Graph's theme. Include only tokens you need to change:

```ts
import type { ThemeOption } from '@antv/g6-lite';

const brandTheme: ThemeOption = {
  type: 'light',
  nodeFill: '#00A876',
  nodeSize: 36,
  edgeStroke: '#00A876',
  edgeLineWidth: 2,
  canvasBackground: '#F1F8F5',
};
```

State maps are replaced in full. To retain preset states such as disabled, construct a new map using the [spread pattern](/en/docs/api/options#precedence).

## Precedence [#precedence]

Both nodes' explicit green fill overrides the theme's blue. Selected uses the orange outline from node.stateStyles.selected. That entire state object is chosen, without filling in the theme's purple selected fill, so the node stays green.



```ts
import { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: [
        { id: 'Base style', x: 0, y: 0 },
        { id: 'Selected', x: 180, y: 0, states: ['selected'] },
      ],
      edges: [{ source: 'Base style', target: 'Selected' }],
    },
    theme: {
      type: 'light', nodeFill: '#1783FF',
      nodeStateStyles: { selected: { fill: '#873BF4', stroke: '#873BF4' } },
    },
    node: {
      style: { fill: '#00A876', size: 36, label: (node) => node.id, labelOffsetY: 8 },
      stateStyles: { selected: { stroke: '#F08F56', strokeWidth: 3 } },
    },
    behaviors: [],
    autoFit: { padding: 56, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  try {
    await graph.render();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}
```



## Switch themes [#switch-themes]

Update the theme and label colors together on an existing graph instance:

```ts
graph.updateOptions({
  theme: 'dark',
  node: { style: { labelColor: '#E2E8F0' } },
  edge: { style: { labelColor: '#E2E8F0' } },
});
```

Each theme replaces the previous theme option. To retain brand tokens, pass `{ ...brandTheme, type: 'dark', canvasBackground: '#1a1a1a' }`; those explicit brand tokens will also continue to override the dark preset.

Switching refreshes styles while preserving graph data, states, and the camera. It does not rerun layout or fit the graph. Synchronize system dark mode, page CSS, and Combo styles in the application; check contrast for label backgrounds, icons, and decorations too.

## Default visual semantics [#default-visual-semantics]

Omitting theme selects light, with default node size 24. Labels require configured text, and their colors do not automatically follow the theme. See the [Theme reference](/en/docs/api/options#state-presets) for defaults and state styles, or compare all built-in states in [Default themes and interaction states](/en/docs/examples/default-theme).

## Common questions [#common-questions]

### Why did changing nodeFill leave the nodes unchanged? [#why-did-changing-nodefill-leave-the-nodes-unchanged]

Check node.style.fill and custom extension defaults first: they take precedence over theme defaults. For selected or other states, also check that state's fill.

### Why is text hard to read after switching to dark? [#why-is-text-hard-to-read-after-switching-to-dark]

Themes have no label-color token. Update node/edge.style.labelColor too; custom labels and backgrounds also need colors suitable for the dark canvas.

### Why did disabled lose its dimming when I changed only selected? [#why-did-disabled-lose-its-dimming-when-i-changed-only-selected]

Passing nodeStateStyles replaces the entire preset map. Spread the original map before changing selected. Do not mutate shared state objects in the resolveTheme result.

## Related [#related]

* [Theme reference](/en/docs/api/options#options-theme): tokens, presets, precedence, and resolveTheme.
* [Nodes](/en/docs/guides/node) · [Edges](/en/docs/guides/edge): data-driven appearance.
* [Labels and icons](/en/docs/guides/label) · [Combos](/en/docs/guides/combo): coordinate other visual elements.

**Related runnable examples**

* [Default themes and interaction states](/en/docs/examples/default-theme)


# Transforms (/en/docs/guides/transform-overview)





## What is a transform? [#what-is-a-transform]

A transform prepares a full set of graph data. Use it to share logic that generates node labels or filters the nodes and edges to draw.

## When transforms run [#when-transforms-run]

G6Lite runs custom transforms when `render()` or `setData()` processes a full input. It calls each `beforeRender(data)` in `transforms` order, then uses the result for layout and drawing.

Calling `layout()` or `updateNodeData()` alone uses the current graph data. To keep a label in sync with a node field, read that field directly in the `node.style.label` style function.

## Built-in transforms [#built-in-transforms]

| Type                     | Description                                                                 | Configuration example                                                             |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `process-parallel-edges` | Separates overlapping `line` or `arc` edges between the same pair of nodes. | [Parallel edge options and examples](/en/docs/guides/edge#entries-and-precedence) |

Parallel edge offsets are computed after the graph data is applied. When separation is enabled, adding or removing an edge also rearranges the edges in its group.

## Configuration [#configuration]

### Basic configuration [#basic-configuration]

Set `transforms` when you create the graph. Use the built-in transform name directly, or register a custom transform before using it.

```ts
const graph = new Graph({
  container,
  data,
  transforms: ['process-parallel-edges'],
});

await graph.render();
```

### Configure transform options [#configure-transform-options]

Use an object to pass parameters. Set `type` to the transform name and put the parameters in `options`. Here, `offset` controls parallel edge spacing.

```ts
const graph = new Graph({
  container,
  data,
  transforms: [{ type: 'process-parallel-edges', options: { offset: 48 } }],
});

await graph.render();
```

### Replace or remove transforms [#replace-or-remove-transforms]

To replace a custom transform or change its parameters, destroy the old graph and create a graph with the new `transforms`. To remove a transform, omit it from the new configuration. You can also use `updateOptions()` to change parallel edge spacing or toggle separation at runtime. [Parallel edge options](/en/docs/guides/edge#grouping-and-spacing)

## Custom transforms [#custom-transforms]

This example implements `docs-normalize`, a transform that prefixes node names to generate labels such as `Svc: API`.

### Implement and register [#implement-and-activate]

Implement `beforeRender(data)` in a factory. Read the nodes from the supplied `GraphData` and return the complete transformed data synchronously. The example adds `data.label` to each node and preserves the edges, Combos, and other fields.

Register the factory with `register('transform', 'docs-normalize', createNormalize)`, then configure the graph.

```ts
transforms: [
  { type: 'docs-normalize', options: { prefix: 'Svc' } },
],
node: {
  style: { label: (node) => String(node.data?.label ?? node.id) },
},
```

### Code example [#code-example]

**Update name** only changes the node name. The generated label and the `run` count stay the same. **Reload data** calls `setData()`, updates the label from the new input, and increments `run`.



```ts
export function createNormalize(): TransformExtension<NormalizeOptions> {
  let prefix = 'Svc';
  let report: NormalizeOptions['onPhase'];
  const configure = (options: Readonly<Partial<NormalizeOptions>>) => {
    prefix = options.prefix ?? 'Svc';
    report = options.onPhase;
  };
  return {
    init(_context, options) { configure(options); report?.('init'); },
    update(options) { configure(options); report?.('update'); },
    beforeRender(data) {
      report?.('run');
      return { ...data, nodes: data.nodes.map((node) => ({
        ...node, data: { ...node.data, label: prefix + ': ' + String(node.data?.name ?? node.id) },
      })) };
    },
    destroy() { report?.('destroy'); report = undefined; },
  };
}
register('transform', 'docs-normalize', () => createNormalize());
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph, register, type GraphData, type TransformExtension } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import GUI from 'lil-gui';

type Phase = 'init' | 'update' | 'run' | 'destroy';
interface NormalizeOptions { prefix?: string; onPhase?: (phase: Phase) => void }
// #region transform
export function createNormalize(): TransformExtension<NormalizeOptions> {
  let prefix = 'Svc';
  let report: NormalizeOptions['onPhase'];
  const configure = (options: Readonly<Partial<NormalizeOptions>>) => {
    prefix = options.prefix ?? 'Svc';
    report = options.onPhase;
  };
  return {
    init(_context, options) { configure(options); report?.('init'); },
    update(options) { configure(options); report?.('update'); },
    beforeRender(data) {
      report?.('run');
      return { ...data, nodes: data.nodes.map((node) => ({
        ...node, data: { ...node.data, label: prefix + ': ' + String(node.data?.name ?? node.id) },
      })) };
    },
    destroy() { report?.('destroy'); report = undefined; },
  };
}
register('transform', 'docs-normalize', () => createNormalize());
// #endregion transform

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const counters: Record<Phase, number> = { init: 0, update: 0, run: 0, destroy: 0 };
  const status = document.createElement('div');
  status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
  status.style.cssText = 'position:absolute;bottom:12px;left:12px;font:12px system-ui;color:#334155;background:white;padding:4px;';
  const updateStatus = () => {
    status.textContent = 'init=' + counters.init + ' update=' + counters.update + ' run=' + counters.run;
  };
  let revision = 0;
  const input = (): GraphData => ({
    nodes: [
      { id: 'A', x: 0, y: 0, data: { name: revision % 2 ? 'New API' : 'API' } },
      { id: 'B', x: 240, y: 0, data: { name: 'DB' } },
    ],
    edges: [{ id: 'A-B', source: 'A', target: 'B' }],
  });
  const graph = new Graph({
    container, data: input(),
    // #region config-transforms
    transforms: [{ type: 'docs-normalize', options: { prefix: 'Svc', onPhase: (phase: Phase) => { counters[phase]++; updateStatus(); } } }],
    // #endregion config-transforms
    node: { style: { size: 32, label: (node) => String(node.data?.label ?? node.id) } },
    behaviors: ['zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas'],
    autoFit: { padding: 64, maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  const ui = createDemoPanel(container);
  const destroy = graph.destroy.bind(graph);
  graph.destroy = () => { ui.destroy(); status.remove(); destroy(); };
  try {
    await graph.render();
    updateStatus();
    ui.addAction('Reload data', () => {
      revision++;
      void graph.setData(input(), { fitView: false }).catch((error) => { status.textContent = String(error); });
    });
    ui.addAction('Update name', () => {
      graph.updateNodeData('A', { name: 'Raw name' });
      updateStatus();
    });
    container.append(status);
    return graph;
  }
  catch (error) { graph.destroy(); throw error; }
}


export function createDemoPanel(container: string | HTMLElement, description = '') {
  const host = typeof container === 'string' ? document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(container)! : container;
  if (getComputedStyle(host).position === 'static') host.style.position = 'relative';

  let gui: GUI | undefined;
  const getGui = () => {
    if (!gui) {
      gui = new GUI({ container: host, width: 160 });
      gui.domElement.classList.add('g6lite-demo-controls');
      gui.domElement.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      Object.assign(gui.domElement.style, {
        position: 'absolute',
        top: '10px',
        right: '10px',
        zIndex: '30',
        maxWidth: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
        maxHeight: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
      });
    }
    return gui;
  };

  let status: HTMLDivElement | undefined;
  const setStatus = (message: string) => {
    if (!status) {
      status = document.createElement('div');
      status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
      status.dataset.role = 'status';
      status.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      status.style.cssText =
        'position:absolute;left:12px;bottom:10px;z-index:20;max-width:min(28rem,calc(100% - 24px));color:#64748b;font:12px/1.45 system-ui,sans-serif;pointer-events:none;white-space:pre-wrap;';
      host.append(status);
    }
    status.textContent = message;
  };
  if (description) setStatus(description);

  return {
    get gui() {
      return getGui();
    },
    addAction(label: string, action: () => void, folder = getGui()) {
      return folder.add({ [label]: action }, label);
    },
    addChoice<T extends string>(
      label: string,
      choices: readonly T[] | Record<string, T>,
      value: T,
      onChange: (value: T) => void,
    ) {
      const options = Array.isArray(choices) ? [...choices] : choices;
      return getGui().add({ value }, 'value', options).name(label).onChange(onChange);
    },
    setStatus,
    destroy() {
      gui?.destroy();
      status?.remove();
    },
  };
}
```



### Options and cleanup [#options-and-cleanup]

| Method                   | What it does in the example                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `init(context, options)` | Reads `prefix` when the instance is created, defaulting to `Svc`.                                                                       |
| `update(options)`        | Reads the complete options when a later `render()` or `setData()` reuses the instance at the same position with the same name.          |
| `beforeRender(data)`     | Generates labels from the current input and returns the processed data.                                                                 |
| `destroy()`              | Releases the callback reference when the graph is destroyed. Release any timers or other resources owned by the transform here as well. |

Return new objects for records you change. If you filter out nodes, also handle their associated edges and Combo references so the result remains valid.

See [TransformOption](/en/docs/api/options#transforms) for configuration fields and [TransformExtension](/en/docs/api/extensions#transformextension) for the extension API.


# Viewport and coordinates (/en/docs/guides/viewport)





The viewport is the part of the graph you can currently see. Panning or zooming changes how you view it; connections and node graph coordinates stay unchanged.

## Graph positions and the current view [#graph-positions-and-the-current-view]

A node's x / y is its graph position, supplied by data or computed by layout. Camera x / y / zoom describes translation and scale. Dragging a node changes its position; dragging the canvas changes the camera.

Relayout and fitting are separate steps: layout computes positions, while fitView adjusts the camera to bring content into view.

## Choose when to fit [#choose-when-to-fit]

| Task                                           | Approach                                                      |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Show all content                               | fitView, with padding and zoom limits as needed               |
| Center without changing scale                  | fitCenter                                                     |
| Locate a node from a list                      | focusItem(id), shrinking when necessary to contain the target |
| Refresh data while keeping the view            | `setData(next, { fitView: false })`                           |
| Keep all content visible after a panel narrows | Configure autoFit at initialization                           |

The first await graph.render() performs an initial fit even with autoFit: false. Data replacement, relayout, and container resizing have separate policies. Do not call render again just to refresh the viewport.

Use the buttons below to compare centering and fitting. Zoom or pan first, then choose Center or Fit. Center retains zoom. Fit adjusts both translation and scale. Reset camera restores the first rendered camera.



```ts
const zoom = () => graph.zoomBy(1.5, { maxZoom: 4 });
const pan = () => {
  const camera = graph.getCamera();
  graph.setCamera({ x: camera.x + 80 });
};
const center = () => graph.fitCenter();
const fit = () => graph.fitView({ padding: [70, 50, 110, 50], maxZoom: 1 });
const reset = () => graph.resetCamera();
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph, type Camera } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import GUI from 'lil-gui';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: [{ id: 'A', x: 0, y: 0 }, { id: 'B', x: 240, y: 80 }],
      edges: [{ id: 'A-B', source: 'A', target: 'B' }],
    },
    node: { style: { size: 32, label: (node) => node.id === 'A' ? 'A (0, 0)' : 'B (240, 80)', labelOffsetY: 10 } },
    behaviors: ['zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas'],
    autoFit: { padding: [70, 50, 110, 50], maxZoom: 1 },
  });
  // #region camera
  const zoom = () => graph.zoomBy(1.5, { maxZoom: 4 });
  const pan = () => {
    const camera = graph.getCamera();
    graph.setCamera({ x: camera.x + 80 });
  };
  const center = () => graph.fitCenter();
  const fit = () => graph.fitView({ padding: [70, 50, 110, 50], maxZoom: 1 });
  const reset = () => graph.resetCamera();
  // #endregion camera
  let saved: Camera;
  // #region saved-view
  const save = () => { saved = graph.getCamera(); };
  const restore = () => graph.setCamera(saved);
  const focus = () => graph.focusItem('B', 32);
  // #endregion saved-view
  const ui = createDemoPanel(container);
  const status = document.createElement('div');
  status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
  status.style.cssText = 'position:absolute;left:12px;bottom:12px;right:12px;padding:8px;background:white;color:#334155;font:12px/1.5 system-ui;white-space:pre-line;pointer-events:none;z-index:20;';
  const point = ({ x, y }: { x: number; y: number }) => `${Math.round(x * 10) / 10}, ${Math.round(y * 10) / 10}`;
  let frame = 0;
  let disposed = false;
  const update = () => {
    const camera = graph.getCamera();
    // #region coordinates
    const rect = container.getBoundingClientRect();
    const client = graph.graphToScreen(0, 0);
    const canvas = { x: client.x - rect.left, y: client.y - rect.top };
    const back = graph.screenToGraph(client.x, client.y);
    // #endregion coordinates
    status.textContent = [
      `A graph (0, 0) | camera (${point(camera)}) | zoom ${camera.zoom.toFixed(2)}`,
      `A canvas (${point(canvas)}) | A client (${point(client)})`,
      `screenToGraph(A client) = (${point(back)})`,
    ].join('\n');
  };
  const schedule = () => {
    if (disposed || frame) return;
    frame = requestAnimationFrame(() => { frame = 0; if (!disposed) update(); });
  };
  const actions: Array<[string, () => void]> = [
    ['Zoom ×1.5', zoom], ['Pan right', pan], ['Center', center], ['Fit', fit], ['Reset camera', reset],
    ['Save view', save], ['Restore view', restore], ['Focus B', focus],
  ];
  const events = ['node:pointermove', 'edge:pointermove', 'canvas:pointermove', 'canvas:pointerup', 'resize'] as const;
  const destroy = graph.destroy.bind(graph);
  graph.destroy = () => {
    disposed = true;
    cancelAnimationFrame(frame);
    for (const event of events) graph.off(event, schedule);
    window.removeEventListener('click', schedule);
    window.removeEventListener('wheel', schedule);
    window.removeEventListener('scroll', schedule, true);
    ui.destroy();
    status.remove();
    destroy();
  };
  try {
    await graph.render();
    if (graph.destroyed) return graph;
    save();
    for (const event of events) graph.on(event, schedule);
    // Refresh after interaction and page scrolling, including the shared toolbar.
    window.addEventListener('click', schedule);
    window.addEventListener('wheel', schedule, { passive: true });
    window.addEventListener('scroll', schedule, { passive: true, capture: true });
    for (const [label, action] of actions) {
      ui.addAction(label, () => { action(); schedule(); });
    }
    container.append(status);
    update();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}


export function createDemoPanel(container: string | HTMLElement, description = '') {
  const host = typeof container === 'string' ? document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(container)! : container;
  if (getComputedStyle(host).position === 'static') host.style.position = 'relative';

  let gui: GUI | undefined;
  const getGui = () => {
    if (!gui) {
      gui = new GUI({ container: host, width: 160 });
      gui.domElement.classList.add('g6lite-demo-controls');
      gui.domElement.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      Object.assign(gui.domElement.style, {
        position: 'absolute',
        top: '10px',
        right: '10px',
        zIndex: '30',
        maxWidth: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
        maxHeight: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
      });
    }
    return gui;
  };

  let status: HTMLDivElement | undefined;
  const setStatus = (message: string) => {
    if (!status) {
      status = document.createElement('div');
      status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
      status.dataset.role = 'status';
      status.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      status.style.cssText =
        'position:absolute;left:12px;bottom:10px;z-index:20;max-width:min(28rem,calc(100% - 24px));color:#64748b;font:12px/1.45 system-ui,sans-serif;pointer-events:none;white-space:pre-wrap;';
      host.append(status);
    }
    status.textContent = message;
  };
  if (description) setStatus(description);

  return {
    get gui() {
      return getGui();
    },
    addAction(label: string, action: () => void, folder = getGui()) {
      return folder.add({ [label]: action }, label);
    },
    addChoice<T extends string>(
      label: string,
      choices: readonly T[] | Record<string, T>,
      value: T,
      onChange: (value: T) => void,
    ) {
      const options = Array.isArray(choices) ? [...choices] : choices;
      return getGui().add({ value }, 'value', options).name(label).onChange(onChange);
    },
    setStatus,
    destroy() {
      gui?.destroy();
      status?.remove();
    },
  };
}
```



[fitView parameters](/en/docs/api/graph#graph-viewport-fitview) · [fitCenter parameters](/en/docs/api/graph#fitcenter)

### Why is the graph still small after fitting? [#why-is-the-graph-still-small-after-fitting]

Check for distant nodes, far-reaching edges or Combos, then inspect padding and maxZoom. The example caps maxZoom at 1 to avoid over-enlarging a small graph. fitCenter only centers; use zoomTo or zoomBy to zoom in explicitly.

## Refresh data with or without fitting [#refresh-data-with-or-without-fitting]

Zoom with the toolbar or drag empty canvas, then choose Reload + keep view. B moves from x=240 to x=800 while the camera stays unchanged; B may leave the viewport. Use Reset example, then Reload + fit to compare: the updated content fits into view.



```ts
await graph.setData(data(next), {
  fitView: keepView ? false : fit,
});
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph, type FitViewOptions, type GraphData } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import GUI from 'lil-gui';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const fit: FitViewOptions = { padding: [76, 48, 100, 48], maxZoom: 1 };
  const data = (wide: boolean): GraphData => ({
    nodes: [{ id: 'A', x: 0, y: 0 }, { id: 'B', x: wide ? 800 : 240, y: 0 }],
    edges: [{ id: 'A-B', source: 'A', target: 'B' }],
  });
  const graph = new Graph({
    container, data: data(false), autoFit: false,
    node: { style: { size: 32, label: (node) => node.id, labelOffsetY: 10 } },
    behaviors: ['zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas'],
  });
  let wide = false;
  let disposed = false;
  let frame = 0;
  let lastAction = 'Initial view';
  const reload = async (keepView: boolean) => {
    const before = graph.getCamera();
    const next = !wide;
    // #region preserve-view
    await graph.setData(data(next), {
      fitView: keepView ? false : fit,
    });
    // #endregion preserve-view
    if (graph.destroyed) return;
    wide = next;
    const after = graph.getCamera();
    const unchanged = before.x === after.x && before.y === after.y && before.zoom === after.zoom;
    lastAction = `Last reload (${keepView ? 'keep view' : 'refit'}): camera ${unchanged ? 'unchanged' : 'changed'}`;
  };
  const ui = createDemoPanel(container);
  const status = document.createElement('div');
  status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
  status.style.cssText = 'position:absolute;left:12px;bottom:12px;right:12px;padding:8px;background:white;color:#334155;font:12px/1.5 system-ui;white-space:pre-line;pointer-events:none;z-index:20;';
  const update = () => {
    const camera = graph.getCamera();
    status.textContent = `A (0, 0), B (${wide ? 800 : 240}, 0) | ${lastAction}\ncamera (${camera.x.toFixed(1)}, ${camera.y.toFixed(1)}) | zoom ${camera.zoom.toFixed(2)}`;
  };
  const schedule = () => {
    if (disposed || frame) return;
    frame = requestAnimationFrame(() => { frame = 0; if (!disposed) update(); });
  };
  const actions: Array<[string, () => void | Promise<void>]> = [
    ['Reload + keep view', () => reload(true)],
    ['Reload + fit', () => reload(false)],
    ['Focus A', () => { graph.focusItem('A'); lastAction = 'Focused A'; }],
  ];
  const events = ['node:pointermove', 'edge:pointermove', 'canvas:pointermove', 'canvas:pointerup', 'resize'] as const;
  const destroy = graph.destroy.bind(graph);
  graph.destroy = () => {
    disposed = true;
    cancelAnimationFrame(frame);
    for (const event of events) graph.off(event, schedule);
    window.removeEventListener('click', schedule);
    window.removeEventListener('wheel', schedule);
    ui.destroy(); status.remove();
    destroy();
  };
  try {
    await graph.render();
    if (graph.destroyed) return graph;
    graph.fitView(fit);
    for (const event of events) graph.on(event, schedule);
    window.addEventListener('click', schedule);
    window.addEventListener('wheel', schedule, { passive: true });
    const buttons = actions.map(([label, action]) => ui.addAction(label, async () => {
        for (const item of buttons) item.disable();
        try {
          await action();
          if (!disposed) update();
        } catch {
          if (!disposed) { lastAction = 'Update failed'; update(); }
        } finally {
          if (!disposed) for (const item of buttons) item.enable();
        }
    }));
    container.append(status);
    update();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}


export function createDemoPanel(container: string | HTMLElement, description = '') {
  const host = typeof container === 'string' ? document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(container)! : container;
  if (getComputedStyle(host).position === 'static') host.style.position = 'relative';

  let gui: GUI | undefined;
  const getGui = () => {
    if (!gui) {
      gui = new GUI({ container: host, width: 160 });
      gui.domElement.classList.add('g6lite-demo-controls');
      gui.domElement.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      Object.assign(gui.domElement.style, {
        position: 'absolute',
        top: '10px',
        right: '10px',
        zIndex: '30',
        maxWidth: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
        maxHeight: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
      });
    }
    return gui;
  };

  let status: HTMLDivElement | undefined;
  const setStatus = (message: string) => {
    if (!status) {
      status = document.createElement('div');
      status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
      status.dataset.role = 'status';
      status.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      status.style.cssText =
        'position:absolute;left:12px;bottom:10px;z-index:20;max-width:min(28rem,calc(100% - 24px));color:#64748b;font:12px/1.45 system-ui,sans-serif;pointer-events:none;white-space:pre-wrap;';
      host.append(status);
    }
    status.textContent = message;
  };
  if (description) setStatus(description);

  return {
    get gui() {
      return getGui();
    },
    addAction(label: string, action: () => void, folder = getGui()) {
      return folder.add({ [label]: action }, label);
    },
    addChoice<T extends string>(
      label: string,
      choices: readonly T[] | Record<string, T>,
      value: T,
      onChange: (value: T) => void,
    ) {
      const options = Array.isArray(choices) ? [...choices] : choices;
      return getGui().add({ value }, 'value', options).name(label).onChange(onChange);
    },
    setStatus,
    destroy() {
      gui?.destroy();
      status?.remove();
    },
  };
}
```



Use fitView: false to keep the view; no camera save-and-restore is needed. New coordinates, layouts, and states still apply. Keeping the camera does not guarantee that a node stays at the same screen position. See [preserving selection](/en/docs/guides/states#preserve-selection-when-replacing-data) separately.

Omitting the second setData argument uses fitView(0.9); it does not inherit the initial autoFit padding. Pass a fit options object to this setData call, as in the example, to reuse your padding.

**Asynchronous refresh and saved views**

The example disables buttons during an update. For concurrent application requests, use a request sequence or cancellation to apply only the latest result. Check graph.destroyed after asynchronous work.

To restore a view across pages, save the getCamera() snapshot and call setCamera(saved) after the new instance's await render(). The camera records translation and zoom only; a different container size or different graph positions may show a different area. Calling fitView immediately afterward overwrites the restored camera.

## Handle resizing and completed layouts [#handle-resizing-and-completed-layouts]

Configure autoFit at initialization to keep all content visible after panel resizing. Keep false (the default) to retain the user's zoom and pan during exploration. Graph uses ResizeObserver to synchronize container dimensions; neither policy requires recreating the instance.

Zoom first, then switch Width 65% / 100% below. Only container CSS width changes. Inspect the final zoom and camera after resize; the complete source includes the listener and cleanup.



```ts
autoFit: { padding: [84, 40, 100, 40], maxZoom: 1 },
```

**Complete runnable code**

```ts
import { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import GUI from 'lil-gui';

export async function run(container: HTMLElement) {
  const originalWidth = container.style.width;
  const originalOutline = container.style.outline;
  const graph = new Graph({
    container,
    data: {
      nodes: [{ id: 'A', x: 0, y: 0 }, { id: 'B', x: 800, y: 0 }],
      edges: [{ id: 'A-B', source: 'A', target: 'B' }],
    },
    node: { style: { size: 32, label: (node) => node.id, labelOffsetY: 10 } },
    behaviors: ['zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas'],
    // #region auto-fit
    autoFit: { padding: [84, 40, 100, 40], maxZoom: 1 },
    // #endregion auto-fit
  });
  // ResizeObserver detects these CSS width changes; no setSize or render call.
  const narrow = () => { container.style.width = '65%'; };
  const wide = () => { container.style.width = '100%'; };
  const ui = createDemoPanel(container);
  const status = document.createElement('div');
  status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
  status.style.cssText = 'position:absolute;left:12px;bottom:12px;right:12px;padding:8px;background:white;color:#334155;font:12px/1.5 system-ui;white-space:pre-line;pointer-events:none;z-index:20;';
  let resizeCount = 0;
  let frame = 0;
  let disposed = false;
  const update = () => {
    const camera = graph.getCamera();
    status.textContent = `container ${Math.round(container.getBoundingClientRect().width)} CSS px | resize events: ${resizeCount}\nzoom ${graph.getZoom().toFixed(2)} | camera (${camera.x.toFixed(1)}, ${camera.y.toFixed(1)})`;
  };
  const schedule = () => {
    if (disposed || frame) return;
    frame = requestAnimationFrame(() => { frame = 0; if (!disposed) update(); });
  };
  const resized = () => { resizeCount++; update(); };
  const actions: Array<[string, () => void]> = [
    ['Width 65%', narrow], ['Width 100%', wide],
    ['Zoom ×1.5', () => graph.zoomBy(1.5)],
  ];
  const events = ['node:pointermove', 'edge:pointermove', 'canvas:pointermove', 'canvas:pointerup'] as const;
  const destroy = graph.destroy.bind(graph);
  graph.destroy = () => {
    disposed = true;
    cancelAnimationFrame(frame);
    graph.off('resize', resized);
    for (const event of events) graph.off(event, schedule);
    window.removeEventListener('click', schedule);
    window.removeEventListener('wheel', schedule);
    ui.destroy(); status.remove();
    destroy();
    container.style.width = originalWidth;
    container.style.outline = originalOutline;
  };
  try {
    await graph.render();
    if (graph.destroyed) return graph;
    graph.on('resize', resized);
    for (const event of events) graph.on(event, schedule);
    window.addEventListener('click', schedule);
    window.addEventListener('wheel', schedule, { passive: true });
    container.style.outline = '1px dashed #cbd5e1';
    for (const [label, action] of actions) {
      ui.addAction(label, () => { action(); schedule(); });
    }
    container.append(status);
    update();
    return graph;
  } catch (error) {
    graph.destroy();
    throw error;
  }
}


export function createDemoPanel(container: string | HTMLElement, description = '') {
  const host = typeof container === 'string' ? document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(container)! : container;
  if (getComputedStyle(host).position === 'static') host.style.position = 'relative';

  let gui: GUI | undefined;
  const getGui = () => {
    if (!gui) {
      gui = new GUI({ container: host, width: 160 });
      gui.domElement.classList.add('g6lite-demo-controls');
      gui.domElement.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      Object.assign(gui.domElement.style, {
        position: 'absolute',
        top: '10px',
        right: '10px',
        zIndex: '30',
        maxWidth: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
        maxHeight: 'calc(100% - 20px)',
      });
    }
    return gui;
  };

  let status: HTMLDivElement | undefined;
  const setStatus = (message: string) => {
    if (!status) {
      status = document.createElement('div');
      status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
      status.dataset.role = 'status';
      status.dataset.captureIgnore = '';
      status.style.cssText =
        'position:absolute;left:12px;bottom:10px;z-index:20;max-width:min(28rem,calc(100% - 24px));color:#64748b;font:12px/1.45 system-ui,sans-serif;pointer-events:none;white-space:pre-wrap;';
      host.append(status);
    }
    status.textContent = message;
  };
  if (description) setStatus(description);

  return {
    get gui() {
      return getGui();
    },
    addAction(label: string, action: () => void, folder = getGui()) {
      return folder.add({ [label]: action }, label);
    },
    addChoice<T extends string>(
      label: string,
      choices: readonly T[] | Record<string, T>,
      value: T,
      onChange: (value: T) => void,
    ) {
      const options = Array.isArray(choices) ? [...choices] : choices;
      return getGui().add({ value }, 'value', options).name(label).onChange(onChange);
    },
    setStatus,
    destroy() {
      gui?.destroy();
      status?.remove();
    },
  };
}
```



The container needs nonzero width and height. To reset the view when revealing a hidden tab, explicitly fitView after the container reaches its final size. The resize event follows any automatic fitting.

After await graph.layout(), either call `graph.fitView({ padding: 32, maxZoom: 1 })` or retain the current camera. Layout computes node positions; fitting is explicit. See [layout methods](/en/docs/api/graph#graph-layout) for asynchronous cancellation.

## Convert coordinates to position DOM content [#convert-coordinates-to-position-dom-content]

Use screenToGraph and graphToScreen to convert between graph and client coordinates. Watch A in the canvas above to compare the three coordinate spaces. Zooming or panning changes the canvas position. Scrolling the page changes the client position.

| Coordinates | Origin                                | Common use                                               |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| graph       | The graph's own coordinate system     | Store node positions, run layouts, create graph elements |
| canvas      | Canvas top-left, CSS pixels           | Position auxiliary content inside the canvas container   |
| client      | Browser viewport top-left, CSS pixels | Match mouse clientX / clientY, place fixed menus         |

Convert DOM mouse events using clientX / clientY. Element events already supply event.graph, event.canvas, and event.client. Fixed menus use client coordinates. Absolutely positioned content inside a canvas container without borders or padding uses CSS coordinates relative to that container.

```ts
import type { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';

export function pointAtMouse(graph: Graph, event: MouseEvent) {
  return graph.screenToGraph(event.clientX, event.clientY);
}

// marker is mounted on document.body; point is in graph coordinates
export function placeMarker(graph: Graph, marker: HTMLElement, point: { x: number; y: number }) {
  const client = graph.graphToScreen(point.x, point.y);
  Object.assign(marker.style, {
    position: 'fixed', left: `${client.x}px`, top: `${client.y}px`,
  });
}
```

Reproject the anchor after zooming, panning, or page scrolling; close menus that should not follow. Do not multiply by DPR. screenToGraph does not take offsetX / offsetY or screenX / screenY.

## Common questions [#common-questions]

### Should I save new node positions after panning or zooming? [#should-i-save-new-node-positions-after-panning-or-zooming]

These operations did not move nodes. Read getCamera to save the user's view, or element positions to save the layout; handle them separately.

### Why does a menu drift as I zoom? [#why-does-a-menu-drift-as-i-zoom]

Check for graph coordinates used directly as CSS positions, or canvas positions treated as client. Choose coordinates according to where the menu is mounted.

### Why does centered content still not fit? [#why-does-centered-content-still-not-fit]

fitCenter changes position only. Use fitView to adjust zoom too, and check padding and zoom bounds.

### Why does refreshing move the view with autoFit disabled? [#why-does-refreshing-move-the-view-with-autofit-disabled]

Check that setData receives fitView: false and that application code does not call fitView afterward. Disabling autoFit prevents automatic fitting on container resize; data replacement has its own fitting policy.

### Why do method and wheel zoom limits differ? [#why-do-method-and-wheel-zoom-limits-differ]

minZoom and maxZoom on zoomTo / zoomBy constrain that call only. Wheel limits belong to the zoom-canvas Behavior, and fitView limits are separate again. Set each when consistent limits are required. See [wheel zoom options](/en/docs/api/options#navigation-and-dragging).

Continue with [viewport methods](/en/docs/api/graph#graph-viewport), [autoFit](/en/docs/api/options#autofit), [setData](/en/docs/api/graph#setdata), and [element event coordinates](/en/docs/api/graph/events#read-event-parameters).

**Related runnable examples**

* [Search and focus](/en/docs/examples/search-focus)
* [Viewport and coordinate conversion](/en/docs/examples/viewport-controls)
* [Zoom range and sensitivity](/en/docs/examples/zoom-options)
